sourceDefinition: , aor. yaA^otiY , (Msb,) and, in the dial. of Hudheyl, yaA^ot , without Y ; (S;) and A^atayotuhu , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) [aor. A=tiyhi ;] and in the imperative, some of the Arabs say, ti , suppressing the A , like as is done in xu*o and kulo and muro ; (IJ, M;) inf. n. A_itoyaAnN , (T, S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb.) and A_itoyaAnapN , (M, K,) which should not be used as an inf. n. of un., unless by a bad poetic licence, (Lth, T,) and A^atoYN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and A^utiYN and A_itiYN and maA^otaApN ; (M, K;) He [or it ] came; (Msb;) and I came to him, or it; (S, M, Mgh, * Msb, K;) or was, or became, present at it, namely, a place: (Mgh:) as also A^ataA , aor. yaA^otuw ; (Msb;) and A^atawotuhu , (T, S, M, K), aor. A=tuwhu : (S:) for which reason, we assign the generality of the words mentioned in art. Atw to the present art. also. (M.) [Accord. to the authorities here indicated for the signification of A^ataY , this verb and jaA='a are syn.: some attempt to distinguish them; but contradict one another in so doing: the slight distinctions that exist between them will be best seen by a comparison of the exs. in this art. with those in art. jyA^ :] accord. to Er-Rághib, the proper [or primary] signification of AlA_itoyaAnu is The coming with ease. (TA.) ― -b2- A^ataAhaA , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. A_itoyaAnN , (Msb,) [lit. He came to her, ] means (assumed tropical:) he lay with her; syn. jaAmaEahaA ; (Mgh, Msb;) namely, a woman, (Mgh,) or his wife. (Msb.) Hence an expression in the Kur xxvi. 165. (TA.) ― -b3- A^ataY Alqawoma [ He came to the people: and hence,] he asserted his relationship to the people, not being of them. (Msb.) [See A^atiY~u in art. Atw .] ― -b4- A^atay bihi [ He came with, or brought, him, and it; or] he made him (a man), and it (a thing, such, for instance, as property), to come. (Kull.) [See also 4: and see, in what follows, other significations of A^ataY trans. by means of bi . Hence, A^ataY biwaladK He begot a child, or children. And A^atato bihi She brought him forth; gave birth to him. ] Accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, the meaning of the words in the Kur [ii. 143] A^ayonamaA takuwnuwA yaA^oti bikumu All~`hu jamiyEFA is, Wherever ye be, God will bring you all back unto Himself. (M.) [You say also, A^ataY bibay~inapK He adduced a proof. ] See also 3. ― -b5- A^ataY AlA^amora [ He entered into, engaged in, or occupied himself with, the thing, or affair: and, as also A^ataY bihi ,] he did, executed, or performed, the thing, or affair; (M. K;) and in like manner, Al*~anoba , [and baAl*~anobi ,] the crime, sin, or offence. (M.) It is said in the Kur [ix. 54], walaA yaA^otuwna AlS~alaApa A_il~aA wahumo kusaAlaY , meaning And they do not enter into, or engage in, prayer, unless when they are heavy, or sluggish. (TA.) And you say, A^ataY AlfaAHi$aha , [and biAlfaAHi$api , (see Kur iv. 23 and lxv. 1,)] He entered into, engaged in, or occupied himself with, [or he did, or committed, ] that which was excessively foul or evil. (TA.) And A^ataY biAljay~idi mino qawolK A^awo fiEolK [ He said, gave utterance to, uttered, or expressed, or he brought to pass, did, or effected, what was good, or excellent; he said, or did, well, or excel-lently ]. (Msb in art. jwd .) And A^ataY bijaroYi baEoda jaroYK [ He (a horse) performed, or fetched, run after run ]. (S in art. tA^m , &c.) ― -b6- walaA yufoliHu Als~aAHiru Hayovu A^ataY [in the Kur xx. 72] means Hayovu kaAna [ And the enchanter shall not prosper where he is, or wherever he may be ]; (M, Bd, K;) and where he cometh: (Bd:) or Hayovu A^ataY bisiHorihi [ where he cometh with his enchantment; or where he performeth his enchantment ]: (Jel:) and it is said to mean that where the enchanter is, he must be slain: such is the doctrine of the lawyers. (M.) ― -b7- Z mentions that A^ataY occurs in the sense of SaAra [ He, or it, became; like as we sometimes say, he, or it, came, or came to be ]; like jaA='a in the saying, jaA='a AlbinaA='u muHokamFA . (Kull.) [So you say, AlbinaA='u muHokamFA The building became, or came to be, firm, strong, or compact. ] ― -b8- The saying, in the Kur [xvi. 1], A^ataY A^amoru A=ll~`hi falaA tasotaEojiluwhu means [ The threatened punishment ordained of God hath approached: therefore desire not ye to hasten it: ] its coming hath approached. (TA.) [And in like manner,] A^utiYa fulaAnN , like EuniYa , means Such a one was approached by the enemy come in sight of him. (K.) A^utiyta yaA fulaAnN [ Thou art approached &c., O such a one, ] is said when one is warned of an enemy that has come in sight of him. (Sgh, TA.) And A^ataY Ealayohimu AlEaduw~u means The enemy came to them, [or came down upon them, for, as MF observes, A^ataY when trans. by means of EalaY seems to imply the meaning of nazala ,] overcoming, or overpowering, them. (Bd in xviii. 40.) ― -b9- Hence, A^ataY Ealayohi [and A^ataAhu , as will be seen by what follows,] (assumed tropical:) He destroyed him, or it. (Bd ubi suprà.) And hence, from A_itoyaAnu AlEaduw~i , (Mgh,) A^ataY Ealayohi Ald~ahoru (tropical:) Time, or fortune, destroyed him. (M, Mgh, Msb, K.) Destruction is meant in the Kur [lix. 2], where it is said, fA^atAhumu All~`hu mino Hyovu lamo yaHotasibuwA (assumed tropical:) [ But God brought destruction upon them whence they did not reckon, or expect ]. (EsSemeen, TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xvi. 28], faA^ataY All~`hu bunoyaAnahumo mina AlqawaAEidi , i. e. (assumed tropical:) But God removed their building from the foundations, and demolished it upon them, so that He destroyed them. (TA.) A^ataY Ealayohi also signifies (assumed tropical:) He caused it to come to an end; made an end of it; consumed it; [ devoured it; ] exhausted it; came to, or reached, the end of it; namely, a thing; (Kull;) as, for instance, what was in a bowl; (K in art. jrdm ;) and what was in a vessel; (K in art. jrjb ;) like faraga minohu : (ISd cited in the TA in art. nk$ :) or i. q. mar~a bihi [which may be rendered he went away with it; but this, as an explanation of A^ataY Ealayohi , has another meaning, which see in what follows]. (Kull.) And one says, A^utiYa fulaAnN mino maA^omanihi (assumed tropical:) Destruction came to such a one from the quarter whence he felt secure. (TA.) And A^utiYa Ealay yadi fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) Property belonging to such a one perished. (T.) And yuw^otaY duwnahu (assumed tropical:) He is taken away, or carried off, and overcome. (TA.) A poet says, A^ataY duwna HulowiAlEayo$i Hat~aY A^amar~ahu nukuwbN Ealay A=vaArihin~a nukuwbu meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Misfortunes, in the footsteps of which were misfortunes, ] took away [ what was sweet, of life, and rendered it bitter ]. (TA.) One says also, mino h`hunaA A^utiyato , [so I find it written, but I think that the last word should be A^utiyta , agreeably with a preceding phrase from the T,] (assumed tropical:) Hence the trial, or affliction, came in upon thee. (Mgh.) And A^utiYa mino jihapi ka*aA , with the verb in the passive form, (assumed tropical:) He missed [ his object in respect of such a thing ] by laying hold upon it when it was not fit to be laid hold upon. (Msb.) And A^utiYa Alr~ajulu , [also] like EuniYa , (assumed tropical:) The man was deceived, or deluded, and his faculty of sense became altered to him, so that he imagined that to be true which was not true. (TA.) ― -b10- A^ataY Ealayohi is also syn. with mar~a bihi [meaning He, or it, (as, for instance, a period of time,) passed by him, or over him ]. (Msb.) You say, A^ata Ealayohi HawolN [ A year passed over him; or he became a year old ]. (S, K, Msb, in art. Hwl ; &c.) ― -b11- A^atati Aln~aAqahu , and maA A^aHosana A^atoYa yadaY h*ihi Aln~Aqapi : see art. Atw .

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M,) or AlmaA='a , (K,) or both, (TA,) inf. n. taA^otiyapN and taA^otiY~N , He smoothed, made easy, or prepared, ( sah~ala , S, K, or hay~aA^a , T,) the way, course, passage, or channel, of the water, (T, S, K,) in order that it might pass forth to a place; (S;) he directed a channel for it (M, TA) so that it ran to the places wherein it rested or remained. (TA.) And A^t~Y liA^aroDihi A^atiy~aA He made a rivulet, or a channel for water, to run to his land. (M.) ― -b2- A^t~Y All~`hu lifulaAnK A^amorahu , inf. n. taA^otiyapN , (T, M, * TA,) God prepared, disposed, arranged, or put into a good or right state, [and thus rendered feasible or practicable or easy, ] for such a one, his affair. (M, * TA.)

The saying, in the Kur [xxi. 48], waA_ino kaAna mivoqaAla bihaA ↓ Hab~apK mino xarodalK A^atayonaA , some read thus, (M, * TA,) meaning [ Though it be the weight of a grain of mustard, ] we will bring it [forward for requital]: others read bhA ↓ A=tayonaA , meaning we will give [a recompense] for it; in which case the verb is of the measure A^afoEala : or we will requite for it; in which case the verb is of the measure faAEala . (M, TA.) ― -b2- A=tayotuhu EalaY AlA^amori , (T, S, M, Msb,) inf. n. muw^aAtaApN , (T, S,) I agreed with him, or was of one mind or opinion with him, upon, or respecting, the thing, or affair; I complied with him respecting it; (T, S, M, Msb;) in a good manner: (T:) the vulgar say, waAtayotuhu : (S:) this is of the dial. of the people of El-Yemen, inf. n. muwaAtaApN ; and is the form commonly current: (Msb:) but it should not be used, except in the dial. of the people of El-Yemen. (T.) ― -b3- [Hence, app., A=taY as meaning He aided; a signification mentioned by Golius, on the authority of Z and Ibn-Maaroof.]

definition: It (an affair, T, Mgh, Msb, K, or a thing, S, M) was, or became, prepared, disposed, arranged, or put into a good or right state, for him;
sourceDefinition: It (an affair, T, Mgh, Msb, K, or a thing, S, M) was, or became, prepared, disposed, arranged, or put into a good or right state, for him; (T, * S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) and hence, it (a thing) was, or became, feasible or practicable, and easy, to him; (Mgh;) it (an affair) was, or became, facilitated, or easy, to him; (Msb;) the way thereof (i. e. of an affair) was, or became, facilitated, or easy, to him. (TA.) The following is an ex.: taA^at~aY lahu Ald~ahoru Hat~aY Anojabaro [ Fortune became well, or rightly, disposed for him, so that he became restored to wealth, or competence ]: (T:) or taA^at~aY lahu Alxayoru Alx [ good fortune, or prosperity, became prepared, &c., for him, &c.]. (So in the TA.) And hence the saying, h`*aA mim~aA yataA^at~aY liYa AlmaDogu This is of the things which it is feasible or practicable, and easy, to me to chew. (Mgh). ― -b2- He applied himself to it with gentleness, (As, S, K,) and so tA^t~Y lahaA , meaning liHaAjatihi , to his needful affair or business, (T,) and entered into it, engaged in it, occupied himself with it, did it, executed it, or performed it, by the way, or manner, proper, or suitable, to it. (As, T, S, K. [In the CK, for A^ataAhu mino wajohihi , we find AtAhu En wajohih .]) And tA^t~Y fiY A^amrihi He used gentleness, or acted gently, in his affair. (Msb.) ― -b3- tA^t~Y lahu bisahomK Hat~aY A^aSaAbahu He sought him leisurely or repeatedly [ with an arrow, app. taking aim in one direction and then in another, until he hit him ]. (Z, TA.) ― -b4- jaA='a fulaAnN yataA^at~aY is explained by Fr as meaning yataEar~aDu limaEoruwfika [ Such a one came, or has come, addressing, or applying, or directing, himself, or his regard, or attention, or mind, to obtain thy favour, or bounty ]. (S.) And you say, tA^t~Y limaEruwfihi , meaning taEar~aDa lahu [ He addressed, applied, or directed, himself, &c., to obtain his favour, or bounty ]. (TA.) ― -b5- Some say that tA^t~Y signifies He prepared himself to rise, or stand. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh,) inf. n. muw^aAsaApN , (S, M, K,) I made him my object of imitation ( A_isowatiY ), [meaning I made myself like him, ] in respect of my property: (S:) or I made him an object of imitation [ with, or in respect of, my property ], I imitating his example, and he imitating my example: (Mgh:) and waAsayotuhu is a dial. var., but of weak authority: (S, Mgh:) and A=saAniY [alone] he made me an object of imitation to him by giving me of his property [ and thus reducing himself to my condition in some degree while in the same degree raising me to his ]; (Ham p. 696;) and A^uwaAsiyhi [thus without a second ' ] I make him the object of my own imitation and so share with him my property: (Id p. 198:) or A=sAhu bimaAlihi signifies he gave him of his property, and made him an object of imitation in respect of it: or only, of food sufficient for his want; not of what is superabundant: (M, K:) whence the saying, raHima A@ll~`hu rajulFA A^aEoTaY mino faDolK wawaAsaY mino kafaAfK [ May God have mercy on a man who has given of superabundance, and imparted of food only sufficient for his want so as to make himself equal with him to whom he imparts of such food ]: (TA:) [and A=sAhu signifies he shared with him: and he was, or became, equal with him: for] AlmuwaAsaApu occurs often in trads., signifying the sharing with another, or making another to share with one, in the means of subsistence [ &c. ]; and is originally [ Almuw^aAsaApu ,] with ' : also, the being, or becoming, equal with another: (TA:) and you say, A=sayotuhu binafosiy , meaning I made him equal with myself; in the dial. of El-Yemen waAsayotuhu . (Msb.) A=si bayona Aln~aAsi fiY wajohika , in a letter of 'Omar, means Make thou the people to share [ alike ], one with another, in thy consideration and regard: or, as some say, make thou them equal [ in respect thereof ]. (Mgh.) (IDrd, TA.) [See also an ex. voce A^avarapN ].

sourceDefinition: , originally Amwp , (Msb,) [but whether A^amawapN or A^amowapN is disputed, as will be seen in what follows,] A female slave; (M, K;) a woman whose condition is that of slavery; (T;) contr. of Hur~apN : (S:) [in relation to God, best rendered a handmaid: ] dual A^amataAni : (Msb:) pl. A=mK , (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) like qiADK , (Msb,) a pl. of pauc. [respecting which see what follows after the other pls.], (Lth, T,) and A_imaA='N [the most common form] (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and A_imowaAnN (T, S, M, Msb, K) and A^umowaAnN (K, and so in some copies of the M) and A^amowaAnN (K, and so in some copies of the M) [the last, or last but one, accord. to different copies of the M, on the authority of Lh,] and A^amawaAtN , (M, Msb, K,) for which one may say A^amaAtN . (Ibn-Keysán, TA.) Accord. to Sb (M) and Mbr (TA) it is originally A^amawapN , (S, M, K,) because it has for a pl. A=mK , (S, M,) which is [originally A^aA^omuwN ,] of the measure A^afoEulN , (Lth, T, S,) like A=kumN , pl. of A^akamapN , (Sb, M,) and like A^ayonuqN , [pl. of naAqpN , which is originally nawaqpN ,] for a sing. of the measure faEolapN has not a pl. of this form; (S;) and Mbr says that there is no noun of two letters but a letter has been dropped from it, which it indicates by its pl. or dual, or by a verb if it is derived therefrom: (TA:) or it is originally faEolapN : (AHeyth, T, K:) AHeyth says that they suppressed its final radical letter, and, forming a pl. from it after the manner of naxolapN and naxolN , instead of saying A^amN , which they disliked as being of only two letters, they transposed the suppressed w , changing it into A , and placing it between the A and m . (T: [in which this opinion, though it does not account for the termination of the pl. A=mK , is said to be preferable.]) One says, jaA='a toniYF A^amapu All~`hi [ The handmaid of God came to me ]: and in the dual, jaA='a toniY A^mataA All~`hi : and in the pl., jaA='a niY A_imaA='u All~`hi and A_imowaAnu All~`hi and A^amawaAtu All~`hi ; and one may also say, A^amaAtu All~`h . (Ibn-Keysán, TA.) [ISd says,] wamaAhu All~`hu mino kul~i A^amapK bHajarK is mentioned by IAar as said in imprecating evil on a man; but I think it is mn kl~ A^amoti [ May God cast a stone at him from every elevated place, or the like]. (M.)

definition: a conjunction, (M, Mughnee, K,) to which the later authors have ascribed meanings amounting to twelve: (Mughnee:) a particle which, when occurring in an enunciative phrase, [generally] denotes doubt, and vagueness of meaning;
sourceDefinition: a conjunction, (M, Mughnee, K,) to which the later authors have ascribed meanings amounting to twelve: (Mughnee:) a particle which, when occurring in an enunciative phrase, [generally] denotes doubt, and vagueness of meaning; and when occurring in an imperative or a prohibitive phrase, [generally] denotes the giving of option, or choice, and the allowing a thing, or making it allowable. (S.) ― -b2- First, (Mughnee,) it denotes doubt. (T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, raA^ayotu zayodFA A^awo EamorFA [ I saw Zeyd or 'Amr ]. (T, * S, Msb.) And jaA=niY rajulN A^awi A@moraA^apN [ A man or a woman came to me ]. (Mbr, T.) And labiy^onaA yawomFA A^awo baEoDa yawomK [in the Kur xviii. 18 and xxiii. 115, We have remained a day or part of a day ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- Secondly, (Mughnee,) it denotes vagueness of meaning. (S, Msb, Mughnee, K.) S [it may be used] in the first of the .exs. given above. (Msb.) And so in the saying, waA^an~aA A^awo A_iy~aAkumo laEalaY hudFy A^awo fiY DalaAlK mubiynK [ And verily we or ye are following a right direction or in manifest error ], (S, Mughnee,) in the Kur [xxxiv. 23]; (S;) the ex. being in the former Aw . (Mughnee.) ― -b4- Thirdly, (Mughnee,) it denotes the giving of option, or choice. (T, S, M, Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, kuli Als~amaka A^awi A@$orabi All~abana [ Eat thou the fish, or drink thou the milk ]; i. e. do not thou both of these actions; (Mbr, T, S;) but choose which of them thou wilt. (Mbr, T.) And tazaw~ajo hinodFA A^awo A^uxotahaA [ Take thou as wife Hind or her sister ]. (Mughnee.) And [in like manner] it denotes the making choice. (T.) [So when you say, saA^atazaw~aju hinodFA A^awo A^uxotahaA , meaning I will take as wife Hind or her sister; whichever of them I choose.] ― -b5- Fourthly, (Mughnee,) it denotes the allowing a thing, or making it allowable. (T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, jaAlisi Hasana A^awi A@bona siyriyna [ Sit thou with El- Hasan or Ibn-Seereen ]. (Mbr, T, S.) And qumo A^awi A@qoEudo [ Stand thou or sit ]: and the person to whom this is said may do [one or] both of the se actions. (Msb.) [And similar exs. are given in the Mughnee.]) But walaA tuTiEo minohumo A=vimFA A^aw kafuwrFA [in the Kur lxxvi. 24, And obey not thou, of them, a sinner or a person very ungrateful to God, ] means that thou shalt not obey either of such persons: (Mbr, T, Mughnee:) in which case Aw is more forcible than wa ; for when you say to a person, laA tuTiEo zayodFA waEamorFA [ Obey not thou Zeyd and 'Amr ], he may obey one of them, since the command is that he shall not obey the two. (Zj, T.) ― -b6- Fifthly, (Mughnee,) it denotes unrestricted conjunction. (Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, in the Kur [iv. 46 and v. 9], A^awo jaA='a A^aHadN minokumo mina AlgaAy^iTi [ And if any one of you cometh from the privy ]; (TA;) [where, however, it may also be rendered or, though] meaning wajaA='a ; (T, TA;) the w in this explanation being what is termed a denotative of state. (T.) So, too, accord. to AZ, in the expression A^awo yaziyduwna [ And they exceeded that number], in the Kur [xxxvii. 147]: but see below. (TA.) And so in the words, A^awo A^ano nafoEala fiY A^amowaAlinaA maA na$aA='u [ And our doing, in respect of our possessions, what we will ], in the Kur [xi. 89]. (T, TA.) ― -b7- Sixthly, it denotes transition, (Mughnee,) used in the sense of [the adversative particle] balo , (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) in a case of amplification of speech; (S;) accord. to Sb, on two conditions; that it shall be preceded by a negation or a prohibition, and that the agent shall be mentioned a second time; as in maA qaAma zayodN A^awo maA qaAma EamorNw [ Zeyd did not stand: nay, rather 'Amr did not stand ]; and laA yaqomN zaydN A^awo laA yaqumo Eamoruw [ Let not Zeyd stand: nay, rather let not 'Amr stand ]. (Mughnee.) Accord. to Fr, (Th, M, Mughnee,) it has this meaning in A^awo yaziyduwna [ Nay, rather they exceeded that number], (Th, S, M, Mughnee,) in the Kur [xxxvii. 147, cited above]: (S:) or the meaning is, or they would exceed [that number] in your estimation: or these words with those preceding them in the same verse mean, we sent him to a multitude of whom, if ye saw them, ye would say, They are a hundred thousand, or they exceed [that number]; (M, Mughnee; *) so that it denotes doubt on the part of men, not of God, for He is not subject to doubt: (M:) or we sent him to a hundred thousand in the estimation of men, or they exceeded [that number] in the estimation of men; for God does not doubt: (S:) or Aw is here used to denote vagueness of meaning: (IB, Mughnee:) or, it is said, to denote that a person might choose between saying, “they are a hundred thousand,“ and saying, “they are more;“ but this may not be when one of the two things is the fact: or, accord. to some of the Koofees, it has the meaning of wa : and each of these meanings, except the last, has been assigned to Aw as occurring in the Kur ii. 69 and xvi. 79. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- Seventhly, it denotes division; (Mughnee, K; *) as in the saying, Alkalimapu A@somN A^awo fiEolN A^awo HarofN [ The word is a noun or a verb or a particle ]: so said Ibn-Málik: or, as he afterwards said, in preference, it denotes separation ( Alt~afriyq ) divested of the attribute of denoting doubt and vagueness of meaning and the giving of option or choice; adducing as one of his exs. of this meaning the saying, waqaAluwA kuwnuwA huwdFA A^awo naSaAraY [in the Kur ii. 129, And they said, “Be ye Jews” or “Christians” ]; because the use of w in division is better; as when you say, Alkalimapu A@somN wafiEolN waHarofN : or it denotes, accord. to some, distinction ( Alt~afoSiyl ); and the meaning of the ex. last cited, say they, is, and the Jews said, “Be ye Jews,” and the Christians said, “Be ye Christians.” (Mughnee.) It is [said to be] used in this last sense (that of AltfDyl ) in the saying, kunotu A=kulu All~aHoma A^awi AlEasala [ I used to eat flesh-meat or honey ]; i. e. I used to eat flesh-meat one time and honey another time: and so in the Kur vii. 3 and x. 13. ― -b9- Eighthly, (Mughnee,) it is used in the sense of the exceptive A_il~aA , (Mughnee, K,) or A_il~aA A^ano (M;) and in this case the aor. after it is mansoob, because of A^ano suppressed. (Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, laA^aqotulan~ahu A^awo yusolima [ I will assuredly slay him or he shall become a Muslim; i. e., unless he become a Muslim ]. (Mughnee. [And a similar ex. is given in the M.]) So, too, in the saying, wakunotu A_i*aA gamazotu qanaApa qawomK kasarotu kuEuwbahaA A^awo tasotaqiymaA [ And I used, when I pinched and pressed the spear of a people, to break its knots, or joints, or its internodal portions, (the shaft being a cane,) or, i. e. unless, it became straight ]: (Mughnee, K: *) a prov., of which the author is Ziyád ElAajam; meaning, when a people behaved with hardness to me, I endeavoured to soften them: (TA in art. gmz :) thus related by Sb, the verb ending it being rendered mansoob by Aw ; and thus he heard it from some one or more of the Arabs; but in the original verses, which are but three, it is tasotaqiymu , with refa. (IB and TA in art. gmz .) [And similar to these above are the sayings,] A_n~ahu lifulaAnK A^awomaA binajodK qarZahu [ Verily it belongs to such a one or there is not, i. e. unless there be not, in Nejd, a qaraZap (see art. qrZ )]: and laA=tiyan~aka A^awo maA binajodK qaraZapN [ I will assuredly come to thee or there is not, i. e. unless there be not, in Nejd, a qaraZap ]; meaning I will assuredly come to thee, in truth. (T.) ― -b10- Ninthly, (Mughnee,) it is used in the sense of A_ilaY , (Mughnee, K,) or A_ilaY A^ano ; (S;) in which case also the aor. after it is mansoob, because of A^ano suppressed: (Mughnee:) and in the sense of Hat~aY [which is also syn. with A_itaY ]. (Fr, T, M, K.) So in the saying, laA^aDoriban~ahu A^awo yatuwba [ I will assuredly beat him until he repent ]. (S. [And similar exs. of Aw as explained by Hat~ay are given in the T (from Fr) and in the M and in the Mughnee.]) And so in the saying of the poet, laA^asotasohilan~a AlS~aEoba A^awo A^udorika AlmunaY famaA A@noqaAdati AlA=maAlu A_il~aA liSaAbiri [ I will assuredly deem easy what is difficult until I attain the objects of wish; for hopes become not easy of accomplishment save to one who is patient ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b11- Tenthly, some say, (Mughnee,) it denotes nearness [of one event or thing to another]; as in the saying, maA A^adoriY A^asal~ama A^awo wad~aEa [ I know not whether he saluted or bade farewell ]: (Mughnee, K: [but in the CK this ex. is misplaced:]) this, however, is manifestly wrong; Aw being here used to denote doubt, and the denoting of nearness being only inferred from the fact of the saluting being confounded in the mind with the bidding farewell, since this is impossible or improbable when the two times are far apart. (Mughnee.) ― -b12- Eleventhly, (Mughnee,) it occurs as a conditional, (T, Mughnee, K,) accord. to Ks alone; (T;) or rather as a conjunctive and conditional; waA_ino being meant to be understood in its place; though in truth the verb that precedes it indicates that the conditional particle [ A_ino ] is meant to be understood [before that verb], and Aw retains its proper character, but forms part of that which has a conditional meaning because conjoined with a preceding conditional phrase. (Mughnee.) So in the saying, laA^aDoriban~ahu EaA$a A^awo maAta , (Mughnee, K,) i. e., A_ino EaAiD baEoda AlD~arobi wa A_ino maAta [ I will assuredly beat him if he live (after the beating) or if he die ]: so says Ibn-Esh-Shejeree. (Mughnee.) ― -b13- Twelfthly, accord. to Ibn-Esh-Shejeree, on the authority of some one or more of the Koofees, (Mughnee,) it denotes division into parts, or portions; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 129, before cited,] waqaAluwA kuwnuwA huwdFA A^aw naSaAraY , (Mughnee, K,) i. e. And they said, “Be ye, some of you, Jews, and, some of you, Christians: ” (TA:) but [IHsh says,] it appears to me that the meaning here is that of Alt~afoSiyl mentioned before. (Mughnee.) ― -b14- [In the K it is said to occur also in the sense of A^ano : but this is evidently a mistake, app. originating in one of the two principal sources of the K, namely, the M, in which the same is said, but is exemplified by a phrase in which it is explained by A_il~aA A^ano , the eighth of the meanings of A^awo mentioned above.] ― -b15- See also A^aw~N below.

And jaA=niY rajulN A^awi A@moraA^apN [ A man or a woman came to me ]. (Mbr, T.) And labiy^onaA yawomFA A^awo baEoDa yawomK [in the Kur xviii. 18 and xxiii. 115, We have remained a day or part of a day ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- Secondly, (Mughnee,) it denotes vagueness of meaning. (S, Msb, Mughnee, K.) S [it may be used] in the first of the .exs. given above. (Msb.) And so in the saying, waA^an~aA A^awo A_iy~aAkumo laEalaY hudFy A^awo fiY DalaAlK mubiynK [ And verily we or ye are following a right direction or in manifest error ], (S, Mughnee,) in the Kur [xxxiv. 23]; (S;) the ex. being in the former Aw . (Mughnee.) ― -b4- Thirdly, (Mughnee,) it denotes the giving of option, or choice. (T, S, M, Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, kuli Als~amaka A^awi A@$orabi All~abana [ Eat thou the fish, or drink thou the milk ]; i. e. do not thou both of these actions; (Mbr, T, S;) but choose which of them thou wilt. (Mbr, T.) And tazaw~ajo hinodFA A^awo A^uxotahaA [ Take thou as wife Hind or her sister ]. (Mughnee.) And [in like manner] it denotes the making choice. (T.) [So when you say, saA^atazaw~aju hinodFA A^awo A^uxotahaA , meaning I will take as wife Hind or her sister; whichever of them I choose.] ― -b5- Fourthly, (Mughnee,) it denotes the allowing a thing, or making it allowable. (T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, jaAlisi Hasana A^awi A@bona siyriyna [ Sit thou with El- Hasan or Ibn-Seereen ]. (Mbr, T, S.) And qumo A^awi A@qoEudo [ Stand thou or sit ]: and the person to whom this is said may do [one or] both of the se actions. (Msb.) [And similar exs. are given in the Mughnee.]) But walaA tuTiEo minohumo A=vimFA A^aw kafuwrFA [in the Kur lxxvi. 24, And obey not thou, of them, a sinner or a person very ungrateful to God, ] means that thou shalt not obey either of such persons: (Mbr, T, Mughnee:) in which case Aw is more forcible than wa ; for when you say to a person, laA tuTiEo zayodFA waEamorFA [ Obey not thou Zeyd and 'Amr ], he may obey one of them, since the command is that he shall not obey the two. (Zj, T.) ― -b6- Fifthly, (Mughnee,) it denotes unrestricted conjunction. (Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, in the Kur [iv. 46 and v. 9], A^awo jaA='a A^aHadN minokumo mina AlgaAy^iTi [ And if any one of you cometh from the privy ]; (TA;) [where, however, it may also be rendered or, though] meaning wajaA='a ; (T, TA;) the w in this explanation being what is termed a denotative of state. (T.) So, too, accord. to AZ, in the expression A^awo yaziyduwna [ And they exceeded that number], in the Kur [xxxvii. 147]: but see below. (TA.) And so in the words, A^awo A^ano nafoEala fiY A^amowaAlinaA maA na$aA='u [ And our doing, in respect of our possessions, what we will ], in the Kur [xi. 89]. (T, TA.) ― -b7- Sixthly, it denotes transition, (Mughnee,) used in the sense of [the adversative particle] balo , (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) in a case of amplification of speech; (S;) accord. to Sb, on two conditions; that it shall be preceded by a negation or a prohibition, and that the agent shall be mentioned a second time; as in maA qaAma zayodN A^awo maA qaAma EamorNw [ Zeyd did not stand: nay, rather 'Amr did not stand ]; and laA yaqomN zaydN A^awo laA yaqumo Eamoruw [ Let not Zeyd stand: nay, rather let not 'Amr stand ]. (Mughnee.) Accord. to Fr, (Th, M, Mughnee,) it has this meaning in A^awo yaziyduwna [ Nay, rather they exceeded that number], (Th, S, M, Mughnee,) in the Kur [xxxvii. 147, cited above]: (S:) or the meaning is, or they would exceed [that number] in your estimation: or these words with those preceding them in the same verse mean, we sent him to a multitude of whom, if ye saw them, ye would say, They are a hundred thousand, or they exceed [that number]; (M, Mughnee; *) so that it denotes doubt on the part of men, not of God, for He is not subject to doubt: (M:) or we sent him to a hundred thousand in the estimation of men, or they exceeded [that number] in the estimation of men; for God does not doubt: (S:) or Aw is here used to denote vagueness of meaning: (IB, Mughnee:) or, it is said, to denote that a person might choose between saying, “they are a hundred thousand,“ and saying, “they are more;“ but this may not be when one of the two things is the fact: or, accord. to some of the Koofees, it has the meaning of wa : and each of these meanings, except the last, has been assigned to Aw as occurring in the Kur ii. 69 and xvi. 79. (Mughnee.) ― -b8- Seventhly, it denotes division; (Mughnee, K; *) as in the saying, Alkalimapu A@somN A^awo fiEolN A^awo HarofN [ The word is a noun or a verb or a particle ]: so said Ibn-Málik: or, as he afterwards said, in preference, it denotes separation ( Alt~afriyq ) divested of the attribute of denoting doubt and vagueness of meaning and the giving of option or choice; adducing as one of his exs. of this meaning the saying, waqaAluwA kuwnuwA huwdFA A^awo naSaAraY [in the Kur ii. 129, And they said, “Be ye Jews” or “Christians” ]; because the use of w in division is better; as when you say, Alkalimapu A@somN wafiEolN waHarofN : or it denotes, accord. to some, distinction ( Alt~afoSiyl ); and the meaning of the ex. last cited, say they, is, and the Jews said, “Be ye Jews,” and the Christians said, “Be ye Christians.” (Mughnee.) It is [said to be] used in this last sense (that of AltfDyl ) in the saying, kunotu A=kulu All~aHoma A^awi AlEasala [ I used to eat flesh-meat or honey ]; i. e. I used to eat flesh-meat one time and honey another time: and so in the Kur vii. 3 and x. 13. ― -b9- Eighthly, (Mughnee,) it is used in the sense of the exceptive A_il~aA , (Mughnee, K,) or A_il~aA A^ano (M;) and in this case the aor. after it is mansoob, because of A^ano suppressed. (Mughnee, K.) So in the saying, laA^aqotulan~ahu A^awo yusolima [ I will assuredly slay him or he shall become a Muslim; i. e., unless he become a Muslim ]. (Mughnee. [And a similar ex. is given in the M.]) So, too, in the saying, wakunotu A_i*aA gamazotu qanaApa qawomK kasarotu kuEuwbahaA A^awo tasotaqiymaA [ And I used, when I pinched and pressed the spear of a people, to break its knots, or joints, or its internodal portions, (the shaft being a cane,) or, i. e. unless, it became straight ]: (Mughnee, K: *) a prov., of which the author is Ziyád ElAajam; meaning, when a people behaved with hardness to me, I endeavoured to soften them: (TA in art. gmz :) thus related by Sb, the verb ending it being rendered mansoob by Aw ; and thus he heard it from some one or more of the Arabs; but in the original verses, which are but three, it is tasotaqiymu , with refa. (IB and TA in art. gmz .) [And similar to these above are the sayings,] A_n~ahu lifulaAnK A^awomaA binajodK qarZahu [ Verily it belongs to such a one or there is not, i. e. unless there be not, in Nejd, a qaraZap (see art. qrZ )]: and laA=tiyan~aka A^awo maA binajodK qaraZapN [ I will assuredly come to thee or there is not, i. e. unless there be not, in Nejd, a qaraZap ]; meaning I will assuredly come to thee, in truth. (T.) ― -b10- Ninthly, (Mughnee,) it is used in the sense of A_ilaY , (Mughnee, K,) or A_ilaY A^ano ; (S;) in which case also the aor. after it is mansoob, because of A^ano suppressed: (Mughnee:) and in the sense of Hat~aY [which is also syn. with A_itaY ]. (Fr, T, M, K.) So in the saying, laA^aDoriban~ahu A^awo yatuwba [ I will assuredly beat him until he repent ]. (S. [And similar exs. of Aw as explained by Hat~ay are given in the T (from Fr) and in the M and in the Mughnee.]) And so in the saying of the poet, laA^asotasohilan~a AlS~aEoba A^awo A^udorika AlmunaY famaA A@noqaAdati AlA=maAlu A_il~aA liSaAbiri [ I will assuredly deem easy what is difficult until I attain the objects of wish; for hopes become not easy of accomplishment save to one who is patient ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b11- Tenthly, some say, (Mughnee,) it denotes nearness [of one event or thing to another]; as in the saying, maA A^adoriY A^asal~ama A^awo wad~aEa [ I know not whether he saluted or bade farewell ]: (Mughnee, K: [but in the CK this ex. is misplaced:]) this, however, is manifestly wrong; Aw being here used to denote doubt, and the denoting of nearness being only inferred from the fact of the saluting being confounded in the mind with the bidding farewell, since this is impossible or improbable when the two times are far apart. (Mughnee.) ― -b12- Eleventhly, (Mughnee,) it occurs as a conditional, (T, Mughnee, K,) accord. to Ks alone; (T;) or rather as a conjunctive and conditional; waA_ino being meant to be understood in its place; though in truth the verb that precedes it indicates that the conditional particle [ A_ino ] is meant to be understood [before that verb], and Aw retains its proper character, but forms part of that which has a conditional meaning because conjoined with a preceding conditional phrase. (Mughnee.) So in the saying, laA^aDoriban~ahu EaA$a A^awo maAta , (Mughnee, K,) i. e., A_ino EaAiD baEoda AlD~arobi wa A_ino maAta [ I will assuredly beat him if he live (after the beating) or if he die ]: so says Ibn-Esh-Shejeree. (Mughnee.) ― -b13- Twelfthly, accord. to Ibn-Esh-Shejeree, on the authority of some one or more of the Koofees, (Mughnee,) it denotes division into parts, or portions; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 129, before cited,] waqaAluwA kuwnuwA huwdFA A^aw naSaAraY , (Mughnee, K,) i. e. And they said, “Be ye, some of you, Jews, and, some of you, Christians: ” (TA:) but [IHsh says,] it appears to me that the meaning here is that of Alt~afoSiyl mentioned before. (Mughnee.) ― -b14- [In the K it is said to occur also in the sense of A^ano : but this is evidently a mistake, app. originating in one of the two principal sources of the K, namely, the M, in which the same is said, but is exemplified by a phrase in which it is explained by A_il~aA A^ano , the eighth of the meanings of A^awo mentioned above.] ― -b15- See also A^aw~N below.

sourceDefinition: , also pronounced baAjN , without ' , (IAar, S, Msb, K,) but the former alone is mentioned by Th in the Fs, and is the chaste word, (TA,) arabicized, from the Persian baAhaA , (S,) A sort, or species, (S, K,) of food, or viands. (S.) Hence the saying, AijoEali AlbaA^ojaAt baA_ojAF waAHidFA [ Make thou the sorts, or species, of food, or viands, to be one sort, or species ]: (S, K:) occurring in a trad., in which it is without ' in each case, accord. to IDrst: several different sorts of food being brought to 'Omar, he asked respecting them, and it was said, [They are] sikobaAj and zirobaAj and A_isofiydobaAj ; whereupon he ordered that the bowls should be brought, and their contents were emptied into one; he saying the words above. (Marginal note in a copy of the S.) IKh says that a man would bring various sorts [of food], and one would say, AijoEalohaA bA^ojAF waAHdiA [ Make thou them to be one sort ]. (TA.) The pl. is [ baA^ojaAtN , as shown above, as though the sing. were baA^ojapN , and] A^abowaAjN . (Msb, TA.) laA^ajoEalan~a Aln~aAsa kul~ahumo baA^ojFA waAHidFA is [likewise] a saying of 'Omar, (Msb, TA,) meaning [ I will assuredly make the people, all of them, to be ] one body or assemblage; baA^ojN signifying a state of assembling, or collecting together: (Kz, TA:) or [ of ] one uniform way or mode or manner, (Msb, TA,) as El-Fihree says in the Expos. of the Fs, on the authority of ISd in the book entitled El-'Awees; (TA;) i. e., in respect of gifts, or allowances: (Msb:) accord. to IAar, it is from baA^ojN or baAjN signifying a uniform line of road. (TA.) You say also, Aln~aAsu baA^ojN waAHidN The people are [ as ] one thing. (TA.) And humo fiY A^amorK baA^ojK They are [ in one and the same, or] in an equal, or a uniform, case. (K.) And jaEala AlkalaAma baA^ojAF waAxidFA He made the speech, or language, to be [ uniform, or] of one mode, or manner. (TA.) And AijoEalo h`*A Al$~aYo'a baA^ojFA waAHidFA Make thou this thing to be [ uniform, or] of one way, or mode, or manner. (ISk.) And AijoEali AlA^amora baA^ojFA waAHidFA Make thou the affair, or case, [ uniform, or] one uniform thing. (Fr.)

definition: A certain beast of prey, (M, K,) well known;
sourceDefinition: A certain beast of prey, (M, K,) well known; (K;) a certain animal, (Msb,) namely, the furaAniq [or lion's provider ], (S,) that emulates, or vies with, the lion in running, or that is hostile to the lion: [so may be rendered the words yuEaAdiY AlA^asada ; and in the uncertainty that exists respecting the animal in question, the meaning of this expression is doubtful: an animal may be called (as the jackal is) the lion's provider merely because the lion follows it and deprives it of its prey:] (S, Msb:) or a certain Indian animal, stronger than the lion, between which and the lion and leopard, or panther, ( namir ,) exists hostility ( muEaAdaApN ); when it attacks the leopard, or panther, ( nmr ,), the lion aids the latter; but the scorpion is on friendly terms with it, and sometimes makes its abode in its hair: (Kzw:) the word is foreign, or Persian, ( A^aEojamiY~N ,) [app. the Persian babaro , which is said to be applied to the tiger, leopard, and lion, ] arabicized: (M, K:) Az thinks it to be a foreign word introduced into the Arabic language: (Msb:) pl. bubuwrN . (S, Msb, K.)

definition: She (a woman) showed, or displayed, her finery, or ornaments, (S, Msb, K,) and beauties of person or form or countenance, (S, Msb,) to men, (S, K,) or to strangers, or men distantly related to her;
sourceDefinition: She (a woman) showed, or displayed, her finery, or ornaments, (S, Msb, K,) and beauties of person or form or countenance, (S, Msb,) to men, (S, K,) or to strangers, or men distantly related to her; (Msb;) to do which is culpable; but to do so to the husband is not: (TA:) or she showed her face: or she showed the beauties of her neck and face: or she did so exhibiting a pretty look: (TA:) or she showed, or displayed, her finery, or ornaments, and what excites a man's lust. (A boo-Is-hák, TA.) Fr, referring to verse 33 of ch. xxxiii. of the Kur, says that in the time when Abraham was born, the women used to wear a shirt of pearls, not sewed at the two sides; or, as some say, they used to wear garments which did not conceal their persons. (TA.)

definition: [Gr. πύργος , (Golius,) A tower; ] an angle, syn. rukon , (S, K,) of a fortress, (S,) or of a city: (TA:) and sometimes a fortress itself: (S, K:) so called from its conspicuousness and construction...
sourceDefinition: [Gr. πύργος , (Golius,) A tower; ] an angle, syn. rukon , (S, K,) of a fortress, (S,) or of a city: (TA:) and sometimes a fortress itself: (S, K:) so called from its conspicuousness and construction and height: (TA: [see 1:]) or the primary signification of brj is strength; whence A^aboraju in a sense explained below: (Har p. 286:) pl. [of mult.] buruwjN and [of pauc.] A^aboraAjN : (S:) the buruwjN of the wall of a city or fortress are chambers ( buyuwt [meaning towers ]) built upon the wall: and such chambers ( bywt ) built upon the sides of the angles of a qaSor [i. e. pavilion or palace &c.] are sometimes thus called. (Lth.) [Hence,] buroju HamaAmK [ A pigeon-turret; a pigeon-house; being generally constructed in the form of a turret, or of a sugar-loaf;] a lodging-place of pigeons: pl. as above. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) [ A sign of the Zodiac; ] one of the buruwj of the heaven; (S, K;) which are twelve in number; every one having a distinct name: (TA:) the Arabs in ancient times did not know them: (Ham p. 560:) pl. A^aboraAjN as well as buruwjN : (Msb, TA:) these are meant by the buruwj mentioned in the Kur xv. 16 and xxv. 62 and lxxxv. 1: (Bd, Jel:) or in the last of these instances, (Bd,) by the brwj in the heaven are meant the Mansions of the Moon: (Bd, Msb:) or the stars or asterisms or constellations: (TA:) or the great stars or asterisms or constellations; (Bd, Msb;) and so, accord. to Zj, in the second of the said passages of the Kur: (TA:) or the gates of heaven: (Bd, Msb:) or, as some say, i. q. quSuwr [i. e. pavilions &c.]. (TA.)

definition: (in which the final radical letter is elided, [and replaced by p ,] Msb) A ring (T, S, M, &c.
sourceDefinition: (in which the final radical letter is elided, [and replaced by p ,] Msb) A ring (T, S, M, &c.) of brass, (Lth, Lh, T, S, M, [in a copy of the Msb, mn Swf is erroneously put for mino SuforK ,]) or of silver, (Lth, T,) or of some other material, (Lh, M,) slender, and bent at the two ends [lest it should open at the place where the two ends meet], that is put in the nose of a she-camel, (Lth, T,) or put in the nose of the camel, (M, Msb, K,) or in the flesh of the nose of the camel, (Lh, S, M, K,) or, as As says, in one of the two sides of the two nostrils, (S,) app. either for the purpose of ornament or to render the animal obedient; (MF;) [ generally for the latter purpose, to attach the rein thereto: ] when the ring is of hair, it is termed xizaAmapN ; (As, S, Msb;) and when of wood, xi$aA$N : (Msb:) Aboo-' Alee mentions, and explains in like manner, ↓ barowapN and burFY ; [the latter as pl. of the former;] but this is extr.: (M:) J says, [in the S,] Aboo- 'Alee says that burapN is originally barowapN , because it has burFY for a pl., like as qaroyap has qurFY ; but Aboo-' Alee does not say this; he only desires to show that the final radical letter of burapN is w by the fact that barowapN is a dial. var. thereof: (IB, TA:) some, however, remarking upon J's saying that the original of barapN is barowapN , assert that it is correctly ↓ burowapN : (TA:) burapN also signifies an anklet: (M, K:) or any ring; such as a bracelet and an earring and an anklet and the like of these: (S:) the pl. (in the former and the latter senses, M, TA) is buraAtN , (S, M, K,) in [some of] the copies of the K erroneously written buraApN , (TA,) and burFY , (T, S, M,) and buruwna , contr. to analogy, (Msb,) or buriyna (T, S, M, K, [in all of which, except the last, this is in the accus. or the gen. case, but, as it is the nom. case in the K, it may be that buruwna and buriyna are dial. vars., like sinuwna and siniyna ,]) and buriyna . (M, K: [in a copy of the former of which, accord. to the TT, buriY~N and biriY~N are put in the place of the last two of these pls.])

sourceDefinition: The mule; i. e. the animal generated between the he-ass and the mare [or sometimes between the horse and the she-ass ]; (TA;) also called ↓ bag~aAlN ; so in a verse of Jereer: (S, Sgh:) pl. A^abogalN [a pl. of pauc.] (JK) and A^abogaAlN , [also] a pl. of pauc., (Msb,) and bigaAlN , (JK, S, Msb, K,) a pl. of mult.; (Msb;) and quasi-pl. n. ↓ maboguwlaA='u , (K,) meaning a number of mules ( bigaAl ) together: (JK, * S:) the female is termed bagolapN ; (S, Msb, K;) pl. bagalaAtN and bigaAlN . (Msb.) See 2, in two places. You say TariyqN fiyhi A^abowaAlu AlbigaAli [ A road in which is the urine of mules ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) a difficult road. (TA.) And fulaAnapu A^aEoqaru mino bagolapK [ Such a woman is more barren than a she-mule ]. (TA.) And Albagolu nagolN wa huwa lahu A^aholN [ The mule is a bastard, and he is a relation to him ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) he is a bastard. (TA.) And as the mule suggests the idea of evil disposition, or perverseness, and roughness, you say, in describing him who is low, or ignoble, huwa bagolN nagolN (assumed tropical:) [ he is a mule, a bastard ]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) The people of Egypt say, Ai$otaraY fulaAnN bagolapF HasonaA='a , meaning (tropical:) [ Such a one bought a beautiful ] female slave: and fiY bayoti baniY fulaAnK bigaAlN [(tropical:) In the house of the sons of such a one are slaves, or female slaves ]: and Ai$otarayotu mino bigaAli Alyamano wa l`kino bigaAliY Alv~amano [(tropical:) I bought of the slaves, or female slaves, of El-Yemen, but for a high price ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (ISh, TA,) inf. n. balajN , (S, K, TA,) He (a man) had a clear, a conspicuous, or a white, space between the eyes, not having the eyebrows joined; (ISh, TA;) he had a clear space between the eyebrows; (S, K, TA;) he had a wide space, or a space clear of hair, between the eyebrows. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, He (a man) was, or became, bright in countenance: or fair, beautiful, and wide in countenance: or (assumed tropical:) open and pleasant, or cheerful, in countenance: or (assumed tropical:) liberal with acts of beneficence: or (tropical:) generous, beneficent, and open and pleasant, or cheerful, in countenance: see the part. n. A^abolaju , below.] ― -b3- And [hence,] aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) (tropical:) He (a man, TA) was, or became, joyful, glad, or happy. (K, TA.) You say, balija biAl$~ayo'i (tropical:) He rejoiced at the thing; or was rejoiced by it; as also valija . (As, TA.) And balija bihi AlS~adoru faraHFA (tropical:) The bosom became dilated with joy thereat. (A.) And balija baEoda maA Harija (tropical:) [ It (the bosom) became dilated with joy after it had been contracted with grief]. (TA.) ― -b4- [And hence,] aor. and inf. n. as above; (Msb;) and balaja , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. buluwjN ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ Anblj , (S, K,) or ↓ Abtlj ; (so in copies of the A and Msb;) and ↓ tbl~j ; (S, A, K;) and ↓ Ablj ; (Msb, K;) (assumed tropical:) It (the dawn, or daybreak,) shone, was bright, or shone brightly. (S, A, Msb, K.) And Al$~amosu ↓ A^abolajati (assumed tropical:) The sun shone, was bright, or shone brightly. (TA.) And Al$~aYo'u ↓ AblAj~ (assumed tropical:) The thing shone, was bright, or shone brightly. (TA.) ― -b5- And hence, (Msb,) balaja AlHaq~u , and balija ; (Msb;) or ↓ Ablj ; (A, TA;) (tropical:) The truth became apparent, (A, Msb, TA,) manifest, evident, or clear. (A, Msb.) And ↓ AblAj~ , inf. n. AiboliyjaAjN , (S, and so the inf. n. is written in a copy of the K: in another copy of the K it is written AibolijaAjN [inf. n. of ↓ Ablj~ ], and the verb is written Ablj~ in a copy of the S: accord. to the CK, the inf. n. is AiboliylaAjN [of which the verb is ↓ Ablwlj ]:) said of anything, (S, TA,) signifies (tropical:) It was, or became, apparent, manifest, evident, or clear. definition: Clearness of the space between the eyebrows: (S, A, K:) or width of the space between the eyebrows;
sourceDefinition: Clearness of the space between the eyebrows: (S, A, K:) or width of the space between the eyebrows; or [ of ] the space between the eyebrows when clear of hair; as also ↓ balajN [which is the inf. n. of balija ]. (TA.) One says, maA A^aHosana bulojatahu How beautiful is the clearness of the space between his eyebrows! (A.) ― -b2- The part behind the EaAriD [or side of the cheek or face ], to the ear, when there is no hair upon it. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, and ↓ balojapN , (assumed tropical:) The light (S, L, K) of the dawn, or daybreak, (S, L,) in the last part of the night, (S, TA,) at the breaking of the dawn. (TA.) You say, raA^ayotu bulojapN AlS~uboHi (assumed tropical:) I saw the light of the dawn. (S.) And laqiytuhu Einoda Albulojapi (assumed tropical:) [ I met, or found, him, or it, at the break of the dawn ]. (A.) And sarayotu Ald~ulojapa wa Albalojapa Hat~aY waSolatu (assumed tropical:) [ I journeyed during the whole night, or from the beginning of the night, or during the latter part of the night, and the breaking of the dawn, until I arrived ]. (A.) And it is said in a trad., layolapu Alqadori bulojapi (assumed tropical:) The night of Alqdr is bright [ like the dawn ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A man having a clear, a conspicuous, or a white, space between the eyes, not having the eyebrows joined: (ISh, TA:) or having such a space between the eyebrows, (K, * TA,) not having the eyebrows joined: (S, TA:) or having a wide space, or a space clear of hair, between the eyebrows: fem. balojaA='u . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Bright of countenance; the Prophet being said by UmmMaabad to have been A^abolaju Alwajohi ; by which she did not mean the balaj of the eyebrows, for she described him as having joined eyebrows: (A'Obeyd, S, TA:) or fair, beautiful, and wide in countenance, whether long or short: or [alone, or] followed by ↓ balojN , (assumed tropical:) open and pleasant, or cheerful, in countenance; (TA;) and so ↓ the latter alone: (K:) or ↓ the latter, (tropical:) open and pleasant, or cheerful, in countenance, with beneficence: (TA:) or the former, and ↓ the latter, and ↓ baliyjN , (assumed tropical:) liberal with acts of beneficence: (TA:) or the first, (tropical:) generous, beneficent, and open and pleasant, or cheerful, in countenance; although having joined eyebrows. (A, TA.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Shining, bright, or shining brightly; applied to the dawn, or daybreak; (S, A, Msb;) and so ↓ baliyjN , applied to a thing [of any kind]: (TA:) and the former, anything (assumed tropical:) apparent, manifest, evident, or clear; (K;) thus applied to a face, and to the dawn, (TA,) and to the truth, (Msb, TA,) and to an affair or event, or a case, &c. (TA.) It is an act. part. n. of balija . (Msb.) You say, AlHaq~u A^abolaju wa AlbaATilu lajolajN (tropical:) The truth is apparent, manifest, evident, or clear; [ and falsity is a cause of embarrassment, or hesitation, to the speaker; ] (S, A; *) i. e., the latter is agitated to and fro, without having utterance: (S in art. lj :) or the truth is lucid and direct; and falsity is confused and indirect. (TA in that art.) And Huj~apN balojaA='u (assumed tropical:) A manifest, an evident, or a clear, proof or argument. (Msb.)

definition: , (T, S, M, L, Mughnee, K,) as also ↓ baAyada , (L, K,) or baAy^ida , (so in the Mughnee and in a MS.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, L, Mughnee, K,) as also ↓ baAyada , (L, K,) or baAy^ida , (so in the Mughnee and in a MS. copy of the K and in the CK, and in a MS. copy of the K omitted,) a noun inseparably prefixed to A^an~a with its complement, (Mughnee,) used as syn. with gayor , (Ks, T, S, M, &c.,) but never otherwise than in the accus. case, nor as an epithet, nor otherwise than as an exceptive in a case in which the thing excepted is disunited in kind from that from which the exception is made. (Mughnee.) You say, huwa kaviyru AlmaAli bayoda A^an~ahu baxiylN He is possessed of abundant, or much, wealth, but he is niggardly. (ISk, S, M, A, Msb, Mughnee.) ― -b2- Also as syn. with EalaY , (M, K,) as some say; (A'Obeyd, M;) but to render it in the former manner is preferable. (M.) Accord. to some, (L,) it is syn. with EalaY in the following trad.: naHonu AlA=xiruwna Als~aAbiquwna yawoma AlqyaAmapi bayoda A^an~ahumo A^uwtuw AlkitaAba mino qabolinaA wa A^uwtiynaAhu mino baEodihimo [ We, the latter people, shall be those who will precede on the day of resurrection, although they were given the Scripture before us, and we were given it after them ]: (T, L:) El-Umawee holds it to be so: (T:) but Ks says that it here signifies gayor [as in the former ex.]: (T, L: [and so says IHsh in the Mughnee:]) accord. to one recital, it is bAyad ; (L;) or baAy^ida ; so in the Musnad of the Imám Esh-Sháfi'ee: (Mughnee:) IAth says, I have not found this in the classical language in the sense of EalaY : some say that it is biA^ayodK , i. e. by means of strength, or power; and that the meaning is, we shall be those who will precede to Paradise on the day of resurrection by means of strength, or power, given us by God. (L.) ― -b3- Also, [accord. to some,] as meaning mino A^ajoli : (L, Mughnee, K:) as in the saying of Mohammad, A^anaA A^afoSaHu AlEarabi bayoda A^an~iY mino qurayo$K wana$aA^otu fiY baniY saEodK [ I am the most chaste in speech of the Arabs because I am of the tribe of Kureysh and I grew up among the children of Saad ]: (T, L: [in the Mughnee given somewhat differently:]) but Ibn-Málik and others say that it here, also, means gyr , after the manner in which the latter is used in the saying [of a poet], walaA Eayoba fiyhimo gayora A^an~a suyuwfahumo bihin~a fuluwlN mino qiraAEi AlkataAy^ibi [And there is no blemish in them, save that their swords have in them notches from the conflicting of the troops]. (Mughnee.) This manner of praising is termed by Abu-l-'Abbás Mohammad Ibn-Yezeed AisotivobaAtN . (Ham p. 474.) ― -b4- mayoda is also a dial. var. of the same. (A'Obeyd, T, Mughnee.)

definition: [in Hebr. 165 ] A great serpent; (K;) a kind of serpent, (Lth, T, S, M,) one of the greatest of serpents, (Lth, T,) or like the greatest thereof: (M:) it is related that a company of soldiers, on the...
sourceDefinition: [in Hebr. 165 ] A great serpent; (K;) a kind of serpent, (Lth, T, S, M,) one of the greatest of serpents, (Lth, T,) or like the greatest thereof: (M:) it is related that a company of soldiers, on the shore of the Sea of Syria, saw a cloud divide upon the sea, and then rise, and they saw the tail of the tn~yn in a state of commotion in the fringe of the cloud: it is also related that a cloud carries the tn~yn to the country of Yájooj and Májooj [or Gog and Magog], and casts it down there, and they assemble thereupon, and eat its flesh: (T:) [these stories are fanciful accounts of the natural phenomenon called a water-spout, to which this name is applied by the Arabs in the present day: but the word is generally understood to mean a dragon: and a great sea-monster; ] an aquatic animal, great in make, terrible in appearance, long and broad in the body, large in the head, having very glistening eyes, wide mouth and inside, and many teeth: it swallows many animals; the animals of the land and of the sea fear it; and when it moves, the sea becomes agitated with waves by reason of its great strength: in its first state, it is a malignant serpent, that eats what it sees of the beasts of the land; and when its mischief becomes great, God sends an angel that carries it away, and throws it to Yájooj and Májooj: it is related of one that was seen to fall, that it was found to be about two leagues in length, of a colour like that of the leopard, with scales like those of a fish, two great fins in form like those of a fish, a head like a great hill, resembling the head of a man, two long and great ears, and two round eyes; and from its neck branched forth six other necks, every one of them nearly twenty cubits long, and every one of them having a head like that of the serpent. (Kzw.) [Golius thinks it to mean The shark (“ carcharias ”).] ― -b2- Hence, Alt~in~iynu is (assumed tropical:) A certain najom [or constellation; the constellation of the Dragon ]; thus named as being likened to the serpent so called; (M;) a constellation containing thirty-one stars within the figure; among which are those called Alr~aAqiSu and AlEawaAy^i*u and Alr~ubaEu and Al*~iy^obaAni &c. (Kzw, TA. *) ― -b3- [Also, app., (assumed tropical:) A certain imaginary figure in the heavens, extending along the line of the nodes of a planet, which are called the dragon's head and the dragon's tail, in Arabic Aljawozaharu (from the Persian Gawozihoro ), or AljawozaAharaAni , and also AlEuqodataAni , and, to distinguish each from the other, Alr~aA^osu waAl*~anabu : this line is supposed by Golius to be meant by the following description; but I incline to regard it as the result of a confusion of a description of this line with a description of the zodiacal light, a phenomenon supposed to have been unnoticed by the Arabs:] a slight whiteness in the sky, (Lth, T, K,) not an asterism, (Lth, T,) the body of which is in six signs of the zodiac, and the tail, which is slender, black, and twisted, in the seventh sign: it changes place like the planets; is called in Persian ha$otanobaro , (Lth, T, K,) [app. a mistranscription of hasotaburo ,] in astrological computation; and is inauspicious: (Lth, T:) accord. to J, a certain place in the sky; which is a correct explanation, though said in the K to be a mistake. (TA.)

definition: (tropical:) A star, and a lamp, and fire, (A,) or a flame of fire, or a shooting star, (S,) shining brightly: (S:) or shining, glistening, or gleaming, very brightly, as though piercing through the darkness, and dispelling it.
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A star, and a lamp, and fire, (A,) or a flame of fire, or a shooting star, (S,) shining brightly: (S:) or shining, glistening, or gleaming, very brightly, as though piercing through the darkness, and dispelling it. definition: The instrument with which sawiyq is stirred about with water &c.
sourceDefinition: The instrument with which sawiyq is stirred about with water &c.; (S, A, K, &c.;) which is a piece of wood the end whereof has several sides; (S, L;) or a piece of wood at the head of which are two cross pieces of wood; (A, Mgh, L;) and sometimes having three prongs: (IAth, TA:) pl. majaAdiHu . (L.) ― -b2- It is sometimes used tropically, as relating to evil, or mischief. (L.) [Thus it means (tropical:) A stirrer-up of evil or mischief; or a thing that stirs up, or whereby one stirs up, evil or mischief.] ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Any one of the majaAdiyHu Als~amaA='i [or stirrers-up of the sky, or of rain ]; (L;) these being the A^anowaA='N [or stars, or asterisms, which, by their auroral settings or risings, were believed by the Pagan Arabs to bring rain &c. ]; (S, L, K;) of those AnwA' that seldom or never failed [ to bring rain ], accord. to the Arabs: (Mgh:) the Y in the pl. is added to give fulness to the sound of the kesreh; for the regular pl. is majaAdiHu , and the sing. of mjAdyH should by rule be mijodaAHN . (A, IAth, Mgh.) One says, Arosalati Als~amaA='a majaAdiyHuhaA (L) or majaAdiyHu Algayovi (A) (assumed tropical:) [ Its stirrers-up, or the stirrers-up of rain, or the stars or asterisms which were the bringers of it, sent forth rain ]. It is related of 'Omar, that he ascended the pulpit to pray for rain, and, having only offered a prayer for forgiveness, descended; whereupon it was said to him, “ Thou hast not prayed for rain; ” and he replied, laqadi A@sotasoqayotu bimajaAdiyHi Als~amaA='i (assumed tropical:) [ I have indeed prayed for rain by words which are the stirrers-up of rain ]; making the prayer for forgiveness to be a prayer for rain, in allusion to a passage in the Kur, lxxi. 9 and 10; and meaning thereby to deny the efficacy of the AnwA' . (A, * Mgh, * L.) AlmijodaHu , also pronounced ↓ AlmujodaHu , (S, K,) thus pronounced by El-Umawee, (S,) is moreover the name of (assumed tropical:) A particular star or asterism, one of those which the Pagan Arabs asserted to be bringers of rain: (L:) said to be Ald~abaraAnu [ the Hyades; or the five chief stars thereof; or the brightest star thereof, a of Taurus ]; (S, A, L, K;) [which is called by this name of AldbrAn ] because it rises latterly [with respect to the Pleiades], (S,) or because it follows ( yadoburu , i. e. yatobaEu ,) the Pleiades: (T in art. dbr :) [whence] it is also called HaAdiY Aln~ujuwmi [“ the urger of the stars, ” properly, “ with singing ”], (S,) or HaAdiY Aln~ajomi [“ the urger of the asterism, ” meaning, “ of the Pleiades ”], and taAliY Aln~ajomi [“ the follower of the asterism, ” or, “ of the Pleiades ”], (Kzw,) and Alt~aAliY and Alt~aAbiEu [“ the follower ”]: (Sh:) or it is a small star or asterism, between AldbrAn and Alv~uray~aA [or the Pleiades ]: (IAar, K:) [perhaps meaning the four stars that are the chief stars of the Hyades exclusively of a Tauri: ] or three stars, (Mgh, TA,) like the three stones upon which a cooking-pot rests, (TA,) likened to a three-pronged mijodaH ; (Mgh, TA;) on the [ auroral ] rising of which, heat is expected: (TA:) the Arabs regarded it as one of the AnwA' which [by their auroral setting] foretokened rain. (IAth.) AlmijodaHaAni is a name by which some of the Arabs called (assumed tropical:) The two wings of AljawozaA=' [or Orion ]. (Sh, TA.) ― -b4- mijodaHN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A certain mark made with a hot iron upon the thighs of camels. (K.)

definition: A gulp, or as much as is swallowed at once, of water;
sourceDefinition: A gulp, or as much as is swallowed at once, of water; a juroEap of water being like a luqomap of food: (Msb:) or a sup, or sip; or as much as is supped, or sipped, at once; or a mouthful of what is supped, or sipped; (syn. HusowapN ;) of water; (S, K;) as also ↓ jaroEapN and ↓ jiroEapN : or juroEapN and ↓ jaroEapN are substs. [signifying the act of swallowing water] from jariEa AlmaA='a “ he swallowed the water: ” (K:) or ↓ jaroEapN signifies a single act of swallowing water: (IAth, L:) and juroEapN , what one swallows: (L, K:) or a mouthful which one swallows: (TA:) or a small draught: (IAth:) and its pl. is juraEN . (Msb, TA.) The dim. is ↓ jurayoEapN . (S, K.) And hence the prov., A^afolata fulaAnN jurayoEapa Al*~aqani , (Sgh, K,) the verb being intrans., and jryEp being in the accus. case as a denotative of state, as though the speaker said, A^afolata qaA*ifFA jurayoEapa Al*~aqani ; (Sgh;) or bijurayoEapi Al*~aqani ; (S, K;) or ↓ bijurayoEaA=y^ihaA ; (K;) Such a one escaped [from destruction] when his spirit, or the remains thereof, had become in his mouth; (L, K;) or near thereto, (K,) as a sup [or little sup ] of water to the chin [of a person drinking]; (TA;) or when death was as near to him as a little sup of water to the chin; (L;) or when at his last gasp: (Fr, S:) applied to one who has been at the point of destruction, and then escaped: (S:) or, accord. to AZ, it is thus; A^afolataniY jurayoEapa Al*~aqani , which may mean he made me to escape &c., or he escaped from me &c.; in the latter case, AfltnY being for A^afolata min~iY ; and [it is said that] jryEp is prefixed to Al*qn because the motion of the chin indicates the nearness of the departure of the soul: or the meaning of the words related by AZ may be, he made me, i. e. the remains of my soul, to escape; the last two words being a substitute for the pronoun affixed to the verb. (Sgh.) One says also, A^afolatanaYi jurayoEapa Alr~iyqi , meaning He outwent me, [or escaped me, ] and I swallowed my spittle in wrath, or rage, against him. (TA.) And maA mino juroEapK A^aHomadu EuqobaAnFA mino juroEapi gayoZK nakoZimuhaA (tropical:) [ There is nothing that is swallowed more praiseworthy in its result than what is swallowed of wrath, or rage, which we repress, or restrain ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A kinaAnap [or quiver ] (A, K) for arrows (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) of the kind called nu$~aAb (S, A, Msb, K) and for those that are called nabol also: (Ham p. 154:) but some make a distinction between jaEobapN and kinaAnapN : the former, they say, is for n$~Ab ; and the latter, for nbl : (Mz, MF:) accord. to IDrd, the knAnp is only for nbl , and is of leather: that which is of wood is called jafiyr : and that which is of two pieces [of wood] joined together is called qrn [i. e. qaranN ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) accord. to ISh, the jEbp is round and wide, with a cover on the top, over its mouth: the wafoDap is smaller, and its upper and lower parts are of equal size; whereas the jEbp is wide in its upper part, and contracted in its lower part; wide in its upper part that the feathers of the arrows [ having ample room ] may not become detached; for the arrows are put in the quiver with the points downwards: each of these two kinds is made of two corresponding pieces of wood: (TA:) the pl. is jiEaAbN (S, A, Msb, K) and jaEabaAtN . definition: One of the names of the months, (Msb, K,) applied to two of the Arabian months, together called jumaAdayaAni , (TA,) and distinguished by the appellations of jumaAdaY AlA^uwlaY and jumaAdaY...
sourceDefinition: One of the names of the months, (Msb, K,) applied to two of the Arabian months, together called jumaAdayaAni , (TA,) and distinguished by the appellations of jumaAdaY AlA^uwlaY and jumaAdaY AlA=xirapu [ the fifth and sixth months of the Arabian year ]: (S, K:) it is of the measure fuEaAlaY , from Aljamodu ; (S;) the two months to which it is applied being [said to be] so called because, when the months were named, these two fell in the season of the freezing of water: (ISd, L, Msb:) [but this derivation seems to have been invented when the two months thus named had fallen back, into, or beyond, the winter; for when they received this appellation, the former of them evidently commenced in March, and the latter ended in May; therefore I hold the opinion of M. Caussin de Perceval, that they were thus called because falling in a period when the earth had become dry and hard by reason of paucity of rain, from jamaAdN , an epithet applied to land upon which rain has not fallen, or from jumaAdaY , an epithet applied to an eye that sheds few tears; which opinion is confirmed by the obvious derivations of the names of other months, SafarN and rabiyEN and ramaDaAnu and $aw~aAlN :] afterwards, when the lunar months superseded the solar, the same names were retained: (Msb:) [see zamanN , and Alhijorapu :] jmAdY is determinate, (K,) being a proper name, (TA,) and of the fem. gender: (Msb, K:) if you find it masc., it is because it is made to accord to Al$~ahoru : all the other names of the months are masc.: (Fr, IAmb, Msb:) the pl. is jumaAdayaAtN , (Fr, L, K,) agreeably with analogy; and if the form jimaAdN [a mistranscription for jamaAy^idu , like HabaAy^iru , pl. of HubaAraY ,] were used, it would also be agreeable with analogy. (Fr, L.) The former of these two months is also called jumaAdaY xamosapK ; and the latter, jumaAdaY sit~apK ; (K;) which mean, respectively, Jumádà the fifth month and Jumádà the sixth month, from the commencement of the year. (TA.) Lebeed says, [describing a pair of wild asses,] Hat~aY A_i*aA salaxaA jumaAdaY sit~apF jazaA= faTaAla SiyaAmuhu waSiyaAmuhaA [ Until, when they both pass, and come to the end of, Jumádà, completing six months, they satisfy themselves with green pasture so as to be in no need of water, and his and her abstinence from water becomes of long continuance ]: thus cited by Bundár; st~p being in the accus. case as a denotative of state, and by jmAdY being meant jmAdY AlA=xrp : or, accord. to IAar, the poet said st~pK , meaning the six months of winter, which are the months of dew; and Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee says the like. (MF.) AHn says that the Arabs applied the name of jmAdY to The whole of the winter; [see above;] whether the winter were at the same time as the months so called or not: and Aboo-Sa'eed says the like. (L.) ― -b2- See also jaAmidN .

sourceDefinition: , applied to water, (Msb, K,) &c., (Msb,) [i. e.] anything fluid, or liquid, (K,) In a state of congelation, concretion, or solidity; freezing; as also ↓ jamodN ; contr. of *aAy^ibN : (Msb, K:) you say maA='N jamodN [as well as maA='N jaAmidN ]: (Msb:) or ↓ jamodN signifies what is congealed, or frozen, of water [&c.]; ice; (S, A;) contr. of *awobN : (S:) [see also jamadN :] it is originally an inf. n.: (S, Msb, K:) [or it is an epithet from jamuda , like DaxomN from Daxuma :] and ↓ jamadN is a pl. [or rather a quasi-pl. n.] of jaAmidN , (S, Msb, K,) like as xadamN is of xaAdimN : (S, Msb:) you say, qado kavura Aljamadu [ The frozen waters have become many ]. (S.) [Hence,] mux~apN jaAmidapN A hard piece of marrow. (L.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) Remaining fixed, stationary, or motionless. (Bd and Jel in xxvii. 90.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A thing that does not grow, or increase; [ incapable of growth, or increase; inanimate; ] as stone, in contradistinction to a tree [and an animal]. (Kull.) [See also jamaAdN .] You say, laka jaAmidu h`*aA AlmaAli wa*aAy^ibuhu (A, L, K *) (tropical:) To thee belongs, or shall belong, what consists of gold and silver [ or the like inanimate things ], of this property, and what consists of live stock, thereof: (L, K:) or what consists of stones, thereof, and what consists of trees, thereof: or what is solid, thereof, and what is fluid, or liquid, thereof. (L.) ― -b4- [Hence its application in lexicology and grammar to (assumed tropical:) A noun that is not an inf. n. nor derived from an inf. n.; a noun having the quality of a real substantive ( Aisomi EayonK ), opposed to that which has the quality of an ideal substantive ( Aisomu maEonFY ): and (assumed tropical:) a verb that has but one tense and no inf. n., as layosa and niEoma &c., opposed (as is said in the TA voce qado ) to mutaSar~ifN : it may be rendered (and so I have rendered it), in these cases, aplastic. ] ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Lifeless; dead. (Kull p. 147.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) Stupid, dull, wanting in intelligence; inert; not sharp, penetrating, vigorous, or effective, in the performing of affairs; or soft, without strength or sturdiness, and without endurance. sourceDefinition: : see jaAmidN , last sentence but one, in two places. ― -b2- The person who is entrusted with the management of affairs in a game of chance ( qimaAr [here meaning the game called Almayosir ]): (K:) [ i. q. DariybN :] or the person entrusted with the management of affairs among a people or party, (T, K, TA,) who does not take part in the game called Almayosir , except that he shuffles the arrows ( yaDoribu bihaA ) for the players, and has them placed in his hands, and is confided in with respect to them, and compels him who has incurred an obligation to fulfil it: (L, TA:) or one who takes no part in the game called Almayosir , (who is called baramN ,) but who sometimes shuffles, or deals forth, the arrows, ( yufiyDu bihaA ,) for the players; so in the following verse of Tarafeh: waA^aSofara maDobuwHK naZarotu Hawiyrahu EalaY Aln~aAri waA@sotawodaEotuhu kaf~a mujomidi [ And of many a yellow arrow, changed in colour by fire, I have awaited the sound over the fire, and I have deposited it in the hand of one taking no part in the game but only shuffling, or dealing forth, the arrows for the players ]; meaning, I have awaited its sound, which was like an answer proceeding from it, when I straightened it and marked it, over the fire: (S:) [or, accord. to the EM (p. 105), where we find HiwaArahu in the place of Hawiyrahu , the meaning is, and of many a yellow arrow, &c., I have awaited the returning and gaining, while we were assembled at the fire, &c.:] or mjmd here means a man taking with both his hands so as not to let anything go forth from them: (AA, TA:) or, accord. to As, it here means a man entering upon Jumádà, which was in that [the poet's] time a month of cold: (S, K: *) or one whose arrow does not gain anything in the game called Almayosir : (L:) or a person in whom one confides, and who is tenacious of that which is in his hand or possession, and not to be deceived. (A 'Obeyd, TA.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. HabaTN , (Az, S, K, &c.,) He (a beast, Az, S, or a camel, ISd, K) ate much, (S,) or had pain in his belly from pasture which he found unwholesome, or from eating much of herbage,...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. HabaTN , (Az, S, K, &c.,) He (a beast, Az, S, or a camel, ISd, K) ate much, (S,) or had pain in his belly from pasture which he found unwholesome, or from eating much of herbage, (ISd, K,) so that he became swollen, or inflated, thereby (S, ISd, K) in his belly, (S,) and there would not come forth from him (S, ISd, K) what was in it, (S,) or anything; (ISd, K;) he did not void either thin dung or urine, his belly being bound: (Az:) or he (a sheep, or goat, ISk, S) became swollen, or inflated, in his belly, in consequence of eating [ the herb called ] *uraq , (ISk, S, K, *) which is the Hanoda quwq [i. e. the herb lotus, melilot, or bird's-foot-trefoil ]: (ISk, S:) or he (a beast) lighted upon good pasturage, and ate immoderately, so that he became swollen, or inflated, and died: (Z, IAth:) or, in speaking of a horse, you do not say, HabiTa Alfarasu , but HabiTa quSayoraY Alfarasi , or xaASiratuhu , or mawoqifuhu , because it means that the horse's belly became swollen, or inflated: (ISd, Z, L:) you say also, HabiTa baTonuhu his belly became swollen, or inflated, so that he died: (Az, TA:) or his (a man's) belly became swollen, or inflated, by food &c.: (Mbr, TA in art. HbTA^ :) and HabiTa is also said of the skin, meaning it became swollen, or inflated. (TA.) [See also Q. Q. 3; and see HabaTN below.] ― -b2- Hence, app., i. e. from HabiTa said of the belly, (Az, TA,) or it is from this verb said of a beast, (Z, IAth, TA,) HabiTa Eamaluhu , (Az, S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. ; (Az, Msb, K;) and HabaTa , aor. ; (AZ, Az, Msb, K;) the latter, says Az, heard by AZ from an Arab of the desert, but I have not heard it on any other authority; (TA;) inf. n. HaboTN , (Az, S, K, [but in the Msb it seems to be indicated that it is HabaTN ,]) with the b quiescent, (Az, S,) thus differing from the inf. n. of HabiTa said of the belly, (Az, TA,) and HubuwTN , (Az, S, Msb, K,) which latter, accord. to AZ, is the inf. n. of HabaTa like Daraba ; (T, TA;) (tropical:) His work, or deed, became null, or void, or of no account; it went for nothing; it perished; (Az, Msb, TA;) for like as he of whom one says HabiTa baTonuhu perishes, so does the work, or deed, of the hypocrite: (Az, TA:) or it became ineffective of reward; its reward became annulled. (S, K.) And hence also, (Z, TA,) HabiTa damuhu , aor. , (Z, Msb, K, TA,) but not HabaTa also, as is implied in the K, (TA,) and in this case the inf. n. is HabaTN , (Msb, * TA,) with the b movent, (TA,) (tropical:) His blood (the blood of one slain, K) went for nothing; unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulct. (Msb, K, TA.) ― -b3- HabiTa said of the water of a well, i. q. A^aHobaTa , q. v. (TA.) ― -b4- Said of a wound, (S, Ibn-' Abbád, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. HabaTN , with fet-h to the b , (S, K,) It had scars remaining after having healed: (Ibn-' Abbád, K: *) or it broke open again; or became recrudescent; syn. Eariba [which has the signification given above on the authority of Ibn-' Abbád as well as what follows it] and nukisa . (S.) [See also HabaTN below.]

definition: [inf. n. of HabiTa , q. v.:] A beast's having the belly swollen, or inflated, so that what is in it does not come forth, in consequence of eating much: (S:) or pain in the belly, of a camel, from...
sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of HabiTa , q. v.:] A beast's having the belly swollen, or inflated, so that what is in it does not come forth, in consequence of eating much: (S:) or pain in the belly, of a camel, from pasture which he finds unwholesome, or from herbage of which he has eaten much, so that he becomes swollen, or inflated, therefrom, (ISd, K,) in his belly, (TA,) and nothing comes forth from him: (ISd, K:) or a swelling, or inflation, of the belly, (K,) or a beast's having the belly swollen, or inflated, (ISk, S,) from eating [ the herb called ] *uraq : (ISk, S, K:) [see 1:] and a swelling in the udder or other thing: (K:) or, accord. to the M, the slightest swelling in the udder: or, as some say, swelling, or inflation, wherever it be, from disease or other cause. (TA.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a mim~aA yunobitu Alr~abiyEu mDA yaqotulu HabaTFA A^awo yulim~u [ Verily, of what the ( rain, or season, called ) rbyE causes to grow, is what kills by inflation of the belly, or nearly does so ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- The scars, or marks, of a wound, or of whips, upon the body, after healing: or the swollen scars, or marks, ( of whips, TA,) not lacerated: when mangled and bleeding, they are termed Euluwb [pl. of Ealob ]: (K:) the excrescent flesh upon the scars of wounds. (Sgh.)
