Had~q , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He, or it, prevented, hindered, impeded, withheld, restrained, debarred, inhibited, forbade, prohibited, or interdicted : (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, TA:) this is the primary signification: (Mgh:) and he repelled, turned away, or averted, (L, K, TA,) evil [or the like], and also a person from a thing, good or evil. (L.) You say, Had~a Alr~ajula Eani AlA^amori He prevented, or hindered, and withheld, or restrained, the man from the thing, or affair. (L.) And Hadadotu fulAnFA Eani Al$~ar~i I prevented, or hindered, such a one from [ falling into ], or preserved him from, evil. (L.) And qado Had~a A@ll~`hu *`lika Ean~aA [ God hath forbidden us that ]. (S.) And Aall~`hum~a A@Hoduwdohu (T, A, L) O God, prevent him from hitting the mark : said with reference to a man shooting, or casting a missile weapon, or the like. (T, L.) And Hud~a He (a man) was prevented, or withheld, from obtaining good fortune, success, or what he desired or sought. (L.) And Had~a A@ll~`hu Ean~aA $ar~a fulaAnK May God repel, or avert, from us, the evil, or mischief, of such a one. (L.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Had~ahu , (S, L, Msb,) aor. , (L,) inf. n. Had~N , (L, Msb, K,) He inflicted upon him the castigation, or punishment, termed Had~N ; (S, L;) he inflicted upon him (namely, a criminal or an offender [against the law],) a castigation, or punishment, that should prevent him from returning to his crime or offence, and that should prevent others from committing such a crime or such an offence : (K, * TA:) he inflicted upon him a flogging. (Msb.) ― -b3- Had~a $ayoy^FA mino gayorihi , aor. , (L,) inf. n. Had~N ; (L, K;) and ↓ Hd~dhu ; (L;) He distinguished, or separated by some mark or note, or marks or notes, a thing from another thing. (L, K. *) And Had~a Ald~aAra , aor. and inf. n. as above; (S, Msb;) and ↓ H~ddhA , inf. n. taHodiydN ; (S;) He distinguished the house from the parts adjoining it, by mentioning [or defining ] its limits. Msb.) -A2- [And hence, Had~a in logic, inf. n. Had~N , (assumed tropical:) He defined a word; as also ↓ Hd~d , inf. n. taHodiydN .] ― -b2- Had~a , (L, Msb, K,) aor. , (L, Msb,) inf. n. Had~N ; (L;) and ↓ Hd~d , (S, L, Msb, K,) [which is more common,] inf. n. taHodiydN ; (S;) and ↓ AHd~ , (S, L, K,) which is the form preferred by Lh, (L,) inf. n. A_iHodaAdN ; (S;) and ↓ AstHd~ ; (As, S, L;) He edged, or sharpened, a knife, (L, K,) a blade, (S,) a sword, (L, Msb,) or anything blunt, (L,) [and pointed, or made sharp-pointed, an arrow-head or the like,] with a stone or file. (L, K.) ― -b3- [And hence,] Had~a baSarahu A_ilayohi , aor. ; (Lh, L;) and ↓ AHd~hu , (L,) or AHd~ Aln~aZara Alyh ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ Hd~dhu ; (K in art. ltA^ , &c.;) (tropical:) He looked sharply at him, or it; (L;) or intently, or attentively. (Msb.) -A3- Had~ato , (S, Mgh, L, K,) or Had~ato EalaY zawojihaA , (Msb,) aor. and , inf. n. HidaAdN (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K) and Had~N ; (L, K;) and ↓ AHd~t , (As, S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iHodaAdN ; (Mgh, Msb;) the former the more common in the language of the Arabs, but the latter preferred by the early grammarians, (Fr, TA,) and the only form known to As, (S,) who rejected the former; (Msb;) She (a woman) abstained from the wearing of ornaments, (A 'Obeyd, S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) and the use of perfumes, (L,) and dye for the hands &c., (S, Mgh,) because forbidden such things, or because she forbade herself, (Mgh,) and put on the garments of mourning, (A,) after the death of her husband, (S, Mgh,) or on account of the death of her husband, (A 'Obeyd, A, Msb,) for the period called AlEid~ap : (K:) or she mourned for her husband, and put on the garments of mourning, and abstained from the wearing of ornaments, and the use dye for the hands &c. (L.) The epithets applied to a woman in this case are ↓ HaAd~N (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ muHid~N (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K) and ↓ muHid~apN also, but the first [always] without p , (Msb,) or both more chaste without p . (TA.) -A4- Had~a , aor. , inf. n. Hid~apN ; (S, L, Msb, K;) and ↓ AHtd~ ; (L, K;) [and app. ↓ AnHd~ , q. v.;] It (a sword, S Msb, and a knife, L, K, [or the like,] and a canine tooth, L) was, or became, [ edged, or] sharp, or pointed. (S, L, Msb, K.) ― -b2- [And hence,] Had~a , aor. , inf. n. Hid~apN , (tropical:) He was, or became, sharp [or effective ] in respect of eloquence, and of intellect, or understanding, and of anger. (L.) And Had~a Ealayohi , aor. , (S, L, K,) inf. n. Hid~apN and Had~N , (S, L,) (tropical:) He became excited against him by sharpness, or hastiness, of temper; by irascibility, passionateness, or angriness; (Ks, S, L, K;) as also Ealayohi ↓ AHtd~ : (TA:) and Had~a Ealayohi , aor. as above, inf. n. HadadN ; (L, K;) and ↓ Hd~d , (accord. to some copies of the K,) and ↓ AHtd~ , (S, [in which it is not followed by Elyh ,] A, L, K,) and ↓ AstHd~ ; (L, K;) (tropical:) he was angry with him; (S, * A, L, K;) but Az remarks upon the last of these verbs as not heard from the Arabs of classical times in this sense: (L:) and bihimo ↓ tHd~d (tropical:) he became exasperated by them: syn. tHr~$ . (AZ, L.)

definition: Prevention, hinderance, an impediment, a withholding, restraint, a debarring, inhibition, forbiddance, prohibition, or interdiction;
sourceDefinition: Prevention, hinderance, an impediment, a withholding, restraint, a debarring, inhibition, forbiddance, prohibition, or interdiction; (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ HadadN : (S, L, K:) and, both words, a repelling, or an averting. (K. [See 1.]) A poet says, (S,) namely, Zeyd Ibn-' Amr Ibn-Nufeyl, (TA,) laA taEobudan~a A_il`hFA gayora xaAliqikumo ↓ waA_ino duEiytumo faquwluwA duwnahu Hadadu [ Ye shall by no means worship any deity except your Creator; and if ye be invited to do so, say ye, There is an impediment in the way of it, or a prohibition against it ]. (S, TA.) And one says, ↓ duwna maA saA^alota Eanohu HadadN (A, * L) There is an impediment, or a prohibition, in the way of that respecting which thou hast asked. (L.) And Eanohu ↓ laAHadada There is nothing to prevent, or hinder, one from it. (L. [But this admits of another meaning, as will be seen, under the word HadadN , below.]) ― -b2- [Hence,] A restrictive ordinance, or statute, of God, respecting things lawful and things unlawful: pl. HuduwdN . (L.) The Huduwd of God are of two kinds: first, those ordinances prescribed to men (T, Mgh, L) respecting eatables and drinkables and marriages &c.; what are lawful thereof and what are unlawful: (T, L:) the second kind, castigations, or punishments, prescribed, or appointed, to be inflicted upon him who does that which he has been forbidden to do; (T, Mgh, L;) as the Hd~ of the thief, which is the cutting off of his right hand for stealing a thing of the value of a quarter of a deenár or more; and that of the fornicator or fornicatress, which is flogging with a hundred stripes and banishment for a year; and that of the adulterer or adulteress, which is stoning; and that of the person who [falsely] charges an honest or a married woman with adultery, which is flogging with eighty stripes [as is also that of the person who has committed the crime of drunkenness]: (T, L:) the first kind are called Hdwd because they denote limits which God has forbidden to transgress: the second, because they prevent one's committing again those acts for which they are appointed as punishments; (T, Mgh, L;) or because the limits thereof are determined: (Mgh:) the latter kind of Hd~ is also explained as being that [ castigation, or punishment, ] which prevents the criminal from returning to his crime, and prevents others from committing his crime. (L, K. *) lawo raA^ayotahu EalaY Had~K , in a saying of ' Omar, means Hadst thou seen him engaged in an affair requiring the infliction of the Hd~ . (Mgh.) ― -b3- A bar, an obstruction, a partition, or a separation, (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, * K,) between two things, (S, A, L, K,) or between two places, (Mgh,) [or between two persons, ] to prevent their commixture, or confusion, or the encroachment of one upon the other: (L:) an inf. n. used as a subst.: (Mgh:) pl. HuduwdN . (L.) ― -b4- A limit, or boundary, of a land or territory: pl. as above. (L.) [Hence, jaAwaza AlHad~a (assumed tropical:) He, or it, exceeded the proper, due, or common, limit; was excessive, immoderate, beyond measure, enormous, inordinate, or exorbitant. ] ― -b5- [And hence, in logic, (assumed tropical:) A definition. ] It is applied by the learned to the Haqiyqap of a thing, [or that by being which a thing is what it is, ] because it is [a term] collective and restrictive. (Mgh.) ― -b6- The end, extremity, or utmost point, of a thing: (S, L, K:) pl. as above. (L.) ― -b7- [(assumed tropical:) The point, or verge, of an event.] The saying musolimapN mawoquwfapN EalaY Had~i maHoramK means (assumed tropical:) A Muslimeh brought to the point, or verge, of being subjected to an infidel's lying with her: and in like manner, musolimN mawoquwfN EalaY Had~i kuforK (assumed tropical:) A Muslim brought, by beating or slaughter, to [ the point, or verge, of ] denying God. (Mgh.) ― -b8- The edge, or extremity of the edge, (S, L,) and point, (L,) of anything, (S, L,) as of a sword, a knife, a spear-head, and an arrow: (L:) the part of a sword [&c.] with which one cuts: (MF:) pl. as above. (L.) ― -b9- See also Hid~apN , in four places. ― -b10- [And hence, app.,] Arms, or weapons; as in the phrase *awuw Had~K [ Possessors of arms or weapons: or this may mean (tropical:) persons endowed with valour ]. (Ham p. 143.) ― -b11- A side, region, quarter, or tract. (L.) ― -b12- (assumed tropical:) Station, standing, rank, condition, or the like; syn. marotabapN . (KL.) ― -b13- [(assumed tropical:) A case: as when a noun is said to be fiY Had~i Alr~afoEi in the nominative case. ― -b14- And (assumed tropical:) A class, or category: as when a verb is said to be mino Had~i Daraba of the class, or category, of Daraba .] ― -b15- [(tropical:) A quarter of the year.] You say, A^aqaAma Had~a Alr~abiyEi (tropical:) He remained, stayed, or abode, during the quarter of the rbyE . (A.) -A2- See also maHoduwdN .

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ muHaAd~N . (A.) You say, fulaAnN Hadiydu fulaAnK Such a one is the close, or next, neighbour of such a one; meaning that the house of the former is next by the side of that of the latter; (A, * L;) or that the land of the former is adjacent to that of the latter. (S, L.) And huwa HadydiY fiY Ald~aAri , i. e. ↓ muHaAd~iY [ He is my next neighbour in respect of house ]. (A.) And daAriY Hadiydapu daArihi , and ↓ muHaAd~atuhaA (L, K,) or lidaArihi ↓ muHAd~apN , (A,) My house is close, or next, or adjoining, to his house; meaning that the limit of the former is like that of the latter. (L, K. *) -A2- Also, (S, L, Msb, K,) used as masc. and fem. without p , and also as fem. with p , (L,) and ↓ HaAd~N , (S, L, Msb,) but this is disapproved by IKh, (TA,) though allowed by some as agreeable with analogy, (MF,) and ↓ HudaAdN , (As, L, K,) and ↓ Hud~aAdN , (AA, S, L, K,) [ Edged, or sharpened; or] sharp; applied to a sword, (S, Msb,) a knife, (L, Msb, K,) [and the like: and pointed, or sharp-pointed: ] pl. [of the first] HidaAdN , (S, L, K,) masc. and fem.; (L;) and HadiydaAtN and HadaAy^idu , (L, K,) fem. (L.) And naAbN HadiydN and HadiydapN A sharp canine tooth: (L, K:) HudaAdN thus applied has not been heard. (L.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rajulN HadiydN (tropical:) A man who is sharp [or effective ] in respect of eloquence, and of intellect or understanding, and (as also ↓ muHotad~N , S) of anger: pl. A^aHid~aA=hu and A^aHid~apN and HidaAdN . (L, K.) And A^alosinapN HidaAdN (assumed tropical:) Sharp tongues. (S.) And rajulN Hadiydu Aln~aAZiri (tropical:) [ A man who looks sharply, or boldly; ] a man not suspected of evil, so that he should cast down his eyes. (L.) fabaSaruka Alyawoma HadiydN [in the Kur 1. 21] means (assumed tropical:) And thy sight, or intellect, to-day, is ] sharp, or piercing; so that thou perceivest therewith what thou didst not know, or what thou deemedst improbable, in thy life on earth: (Jel:) or thy judgment, to-day, is penetrating. (L.) [Hence also,] raAy^iHapN HadiydapN (L) and ↓ HaAd~apN (L, K) (tropical:) A sharp, or pungent, odour. (L, K.) And naAqapN Hadiydapu Aljir~api (tropical:) A she-camel whose cud has a pungent odour; (K, TA;) which is a quality approved. (TA.) -A3- HadiydN also signifies [ Iron; ] a certain substance, (L,) well known; (S, L, K;) so called because of its resistance: (S, L:) ↓ HadiydapN is a more particular term, (S,) signifying a piece thereof; (L;) [and an instrument, or implement, thereof: ] pl. HadaAy^idu (S, L, K) and HadaAy^idaAtN ; (S L;) the latter (which is erroneously written in the K HadiydaAtN , TA) is a pl. pl., (L,) sometimes occurring in poetry. (S.) It is said in a prov., A_in~a AlHadiyda biAlHadiydi yufolaHu Verily iron with iron is cloven, or cut. (S and K in art. flH .) And in another, taDoribu fiY HadiydK baAridK [ Thou beatest upon cold iron ]: applied in relation to him who hopes for that of which the attainment is remote, or improbable; and to him in whom is nothing to be hoped for. (Har p. 633.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Like iron in hardness: applied in this sense to solid hoofs. (Mgh.)

definition: A door-keeper: (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K:) so called because he prevents men from entering.
sourceDefinition: A door-keeper: (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K:) so called because he prevents men from entering. (Mgh, L.) ― -b2- A keeper of a prison: (S, Mgh, K:) because he prevents persons from going out, or because he works the iron of the shackles. (S. [See what follows.]) ― -b3- The person who inflicts the punishment termed Had~N : so in the saying, A^ujorapN AlHad~aAdi EalaY Als~aAriqi [ The pay of the inflicter of the Hd~ is to be imposed upon the thief ]; or, as some say, the meaning here is, the keeper of the prison, because, in general, he has the charge of the amputation; but the former meaning is the more probable, and more obvious. (Mgh.) ― -b4- A seller of wine; a vintner: because he withholds his wine until he obtains for it a price that contents him: so in the following verse of ElAashà: faqumonaA walam~aA yaSiHo diykunaA A_ilaY jawonapK Einoda Had~aAdihaA [ And we arose, when our cock had not yet crowed, to a wine-jar smeared with pitch, in the possession of its seller ]. (S, L.) ― -b5- A blacksmith; a worker in iron. (Mgh, L, K.) A maker of coats of mail. (TA.)

definition: [for AHtsb A^ajorFA He reckoned upon a reward: or] he sought a reward [from God in the world to come].
sourceDefinition: [for AHtsb A^ajorFA He reckoned upon a reward: or] he sought a reward [from God in the world to come]. (TA.) wayarozuquhu mino Hayovu laA yaHotasibu , in the Kur lxv. 2, means [ And He will supply him with the means of subsistence ] whence he does not reckon, or expect; whence does not occur to his mind. (Bd, Jel.) And mano SaAma ramaDAna A_iymaAnFA waA@HotisaAbFA , in a trad., Whoso fasteth during Ramadán, believing in God and his Apostle, and [ reckoning upon a reward, or] seeking a reward from God. (Mgh, * TA.) You say also, AHtsb bika*aA A^ajorFA Einoda A@ll~`hi (S, K) He reckoned upon obtaining, [or he sought, ] by such a thing, or such an action, a reward from God: (PS:) or he prepared, or provided, such a thing, seeking thereby a reward from God. (K.) And AHtsb Einoda A@ll~`hi xayorFA He prepared, or provided, in store for himself, good, [i. e. a reward, ] with God. (A, Mgh.) And AHtsb AlA^ajora EalaY A@ll~`hi He laid up for himself, in store, the reward, with God, not hoping for the reward of the present life; AiHotisaAbu AlA^ajori relating only to an action done for the sake of God. (Msb.) [Hence,] AHtsb waladahu , (A, Mgh,) or A@bonahu , (Msb,) or A@bonFA , or bnotFA , (S, K, *) is said when one has lost by death an adult child or son or daughter; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) meaning He prepared, or provided, in store for himself, a reward, by his patience on the occasion of his being afflicted and tried by the death of his adult child: (Mgh, * TA:) when a man has lost by death a child not arrived at the age of puberty, you say of him, AifotaraTahu . (S, A, Msb, K.) [Hence also,] AHtsb Eamalahu [ He reckoned upon, or prepared for himself, a reward by his deed: or] he did his deed seeking a reward from God in the world to come. (L, TA.) ― -b2- AiHotasabotu baAl$~aYo'i I included the thing in a numbering, or reckoning; or made account of it; accounted it a matter of importance. (Msb.) And fulaAnN laA yuHotasabu [for lA yHtsb bahi ] Such a one is made no account of; is not esteemed, or regarded, as of any account, or importance. (A, TA.) ― -b3- AiHotasabotu Einodahu means Aikotafayotu [ I was, or became, sufficed, or contented, thereat, or with him, or at his abode ]. (A, TA.) [And IbrD thinks that the verb has the same signification in the phrase AiHotasabotu Ealayohi biAlmaAli , quoted in the TA from the A; holding Elyh to be here used in the sense of Eanohu ; so that the meaning is I was, or became, sufficed, so as to have no need of him, or it, by the property: but I doubt whether this phrase be correctly transcribed.] ― -b4- AHtsb also signifies AinotahaY [ He abstained, or desisted; app. as one sufficed, or contented]. (K.) ― -b5- And AHtsb Ealayohi ka*aA He disapproved and disallowed his doing, or having done, such a thing; (S, K; *) namely, a foul deed: (TA:) whence the appellation ↓ muHotasibN . (K.) And accord. to some, AHtsb A@ll~`ha Ealayohi means He said, May God take, or execute, vengeance upon him; or punish him; for his evil deeds. (Har p. 371. [See HasiybN .]) [In the present day, AHtsb Ealayohi is used as meaning He prayed for aid against him by saying, HasobunaA A@ll~`hu God is, or will be, sufficient for us. ] ― -b6- You say also, AHtsb fulaAnFA , (K,) or AHtsb maA Einodahu , (A,) meaning (tropical:) He endeavoured to learn what such a one had [ in his mind, or in his possession ]. (A, K, * TA.) ― -b7- See also 4.

(Bd, Jel.) And mano SaAma ramaDAna A_iymaAnFA waA@HotisaAbFA , in a trad., Whoso fasteth during Ramadán, believing in God and his Apostle, and [ reckoning upon a reward, or] seeking a reward fro...

AiHotasabotu baAl$~aYo'i I included the thing in a numbering, or reckoning; or made account of it; accounted it a matter of importance. (Msb.) And fulaAnN laA yuHotasabu [for lA yHtsb bahi ] Such a one is made no account of; is not esteemed, or regarded, as of any account, or importance. (A, TA.)

AiHotasabotu Einodahu means Aikotafayotu [ I was, or became, sufficed, or contented, thereat, or with him, or at his abode ]. (A, TA.) [And IbrD thinks that the verb has the same signification in the phrase AiHotasabotu Ealayohi biAlmaAli , quoted in the TA from the A; holding Elyh to be here used in the sense of Eanohu ; so that the meaning is I was, or became, sufficed, so as to have no need of him, or it, by the property: but I doubt whether this phrase be correctly transcribed.]
AHtsb also signifies AinotahaY [ He abstained, or desisted; app. as one sufficed, or contented]. (K.)

And AHtsb Ealayohi ka*aA He disapproved and disallowed his doing, or having done, such a thing; (S, K; *) namely, a foul deed: (TA:) whence the appellation ↓ muHotasibN . (K.) And accord. to some, AHtsb A@ll~`ha Ealayohi means He said, May God take, or execute, vengeance upon him; or punish him; for his evil deeds. (Har p. 371. [See HasiybN .]) [In the present day, AHtsb Ealayohi is used as meaning He prayed for aid against him by saying, HasobunaA A@ll~`hu God is, or will be, sufficient for us....

sourceDefinition: Sufficiency. (K voce hasobN .) ― -b2- Hasobu is a [prefixed] noun (S) [syn. with kafoYu , as is implied in the K voce qaTo ; or] syn. with kaAfiY ; (Msb;) or [virtually] meaning kafaY [as a pret. in the sense of an emphatic aor.]; (S, K;) or yakofiY : (TA:) Sb says that it is used to denote the being sufficed, or content. (TA.) You say, Hasobuka dirohamN [and biHasobika dirohamN , in which latter the b is redundant; meaning Thy sufficiency, or a thing sufficing thee, is a dirhem; a phrase which may be used in two ways; as predicating of what is sufficient, that it is a dirhem; and as predicating of a dirhem, that it is sufficient; in which latter case, bHsbk is an enunciative put before its inchoative, (as also Hasobuka ,) so that the meaning is, a dirhem is a thing sufficing thee, i. e. a dirhem is sufficient for thee; as is shown in a marginal note in my copy of the Mughnee, in art. bi ; or, accord. to the S and K, a dirhem suffices thee: accord. to Bd (iii. 167), bHsbk means muHosibuka , and kaAfiyka , from A^aHosabahu meaning kafaAhu ; and is shown to have this meaning by its not importing a determinate signification in consequence of its being a prefixed noun with its complement in the saying, h`*aA rajulN Hasobuka This is a man sufficing thee ]. (S, Msb, K.) You say also, Hasobuka *`lika That is, or will be, [or let that be, ] sufficient for thee. (TA.) And Hasobuka A@ll~`hu , in the Kur viii. 65, God is, or will be, sufficient for thee. (Fr, TA. See also Hasiybuka A@ll~`hu .) And Hasobuka biSadiyqinaA [ A person sufficing thee is our friend ]; in which the b is added to denote emphatic praise. (Fr, TA in art. bi .) In the saying, h`*aA rajulN Hasobuka mino rajulK This is a man sufficing thee as a man, i. e. supplying to thee the place of any other [by his excellent qualities], (S, K,) and mararotu birajulK Hasobika mino rajulK I passed by a man sufficing thee as a man, (TA,) Hsbk is an expression of praise, referring to the indeterminate noun [ rjl ]; because, in its case, [what is originally (see below)] an inf. n. ( fiEolN [under which term lexicologists, but not grammarians, include the maSodar ]) is rendered, in grammatical analysis, by another word, [i. e., by an act. part. n.,] as though one said muHosibN laka , or kaAfK laka . (S. [Thus Hsbk in these two instances is a Sifap , i. e. an epithetic phrase; and mn rjl is a tamoyiyz , i. e. a specificative phrase.]) When the noun to which Hsbk refers is determinate, you put Hsb in the accus. case, as a HAl , i. e. a denotative of state; as in the saying, h`*aA Eabodu A@ll~`hi Hasobaka mino rajulK This is 'Abd-Allah; being one sufficing thee as a man. (S. [Here mn rjl is, as before, a specificative phrase.]) [See also 4, the corresponding verb.]) Hsb , in this manner, is used alike as sing. and dual and pl.; (S, K;) being [originally] an inf. n. (S.) It is also used alone, [as a prefixed noun of which the complement is understood,] as in the phrase zayodN Hasobu , without tenween, for HasobiY or Hasobuka [&c., meaning Zeyd is sufficient for me or for thee &c.]; like as one says, jaA='aniY zayodN layosa gayoru , for layosa gayoruhu EinodiY . (S. [That is, Hasobu , when thus used, is subject to the same rules as gayoru and qabolu , and baEodu &c. when so used.]) ― -b3- See also HasabN , in three places. -A2- Also, (TA,) and ↓ HisobapN , (K,) Burial of the dead: (TA:) or burial of the dead in stones [app. meaning in a grave cased with stones ]: or burial of the dead wrapped in grave-clothes: like taHosiybN . (K. [See 2.])

definition: i. q. ↓ maHosuwbN ; (S, K;) of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like nafaDN in the sense of manofuwDN ; (S;) Numbered, counted, reckoned, calculated, or computed. (S, K.) ―...
sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ maHosuwbN ; (S, K;) of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like nafaDN in the sense of manofuwDN ; (S;) Numbered, counted, reckoned, calculated, or computed. (S, K.) ― -b2- A number counted. (L.) ― -b3- Amount, quantity, or value. (L.) Sometimes, (S, L, K,) by poetic license, (S,) and in prose, (L,) ↓ HasobN . (S, L, K.) You say, AlA^ajoru biHasabi maA Eamilota , and ↓ biHasobi , The recompense is, or shall be, according to the amount, or quantity, or value, of thy work. (L.) And yujozaY Almaro'u EalaY Hasabi Eamalihi The man is, or shall be, paid according to the amount, or quantity, of his work. (Msb.) And EalaY Hasabi maA A^asodayota A_ilaY~a $ukoriY laka [and ↓ HasobamaA (for EalaY Hasabi maA )] According to the amount, or value, of the benefit, or benefits, that thou hast conferred upon me are my thanks to thee. (L.) And liyakuno Eamaluka biHasabi *`lika Let thy deed, or work, be correspondent to the quantity, or number, of that: or adequate, or equivalent, to that. (S.) And h`*aA biHasabi *aA This is equal in number or quantity, or is equivalent, to that. (K.) And maA A^adoriY maA Hasabu Hadiyvika , i. e. mA qadoruhu [app. I know not what is the value of thy story ]. (Ks, S.) And A^aHosanotu A_ilayohi Hasaba AlT~aAqapi and EalaY Hasabi AlT~aAqapi I benefited him according to the measure of ability. (Mgh.) ― -b4- Also [ Grounds of pretension to respect or honour, consisting in any qualities (either of oneself or of one's ancestors) which are enumerated, or recounted, as causes of glorying: and hence signifying nobility; rank or quality; honourableness, or estimableness, from whatever source derived: ] originally, (MF,) what one enumerates, or recounts, of the deeds, or qualities, in which his ancestors have gloried: (S, A, Mgh, * K, MF:) secondly, what one enumerates, or recounts, of his own deeds, or qualities, in which he glories: thirdly, what one enumerates, or recounts, of any deeds, or qualities, that are causes of his glorying, of whatever kind they be: (MF:) or the memorable deeds, or qualities, of one's ancestors; and one's own deeds, or qualities, in which he glories; because they were enumerated, or recounted, by the Arabs in contending, or disputing, for glory; (T, Msb, * TA;) the latter consisting in such qualities as courage, and good disposition, and liberality: (Msb:) or what are enumerated, or recounted, of generous actions, or qualities: (Msb:) or good actions, or conduct, of oneself, and of one's ancestors: (Sh, Mgh:) or generosity, or nobility, of actions or conduct: (IAar, K:) or righteous, virtuous, or good, actions or conduct: (K:) or good disposition: (TA:) or religion; (S, Msb, K;) piety; because true nobility consists in religion or piety: (MF:) or wealth; (S, K;) because it serves in lieu of true nobility: (TA:) in this sense, and in the sense next preceding, it has no corresponding verb: (TA:) or state, or condition; [i. e. good state or condition; ] syn. baAlN [i. q. HaAlN ]: (K:) or intellect, or understanding: (MF:) and a man's relations, consisting of his children and others: pl. A^aHosaAbN . (Az, Mgh.) Accord. to ISk, (S, Msb,) HasabN and karamN may pertain to him who has not noble ancestors; but not $arafN nor majodN . (S, Msb, * K.) HasabN is also used elliptically, (Mgh, TA,) [in the sense of HasiybN , q. v.,] for *uw HasabK , (TA,) and for *awuw HasabK . (Mgh.) ― -b5- Ai$otaraY biAlHasabi He bought a thing in an honourable manner with respect to himself and the seller: Hsb , here, is said to be from Has~abahu “ he honoured him; ” or from HusobaAnapN “ a small pillow ” [because him for whom you put a pillow you honour: see 2]. (TA.)

definition: A reckoner, or taker of accounts: [see also HaAsibN :] or a sufficer, or giver of what is sufficient;
sourceDefinition: A reckoner, or taker of accounts: [see also HaAsibN :] or a sufficer, or giver of what is sufficient; (K, TA;) from A^aHosaba , of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mufoEilN . (TA.) It has the former of these significations, or the latter, in the phrase, kafaY biA@ll~`hi HasiybFA [ God is sufficient as a reckoner, or as a giver of what sufficeth ], (Fr, K, TA,) in the Kur [iv. 7, and xxxiii. 39]: (TA:) and so in the Kur iv. 88. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Hasiybuka A@ll~`hu , (S, K,) in the L A@ll~`hu ↓ Hasobuka , (TA,) [both of which phrases are used in the present day in the sense here following,] May God take, or execute, vengeance upon thee; or punish thee: (S, L, K:) meaning an imprecation though literally predicatory. (IAmb, Har p. 371.) [See also HusobaAnuka EalaY A@ll~`hi , voce Hasaba .] -A2- Also Characterized, or distinguished, by what is termed, HasabN as explained above [i. e. grounds of pretension to respect or honour; &c.]: (S, K:) generous, liberal, honourable, or noble: (Msb:) bountiful, or munificent: and having a numerous household: (Az, Mgh:) pl. HusabaA='u . (A, K.)

definition: , (inf. n. A_iHoSaA='N , TA,) He numbered, counted, calculated, reckoned, or computed, it: (S, Msb, K:) or he reached the last number thereof: (Ham p. 297:) or he collected it into an aggregate by...
sourceDefinition: , (inf. n. A_iHoSaA='N , TA,) He numbered, counted, calculated, reckoned, or computed, it: (S, Msb, K:) or he reached the last number thereof: (Ham p. 297:) or he collected it into an aggregate by numbering: from HaSFY ; because they used pebbles in numbering like as we use the fingers; (Er-Rághib;) or because they used to divide a thing upon the pebbles, and when nothing remained they said, A^aHoSayonaA , i. e. We have come to the pebbles; or because they used to reckon the spoils, and to divide among themselves, and then to take the pebbles, and put marks upon them, and when they ended the reckoning, and came to the marks, they said, A^aHoSayonaA : (Ham ubi suprà:) or he retained it in his memory: (K, * TA:) or he understood it. sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. HaforN , (Mgh, Msb,) He dug, excavated, or hollowed out, the ground, or earth; (KL, PS, &c.;) he cleared out a thing, (K,) as one does the ground; (S, Msb, K;) and a well; (the Lexicons passim;) and a river; (A, Mgh;) with a miHofaAr ; (A;) or with an iron implement; (K;) and ↓ AHtfr signifies the same. (S, A, K.) And Hafara Ealayohi , and Hafarahu , and ↓ AHtfrhu , He dug for him, (namely, a lizard of the kind called Dab~ , or a jerboa,) to fetch him forth. (A, TA.) ― -b2- [ He burrowed. ] ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) It (a torrent) furrowed a valley. (Msb.) [See also 5.] ― -b4- (tropical:) Inivit feminam: (IAar, Msb, K:) the action being likened to that of a man digging a river. (IAar.) ― -b5- .) ― -b6- h`*aA gayovN laA yaHofiruhu A^aHadN (tropical:) This is a rain of which no one knows the utmost extent. (K, * TA.) ― -b7- Hafara varay zayodK (tropical:) He searched into the affair, or case, of Zeyd, (A, K,) and became acquainted with it. (K.) ― -b8- And Hafara , (S, A, K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., (S, A,) (assumed tropical:) He, or it, emaciated, or rendered lean: (S, K:) it (a copious flow of milk, TA) emaciated a she-goat: (K, TA:) (tropical:) he (a young camel) rendered his mother flabby in flesh by much sucking. (A.) There is no pregnant animal that pregnancy does not emaciate, except the camel: (S, A:) she fattens in pregnancy. (S.) -A2- Hafara He (a child) shed his rawaADiE [or milk-teeth ]. (K, TA.) [See also 4.] ― -b2- Hafarato rawaADiEu Almuhori , or Hufirato , (accord. to different copies of the A,) (tropical:) The milk-teeth of the colt became in a wabbling, or loose, state, previously to their falling out; because, when they have fallen out, their sockets become hollow. (A.) [See 4.] ― -b3- Hafarati AlA^asonaAnu , aor. , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. HaforN ; (S, Msb;) and Hafirat , aor. , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. HafarN , in the dial. of BenooAsad, (S, Msb,) and this is the worse of these two forms, (S,) and HaforN ; (El-Wá'ee;) and Hufirat ; (K;) (tropical:) The teeth became affected with what is termed HaforN [q. v. infrà] or HafarN : (S, Msb, K:) or became unsound: (Mgh:) and Hafara fuwhu and Hafira his teeth cankered. (A.) IDrst says, in the Expos. of the Fs, that Hafara , aor. , inf. n. Hafora fuwhu , is trans.; and that the cause of Hafor of the teeth, [or the agent of the verb Hafara ,] is old age, or the continuance of a yellow incrustation, [or tartar,] or some kind of canker that effects them: but that the verb in the phrase Hafirato sin~uhu , aor. , inf. n. HafarN , is intrans. (MF.) [The truth probably is, that the former verb is both trans. and intrans., and hence Hufirati AlA^asonaAnu ; and that the latter is intrans. only.] ― -b4- And Hafira , aor. , (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, in a bad, corrupt, or unsound, state. (Az.)

A_iHofaArN , (TA,) (tropical:) The child shed his two upper and lower central incisors: ( saqaTato lahu Alv~aniy~ataAni AlEuloyayaAni waAls~ufolayaAni :) so in the K: and to these words we find added, in some copies of the K, liloA_ivonaA='a waAlA_irobaAEi ; and then, waAlmuhorusaqaTato vanaAyaAhu warabaAEiyaAtuhu : but in some good and corrected copies, we read, after AlsflyAn , thus, wAlmhr llAvnA' wAlA rbAE sqTt vnAyAh wrbAEyAth : to which, in some lexicons, [as in the S, though the explanation which follows is there different,] after wAlArbAE , is added waAlquruwHi . (TA. [This is evidently the right reading; and therefore I follow it in an explanation in what is here immediately subjoined.]) ― -b2- AHfr Almuhoru liloA_ivonaA='i waA@loA_irobaAEi (tropical:) The colt shed his central incisors, or nippers, and each of the teeth immediately next to these: (K: see what next precedes:) or AHfr Almuhoru liloA_ivonaA='a waA@loA_irobaAEi waA@loquruwHi the colt shed his milk teeth ( rawaADiE ), [ the central pair, the second pair, and the third pair, in each jaw, ] and grew others: (S:) or AHfr Almhr , [inf. n. A_iHofaArN ,] signifies, the colt had his milk-teeth in a wabbling, or loose, state, previously to their falling out; because, when they have fallen out, their sockets become hollow: (A:) or the colt had his lower and upper central pairs of nippers, of his milk-teeth, in a wabbling, or loose, state: this is during a period extending from thirty months, at the earliest, to three years: then the teeth fall out: then a lower and an upper central pair of nippers grow in the place of the milk-nippers which have fallen out, after three years; and the epithet mubodiy'N is applied to the colt; and the epithet vaniY~N is [also] then applied to him, and continues to be until [again it is said of him] yuHofiru , meaning, he has his lower and upper pairs of nippers, of his milkteeth, in a wabbling, or loose, state: then these fall out, when he has completed four years: then the term A_ibodaA='N is [again] applied to him; [i. c., he is again termed mubodiy'N ;] and he is, and ceases not to be, termed rabaAEK , until [it is said of him] yuHofiru liloqNruwHi [in the TA, tuHofir AlquruwH , which is an evident mistake,] meaning, he has his two corner nippers [ in each jaw ] in a wabbling, or loose, state: this is when he has completed five years: then the term A_ibodaA='N is applied to him as before described: then he is [also said to be] qaAriHN . [This is evidently the right reading; and therefore I follow it in an explanation in what is here immediately subjoined.]) ― -b2- AHfr Almuhoru liloA_ivonaA='i waA@loA_irobaAEi (tropical:) The colt shed his central incisors, or nippers, and each of the teeth immediately next to these: (K: see what next precedes:) or AHfr Almuhoru liloA_ivonaA='a waA@loA_irobaAEi waA@loquruwHi the colt shed his milk teeth ( rawaADiE ), [ the central pair, the second pair, and the third pair, in each jaw, ] and grew others: (S:) or AHfr Almhr , [inf. n. A_iHofaArN ,] signifies, the colt had his milk-teeth in a wabbling, or loose, state, previously to their falling out; because, when they have fallen out, their sockets become hollow: (A:) or the colt had his lower and upper central pairs of nippers, of his milk-teeth, in a wabbling, or loose, state: this is during a period extending from thirty months, at the earliest, to three years: then the teeth fall out: then a lower and an upper central pair of nippers grow in the place of the milk-nippers which have fallen out, after three years; and the epithet mubodiy'N is applied to the colt; and the epithet vaniY~N is [also] then applied to him, and continues to be until [again it is said of him] yuHofiru , meaning, he has his lower and upper pairs of nippers, of his milkteeth, in a wabbling, or loose, state: then these fall out, when he has completed four years: then the term A_ibodaA='N is [again] applied to him; [i. c., he is again termed mubodiy'N ;] and he is, and ceases not to be, termed rabaAEK , until [it is said of him] yuHofiru liloqNruwHi [in the TA, tuHofir AlquruwH , which is an evident mistake,] meaning, he has his two corner nippers [ in each jaw ] in a wabbling, or loose, state: this is when he has completed five years: then the term A_ibodaA='N is applied to him as before described: then he is [also said to be] qaAriHN . (TA from the “Kitáb el-Kheyl” of AO.) [See also 1.]

definition: , [ Digging: a digger.
sourceDefinition: , [ Digging: a digger. ― -b2- And hence,] The HAfr of a beast, ( daAb~ap , S, K,) i. e., of a horse, or mule, or ass; (TA;) [namely, the hoof; a solid hoof; ] as though it dug the ground by reason of the vehemence of its tread upon it; (Msb;) a subst., like kaAhilN and gaAribN : (TA:) pl. HawaAfiru . (S, A, K.) ― -b3- [Hence, by a synecdoche,] xuf~N waHaAfirN (tropical:) Camels and horses. (Mgh in art. xf .) ― -b4- HaAfirN is also applied to (tropical:) The foot of a man, (S, TA,) when it is meant to be characterized as ugly. (TA.) ― -b5- ↓ Aln~aqodu Einoda AlHaAfirapi , (S, A, K,) and AlHaAfiri , (A, K,) is a prov., (S,) meaning, (tropical:) The payment in ready money is on the occasion of the first sentence spoken (Yaakoob, T, * S, K) by the seller, when he says “ I have sold to thee ” [such a thing]. (T.) The origin of the saying was this: horses were the most excellent (K) and precious (TA) of the things that they possessed; and they used not to sell them on credit: a man used to say the words above to another; meaning that its hoof should not remove until he received its price: (K:) and he who says End AlHAfrp (since he makes AlHAfr to mean the beast, Ald~aAb~ap , itself, and since its use in this sense is frequent without the mention of *aAt [prefixed to it],) subjoins to it the sign [ p ] of the fem. gender to show that *aAti AlHaAfiri is meant by this name. (TA.) Or they used to say this on the occasion of racing and betting: and the meaning is, when the horse's hoof first falls upon the dug ground [ at the goal ]: (Abu-l-'Abbás, Az, K:) ↓ HaAfirapN , (Abu-l-'Abbás,) or HaAfirN , (K,) signifying dug ground; (Abu-l- 'Abbás, K; *) ground that is dug by a horse's feet; (Har p. 653;) like as one says maA='N daAfiqN , meaning madofuwqN . (TA.) Lth says that the saying means, when thou buyest it, thou dost not quit thy place until thou payest ready money. (TA.) This was its origin: then it came to be so often said as to be used with reference to any priority. (K.) ― -b6- [Thus,] ↓ HaAfirapN signifies (tropical:) The original state or constitution of a thing; that wherein it was created: and the returning in a thing, so that the end thereof is brought back to its beginning. (K.) It is said in the Kur [lxxix. 10], A^ay^in~aA ↓ lamaroduwduwna fiY AlHaAfirapi , i. e., (tropical:) Shall we indeed be restored to our first state? (S:) i. e., to life? (Fr:) or to the present world, as we were: (IAar:) or to our first creation, after our death. (TA.) IAar cites the following verse: EalaY SalaEK wa$ayobK A^aHaAfirapF maEaA*a A@ll~`hi mino safihK waEaAri meaning (tropical:) Shall I return to my first state, wherein I was in my youth, when I indulged in amatory conversation, and silly and youthful conduct, after hoariness, and baldness of the fore part of my head? [ I beg God to preserve me from lightwittedness and shameful conduct. ] (S.) One says also, ↓ rajaEa A_ilaY HaAfiratihi , (A,) and HaAfirihi , (TA,) (tropical:) He became old and decrepit: (A, TA:) [ as though he returned to his first state; or became in a state of second childishness. ] And AilotaqawoA faA@qotataluwA Einoda ↓ AlHaAfirapi (S, A, K) and AlHaAfiri (A) (tropical:) They met, and fought one another at the first of their meeting. (S, K.) And ↓ faEala ka*aA Einoda AlHaAfirapi and AlHaAfiri (tropical:) He did so at the first, without delay. (TA.) And ↓ rajaEa EalaY HaAfiratihi (tropical:) He returned by the way by which he had come: (T, S:) or by which he had come forth. (K.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, [in the CK, erroneously, Haluma ,]) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, [in the CK, erroneously, Haluma ,]) aor. , inf. n. HulomN (Msb, TA) and HulumN , of which the former is a contraction, (Msb,) [both used also as simple substs.,] He dreamed, or saw a dream or vision (S, Msb, K) fiY nawomihi (K) in his sleep; (S, * Msb, K;) as also ↓ AHtlm (S, ISd, Msb, K,) and ↓ AnHlm , (ISd, K,) and ↓ tHl~m . (K.) You say, Halama bihi , (S, K, [in the CK, again, erroneously, Haluma ,]) and Eanohu , (K,) and Eanohu ↓ tHl~m , (TA,) and Halamahu also, (S,) He dreamed, or saw a dream or vision, of it: (S, K:) or he saw it in sleep. (M, K.) And Halama biAlmaroA^api He (a man) dreamed in his sleep that he was compressing the woman. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] HulomN and ↓ AiHotilaAmN signify [The dreaming of ] copulation in sleep: (K:) and the verbs are Halama and ↓ AHtlm . (TA.) And [hence,] both signify The experiencing an emission of the seminal fluid; properly, in dreaming; and tropically if meaning, without dreaming, whether awake or in sleep, or by extension of the signification. (TA.) And hence, (Mgh,) Halama , (Mgh, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. HulomN ; (Mgh;) and ↓ AHtlm ; (Mgh, Msb;) He (a boy) attained to puberty, (Msb,) [or] to virility. (Mgh, Msb.) -A2- Haluma , with damm [to the l ], inf. n. HilomN , (S, Msb, K,) [ He was, or became, forbearing, or clement; ] he forgave and concealed [ offences ]: or he was, or became, moderate, gentle, deliberate, leisurely in his manner of proceeding or of deportment &c., patient as meaning contr. of hasty, grave, staid, sedate, or calm; (S, K;) and (assumed tropical:) intelligent: (K:) or he managed his soul and temper on the occasion of excitement of anger. (TA.) [See HilomN below.] You say, Haloma Eanohu and ↓ tHl~m [ He treated him with forbearance, or clemency, &c. ]: both signify the same. (TA.) And yaHolumu Eam~ano yasub~uhu [ He treats with forbearance, or clemency, &c., him who reviles him ]. (TA in art. Hml .) -A3- Halima , aor. , (K,) inf. n. HalamN , (TA,) He (a camel) had [ upon him ] many ticks, such as are termed Halam . (K.) ― -b2- Also the same verb, (S, K,) with the same inf. n., (S,) It (a hide, or skin,) had in it worms, such as are termed Halam , (S, K, TA,) whereby it was spoilt and perforated, (S, TA,) so that it became useless. (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, El-Weleed Ibn-'Okbeh, TA,) faA_in~aka waAlkitaAba A_ilaY EaliY~K ka*aAbigapK waqado Halima AlA^adiymu [ For verily thou, as to the letter, or writing, to 'Alee, art like a woman tanning when the hide has become spoilt and perforated by worms ]: (S, TA:) he was urging Mo'áwiyeh to contend in battle with 'Alee, [as though] saying to him, Thou labourest to rectify a matter that has become completely corrupt, like this woman who tans the hide that has become perforated and spoilt by the Halam . (TA.) [The latter hemistich of this verse is a prov.: see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 346.] -A4- Halamahu , (K,) inf. n. HalomN , (TA,) He plucked the Halam from it; [app., accord. to the K, the worms thus called from a hide, or skin;] as also ↓ Hl~mhu : (K:) or, accord. to Az, he took from him, namely, a camel, the [ ticks called ] Halam . (TA.)

definition: [ Forbearance; clemency; ] the quality of forgiving and concealing [ offences ]: (Msb:) or moderation; gentleness; deliberateness; a leisurely manner of proceding, or of deportment, &c.; patience, as...
sourceDefinition: [ Forbearance; clemency; ] the quality of forgiving and concealing [ offences ]: (Msb:) or moderation; gentleness; deliberateness; a leisurely manner of proceding, or of deportment, &c.; patience, as meaning contr. of hastiness: gravity; staidness; sedateness; calmness: syn. A^anaApN : (S, K:) or these qualities with power or ability [ to exercise the contrary qualities ]; expl. by A^anaApN and sukuwnN with qudorapN and quw~apN : (Kull p. 167:) or the management of one's soul and temper on the occasion of excitement of anger: (TA:) or tranquillity on the occasion of emotion of anger: or delay in requiting the wrongdoer: (KT:) it is described by the term viqalN , or gravity; like as its contr. [ safahN ] is described by the terms xiq~apN and EajalN , or levity, or lightness, and hastiness: (TA in art. rjH :) also (assumed tropical:) intelligence; (K;) which is not its proper signification, but a meaning assigned because it is one of the results of intelligence: and ↓ HalomN , with fet-h, is likewise said to have this last meaning; but this requires consideration: (TA:) the former is one of those inf. ns. that are [used as simple substs., and therefore] pluralized: (ISd, TA:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^aHolaAmN and [of mult.] HuluwmN . (K.) Hence, in the Kur [lii. 32], A^amo taA^omuruhumo A^aHolaAmuhumo bih`*aA (K,) said to mean (assumed tropical:) Do their understandings enjoin them this? (TA.) And A^uwluw AlA^aHolaAmi , occurring in a trad., means (assumed tropical:) Persons of understanding. (TA.)

definition: A small tick: (K:) or a large tick;
sourceDefinition: A small tick: (K:) or a large tick; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) like Eul~N ; (S;) and said to be like the head [or nipple, when small, ] of a woman's breast: (Msb:) or a tick in the last stage of its growth; for at first, when small, it is called qamoqaAmapN ; then, HamonaAnapN ; then, quraAdN ; and then, HalamapN : (As, TA:) the pl., (S,) or [rather] coll. gen. n., (Mgh, Msb,) is ↓ HalamN . (S, Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, as being likened thereto, (Mgh,) (assumed tropical:) The head [or nipple, when small, ] of a woman's breast, (T, S, Mgh,) in the middle of the saEodaAnap [or areola ]; (T, TA;) in like manner called quraAdN : (Mgh:) the little thing rising from the breast of a woman: (TA:) the Hab~ap [or small extuberance like a pimple ] upon the head of the breast of a woman: (Msb:) the vuw^oluwl [or small excrescence ] in the middle of the breast of a woman: (K:) and the head [or nipple ] of each of the two breasts of a man: (Msb:) the two together are termed iHalamataAn : (S:) the protuberant piece of flesh is termed HalamapN as being likened in size to a large tick. (Msb.) ― -b3- Also A certain worm, incident to the upper and lower skin of a sheep or goat, (As, S,) in consequence of which, when the skin is tanned, the place thereof remains thin: (S:) or a certain worm, incident to skin, which it eats, so that, when the skin is tanned, the place of the eating rends: pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ HalamN . (K.) -A2- And A species of plant; (S, K;) accord. to As, also called yanamapN : (S:) As is also related to have said that it is a plant of the kind termed Eu$ob , having a dusty hue, a rough feel, and a red flower: another says that it grows in Nejd, in the sands, has a blossom, and roughish leaves, and thorns resembling the nails of a man; and that the camels suffer adhesion of the spleen to the side, and their young are cast, [for wtzl AxyAkhA (an evident mistranscription in the TA), I read watzil~u A^aHobaAluhA ,] when they depasture it from the dry branches: accord. to AHn, it is [ a plant ] less than a cubit [ in height ], having a thick, or rough, leaf, and branches, and a flower like that of the anemone, except that it is larger, and thicker, or rougher: accord. to the K, it signifies also the tree [or plant ] called saEodaAn ; which is one of the most excellent kinds of pasture: but Az says, it has nothing in common with the sEdAn , which is a herb having round [heads of] prickles; whereas the Hlmp has no prickles, but is a well-known kind of janobap ; and I have seen it: (TA:) [Dmr, accord. to Golius, describes it as “ a herb less than the arnoglossa ” (or arnoglossum ), “ whitening in the leaves, and downy. ”]

definition: Having Hilom [i.
sourceDefinition: Having Hilom [i. e. forbearance, or clemency, &c.; forbearing, or clement, &c.]: (Mgh, Msb, K:) pl. HulamaA='u and A^aHolaAmN . (K.) In the Kur xi. 89, it is said to be used by way of scoffing [or irony]. (TA.) AlHaliymu is one of the names of God; meaning [ The Forbearing, or Clement, &c.; or] He Whom the disobedience of the disobedient does not flurry, nor anger against them disquiet, but Who has appointed to everything a term to which it must finally come. (TA.) ― -b2- HaliymapN mugotaAZapN (tropical:) [lit. Calm, angry; or the like; because what it contains is sometimes still and sometimes boiling;] is an appellation given to a stone cooking-pot. (A and TA in art. gyZ .) -A2- A fat camel: (S:) or a camel becoming fat. (ISd, K.) ISd says, I know not any unaugmented verb belonging to it in this sense. (TA.) -A3- And Coming fat. (ISd, K.) -A4- See also HalimN .

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaHuw*u , (S, A, L,) inf. n. Hawo*N , (S, L, K,) He drove the camels quickly; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ A^aHowa*ahaA , (S, L,) inf. n. A_iHowaA*N : (K:) or violently; (M, L;) like HaAzahaA , inf. n. HawozN : (L:) or roughly: (B:) or he drove the camels to water; like HAzhA . (A. TA.) ― -b2- Also He collected the camels together to drive them. (L.) ― -b3- And Hu*otu AlA_ibila and Hi*otuhaA , I mastered, or gained the mastery over, the camels: two forms of the verb mentioned by Zj and IKtt and others, as coordinate to qaAla and xaAfa . (MF, TA.) And HA* AlHimaAru A^utunahu The he-ass gained the mastery over his she-asses, and collected them together; like HAzhA : (L:) [and so jaAnibayohaA ↓ A^aHowa*a :] Lebeed says, Ii$aA LjotamaEatn waOaHowa$a jaAnibatohaA waOaworadahaA EalaY EuwjK TawaAli [ When they became collected together, and he gained the mastery over their flanks, or] drew them together so that not one of them escaped him, [ and brought them to the watering-place, galloping upon long crooked legs; for] by Ewj he means [crooked] legs. (S, L.) ― -b4- And [hence,] HA$hu n. as above; (L;) and ↓ AisotaHowa*a Ealayohi , (S, A, L, K, *) and AstHA* ; (S, L;) He overcame, mastered, or gained the mastery over, him, or it: (S, A, L, K:) [like HAzhu .] You say, EalaY ka*aA ↓ AstHw* He mastered such a thing; gained the mastery over it; gained possession of it. (L.) Ealayohimu Al$~ayoTaAnu ↓ AstHw* [in the Kur [viii. 20] means The devil hath overcome them, or gained the mastery over them: (S, L:) or hath gained the mastery over their hearts: (Th, L:) or hath gained the mastery over them, and inclined them to that which he desired of them: (Msb:) or drove them, having gained the mastery over them. (B.) And Ealayokumo ↓ A^alamo nasotaHowi*o [in the Kur iv. 140], Did we not acquire the mastery over your affairs, and gain possession of your affection? (S, L:) or did we not gain the mastery over you by befriending and aiding you? (Aboo-Ishák, L:) or did we not overcome you, and have it in our power to slay you? (Bd.) AZ says that in all verbs coordinate to AstHw* , the original letters of the root may be preserved: that the Arabs say AisotaSaAba and AisotaSowaba , and AisotajaAba and Aisotajowaba : and that their doing so is agreeable with a rule constantly obtaining with them. (S.) The grammarians say that he who says HaA*a , aor. yaHuw*u , says only AstHA* ; and he who says A^aHowa*a , says in like manner AstHw* . (L.) ― -b5- Also HA* , aor. yaHuw*u , (L,) inf. n. Hawo*N , (L, K,) He guarded, kept, kept safely, protected, took care of, or minded, [a person, or thing;] syn. HaATa , (L,) inf. n. HawoTN . (L, K.) And HA* Ealayohi , (L,) inf. n. Hawo*N ; (K;) and ↓ A^aHowa*a , inf. n. A_iHowaA*N ; (TA:) He was observant, or regardful, of it; (L, K) as, for instance, of prayer: from HA* AlA_ibila signifying "he collected the cames together to drive them." (L.) -b1- And HA* , He did a thing, or an affair, firmly, soundly, thoroughly , or well . (L.) -b2- ALso, aor. and inf. n. as above; and A^Howa*a inf. n. A_iHowA*N ; and A^aHowa*a Als~ayora ; He journeyed hard; went a hard ,or vehement, pace. (L.)

definition: (A, L, Msb) and HaA*u Almatoni (S, L, K) The part of the back of a horse that is beneath the libod [or saddle-cloth ];
sourceDefinition: (A, L, Msb) and HaA*u Almatoni (S, L, K) The part of the back of a horse that is beneath the libod [or saddle-cloth ]; (S, A, L, Msb, K;) i. e. the middle thereof; (Msb;) as also AlHaAlu (Sh, A, L) and HaAlu Almatoni : (S, L:) also the line along the middle of the back (M, L) of a man; (L;) but AlHA* is more approved in this sense: (M, L:) and AlHA* signifies also the back of a man; (L, K;) like AlHAl : pl. A^aHowaAvN . (L.) [Hence,] xafiyfu AlHaA* ‡ A man light of back; (S, A, L, Msb;) as also xafiyfu AlHaAli ; (A;) meaning having little property: and also having a small family to maintain: (L:) or having little property and a small family to maintain: (L, K:) like xafiyfu AlZ~ahori . (A, L, Msb.) and kayofa HaA*uka and HaAluka † [lit. How is thy back? meaning, thy state, or condition? ]. (Sh, L.) HaA*N and HaA*apN both signify † A state, or condition; like HaAlN and HaAlapN , which are the more approved words. (TA.) You say, waAHidapK ↓ humaA biHaA*apK † They are both in one state, or condition . (K.) -b1- AlHaA*aAni The parts of the backs of the two thighs (of a camel, A) against which the tail falls, (S,A, * L, K,) on this side and on that: (L:) or the parts of the two thighs of a beast that faces one when he stands behind it: and two portions of flesh in the outer sides of the two thighs of a man &c.; (ISd, L:) or the hinder parts of the two thighs: pl. A=HaA*N . (Ham p. 443.) They say, A^anoqaEu All~abani maAwaliYa HaA*aYi Aln~aAqapi [ The most thirst quenching of milk is that which is next to the hinder parts of the two thighs of the she-camel ]: i. e., when it is fresh-drawn, without her having been previously sucked by a young one. (TA. [But the first word, there, is AnfE , which I regard as a mistranscription.])

definition: Quick in journeying, or in pace;
sourceDefinition: Quick in journeying, or in pace; one who goes a journey of ten nights in three. (L.) And hence, (tropical:) Quick in everything that he undertakes: quick, sharp, and active in affairs: (L:) active and skilful: (K:) active in a thing by reason of his skilfulness: (AA, S, L:) applied [as meaning active by reason of expertness ] to the wing of a bird of the kind called qaTFA , by a poet. (S, L,) namely, Homeyd Ibn-Thowr: (S:) quick in his affairs, who prosecutes them, or carries them on, well: (L:) one who prosecutes, or carries on, affairs in the best manner, by reason of his knowledge thereof: (A:) one who manages things skilfully, well, or thoroughly: (Msb:) ready, or prompt, in affairs, who masters them, and to whom nothing is out of his way, or sphere, or compass; (As, S, L, K;) as also ↓ Hawiy*N : (L, * K:) one who overcomes, or masters. (L.) And A^aHowaziY~N signifies the same. (S and K &c. in art. Hwz .) ― -b2- It is applied by a poet to thick water ( maA='N mina AlT~avorapi ) as meaning (assumed tropical:) Quick in moving the bowels. (S, L.)

sourceDefinition: [inf. n. of Hw~Y ] signifies The act of drawing together, or contracting: and the state of drawing together, or contracting; or being drawn together, or contracted; as also taHaw~K [inf. n. of ↓ tHw~Y ]: (Lh, K:) or, in the opinion of ISd, taHowiyapN has the former signification; and ↓ taHaw~K , the latter. (IAth. [See Hawiy~apN .])

definition: A place that comprises, comprehends, or contains, a thing: for instance, the belly [or womb] of the mother is a HwA=' to the child [or fœtus].
sourceDefinition: A place that comprises, comprehends, or contains, a thing: for instance, the belly [or womb] of the mother is a HwA=' to the child [or fœtus]. (TA.) ― -b2- A collection of tents ( buyuwt ), near together; as also ↓ muHaw~FY : (K:) or a collection of tents ( bywt ) of people, made of camel's fur: (S:) or a collection of tents ( bywt ) of people, at a water: (TA:) pl. A^aHowiyapN : (S, TA:) and ↓ mHtwY [app. muHotawFY ] and ↓ mHwY [app. maHowFY ] signify a place in which the tents ( bywt ) of a tribe are collected together: (Lth, TA:) the last is of the dial. of El-Yemen, where it is applied to a few small tents collected together in a tract, or region, of fruitful, or productive, land: (TA:) and its pl. is mHAwY [or, more probably, maHaAwK ; with the article, AlmaHaAwiY ]. (Lth, TA.) A tent of [ goats' ] hair, and of [ camels' ] fur, of the Arabs of the desert. (KL.)

definition: -A2- Also A winding, or circling, or coiled, gut or intestine;
sourceDefinition: : see HawFY . -A2- Also A winding, or circling, or coiled, gut or intestine; and so ↓ HaAwiyapN and ↓ HaAwiyaA='u : (K:) [also called qitobN :] or the [ kind of gut, or intestine, termed ] daw~aArap in the belly of the sheep or goat; as also ↓ HaAwiyapN : (IAar:) Hawiy~apN AlbaToni and AlbaToni ↓ HaAwiyapN and AlbaToni ↓ HaAwiyaA='u all signify the same: (S:) the pl. is HawaAyaA ; (K;) or this is the pl. of Hawiy~apN , signifying the A^amoEaA=' [or intestines into which the food passes from the stomach ]; and the pl. of HaAwiyapN and HaAwiyaA='u is [said to be] HawaAwK ; (S;) but IB says that this latter pl. is not held to be allowable by Sb, and that HawaAyaA is the pl. of all the three sings., [originally] of the measure faEaAy^ilu as pl. of the first, and fawaAEilu as pl. of the second and third [though in these two cases it should be by rule HawaA='K ]: AHeyth says that HawaAyaA as pl. of HaAwiyapN is like zawaAyaA as pl. of zaAwiyapN : and ISk mentions AlHaAwiyaAtu as pl. of AlHaAwiyapu and AlHaAwiyaA='u , [in the latter case like qaASiEaAtN as pl. of qaASiEaA='u ,] and explains it as signifying banaAtu All~abani [app. meaning the small guts, or intestines, in which originate the lacteals ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also sing. of HawaAyaA signifying Winding excavations or hollows, which the rain fills, and in which it remains a long time because the soil at the bottom thereof is cohesive and hard, retaining the water: the Arabs call them [also] A^amoEaA=' , likening them to the HawaAyaA of the belly: accord. to AA, the pl. signifies i. q. masaATiHu [pl. of misoTaHN ], made by collecting earth and stones upon smooth and hard rock, to confine thereby water: accord. to IB, on the authority of IKh, wells that are dug in the district of Kelb, in hard ground, whereby is confined the water of the torrents, which they drink throughout the year: accord. to Nasr, a certain construction with masses of rock in the form of a pool, on the way to Et-Teghlibeeyeh, near Ood: accord. to ISd, the sing. signifies a smooth and hard rock which is surrounded with stones and earth, in which water collects. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' , stuffed [ with vumaAm or the like ], which is wound round the hump of the camel; (S, K; *) i. q. sawiy~apN , except that the former is only for camels, and the latter is sometimes for other animals: pl. HawaAyaA : (S:) a subst. from 2 in the last of the senses assigned to it above: (IAth:) [the same is app. meant by what here follows:] a certain thing that is prepared for a woman to ride upon. (TA. [But it was also used by men.]) 'Omeyr Ibn-Wahb El-Jumahee said, on the day of Bedr, when he computed the number of the companions of the Prophet, raA^ayotu AlHawaAyaA EalayohaA AlmanaAyaA [meaning I saw the HwAyA with the men of courage upon them ]: (S:) [for] maniy~apN [sing. of mnAyA ] means (assumed tropical:) “ a man of courage upon his saddle. ” (TA.)

sourceDefinition: ; (Msb, K;) and ↓ xv~rhu , (A, Msb, K,) inf. n. taxoviyrN ; (TA;) He thickened it; made it thick, (Msb, A, K,) and strong; (Msb;) namely, milk, (A, Msb, K,) and honey, and the like, (TA,) and a liniment or the like, (A,) or some other thing. (Msb.) ― -b2- And the former signifies also He left it in a thick state; namely, fresh butter; (As, S, K;) not melting it. (As, S.) It is said in a prov., maA yadoriY A^ayuxoviru A^amo yu*iybu [ He knows not whether to leave in a thick state or to melt ]: (S K; in one copy of the former of which, the fem. forms of the verbs are used:) applied to him who is confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course, and who wavers, or vacillates: its origin being this: a woman melts fresh butter, and what is thick thereof becomes mixed with what is thin, and she is vexed and wearied by her case, and knows not whether to raise the fire with fuel, in order that it may become clear; fearing that, if she do so, it will burn: thus she is perplexed. (K.)

Ainokasara ; as also ↓ AnxrE : (Lth, K:) and [in like manner] ↓ txr~E he (a man) was, or became, relaxed, or flaccid, and weak, or infirm, and soft, or tender. definition: Any weak, bending plant, of whatever kind it be: (As, S:) any plant weak, or fragile, ( qaSiyf ,) and sappy, whether it be a tree or a herb: (TA:) a plant weak by reason of its softness, or tenderness, and sappiness.
sourceDefinition: Any weak, bending plant, of whatever kind it be: (As, S:) any plant weak, or fragile, ( qaSiyf ,) and sappy, whether it be a tree or a herb: (TA:) a plant weak by reason of its softness, or tenderness, and sappiness. (Sgh.) [See also xariEN .] ― -b2- Hence, as some say, (TA,) [The ricinus communis; common palma Christi; or castor-oil-plant; ] a certain plant, (S, Msb, K,) well known, (S,) soft, tender, or pliant, (Msb,) not serving for pasturage, (K,) bearing a berry resembling sparrows' eggs, called Als~imosimu AlhinodiY~u ; accord to Ibn-Jezleh, the best thereof is that called AlbaHoriY~u ; it has the property of loosening phlegm, and it is useful for counteracting the colic and palsy and the [ disease in the face called ] laqowap , the dose extending to a mivoqaAl . (TA.) The word is of the measure fiEowalN ; (Msb;) and J says [in the S] that there is no other word of the same measure except EitowadN , which is the name of a certain valley; but to this have been added *irowadN , the name of a certain mountain; and EitowarN , the name of a certain valley, and not a mistranscription of EitowadN ; and jidowalN , a dial. var. of jadowalN . (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also] AimoraA^apN xirowaEapN A beautiful, and soft, or tender, woman: and [the pl.] xaraAwiyEu , applied to women, signifies [ the same, or merely] beautiful. (TA.) ― -b4- And xirowaEN is likewise applied to youth, or youthfulness, and to life, meaning (tropical:) Soft, or delicate. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. (S, Sgh, L, K) and , (L, K,) inf. n. xa$ofN , (S,) He, or it, made a sound, (L, K,) or what is termed His~ [i. e. a low, faint, gentle, or soft, sound ], (S,) and an audible motion: (S, L:) said of a man: and said also of snow, as meaning it caused one to hear a [ sound such as is termed ] xa$ofap in walking [ upon it ]; as is the case in intense cold. (S.) And xa$afa , aor. , inf. n. xu$uwfN , said of snow, It was rough, so that it caused one to hear a xa$ofap in walking [ upon it ]: and in like manner said of ice; i. e. it was soft, or yielding [ to the feet, crackling ], or easily broken. (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, El-Katámee, (TA,) A_i*aA kab~ada Aln~ajomu Als~amaA='a bi$atowapK EalaYHiyna har~a Alkalobu wAlv~aloju xaA$ifu [ When the asterism of the Pleiades culminates in winter, at the time when the dog whines by reason of the cold, and the snow causes one to hear a slight sound in walking upon it ]: (S:) or, accord. to IB, the right reading is, bisuHorapK [ a little before daybreak, or in the last third of the night ]: (TA:) Hyn is here mansoob because ElY is made to be redundant, and because it is prefixed to a verbal proposition: (S:) this is the more approved way in a case of this kind, when the verb commencing the proposition is a pret.; but some say ElY Hiyni . (I 'Ak p. 199.) ― -b2- xa$afa said of water, It froze. (K.) ― -b3- Said of cold, It was, or became, intense. (K.) ― -b4- xa$afa iY Als~ayori , (K,) inf. n. xa$afaAnN , (JK,) He hastened, made haste, or sped, [app. so as to cause a slight sound to be heard, ] in going, journeying, or pace. (JK, * K.) And mar~a yaxo$ifu He passed along hastening. (TA.) ― -b5- xa$afa , (S, K,) aor. (S, TA) and , (TA,) inf. n. xu$uwfN (S, K) and xa$afaAnN , (K,) He went away in, or into, the land, or country. (S, K.) And xa$afa fulaAnN Such a one journeyed away, went away, or departed, or became hidden or concealed, syn. tagay~aba , (K, TA,) in the land, or country. (TA.) ― -b6- xa$afa fiY Al$~aYo'i (aor. , TA,) He entered into the thing; as also ↓ Anx$f . (K.) ― -b7- xa$afa , inf. n. xa$afaAnN , He (a man) went, or travelled, by night. (K.) ― -b8- And He was bold, or daring, in night-journeying: or he went about, or round about, by night; (L, K, TK; but in the first and second, only the inf. n. is mentioned in this case;) and journeyed much by night. (L.) And xa$afa biAlqawomi , aor. , said of a guide of the way, He went about, or round about, by night, and hastened, or sped, with the party: (JK:) or xa$afa bihimo , inf. n. xa$aAfapN , he (a guide of the way) acted with a penetrative energy, or with sharpness, vigorousness, and effectiveness, with them [ in conducting them ]; as also ↓ x$~f , inf. n. taxo$iyfN . (K, * TA.) ― -b9- xa$afato biwaladihaA She (a woman) cast forth her child [from the womb]. (K.) And xu$ifa bihi He, or it, was cast, or thrown; as also xufi$a bh , and Hufi$a bh . (TA.) -A2- xa$afa raA^osahu biAlHajari He (a man, S) broke his head with the stone. (S, K.)

definition: , (S, A, Mgh, K, TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, K, TA,) aor. , [in the CK, erroneously, ,] inf. n. xaTorN and xaTaraAnN (S, Mgh, K) and xaTiyrN , (JK, K,) He (a camel, S, Mgh, or a stallion [camel], A, K) raised his tail time after time, and struck his thighs with it: (S:) or lashed with it to the right and left: (K:) or moved about his tail: (A, * Mgh, TA:) the stallion does so in threatening, through pride; (T, TA;) or in fighting with others, as though threatening; (A;) or by reason of emaciation occasioned by severe drought; or by reason of sprightliness: but a she-camel, to inform the stallion that she has become pregnant. (TA.) You say also, gaTara b*nbh , aor. : the g being a substitute for the x : (TA:) or each form may be original; but the latter is the less used. (IJ, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xaTara biromoHihi , (A, * K,) and bisayofihi , (K,) and biqaDiybihi , and bisawoTihi , (TA,) inf. n. xaTaraAnN , (K,) (tropical:) He moved his spear up and down, and his sword, (K, TA,) and his rod, and his whip. (TA.) A man does so with the spear when he walks between the two [opposing] ranks. (A.) ― -b3- And xaTara biyadihi fiY ma$oyihi (tropical:) [ He moved his arm up and down in his walking ]. (A.) And xaTara fiY mi$oyatihi , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. xaTaraAnN (K) and xaTiyrN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He moved his arms up and down in his mode of walking, (K, TA,) inclining his body from side to side at the same time. (TA.) And xaTara , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. xaTaraAnN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) shook himself in walking; (S;) and walked with an elegant and a proud and self-conceited gait, with an affected inclining of the body from side to side. (S, TA.) Aljunodu yaxoTiruwna Hawola qaAy^idihimo (assumed tropical:) [ The troops strut around their leader ] is said when they show their energy to their leader; and in like manner, when they assemble and equip themselves in war. (TA.) ― -b4- And xaTara , aor. , inf. n. xaTorN , (assumed tropical:) He (a man) raised his arm, or hand, with a stone which he lifted for the purpose of trying his strength, to cast, or throw, and shook the stone in lifting it. (TA.) ― -b5- And xaTara biA_iSobaEihi A_ilaY Als~amaA='i (tropical:) He moved his finger, [or raised it towards the sky, ] in supplication. (A.) [This one does in the ordinary prayers, in uttering the profession of belief in the unity of God; raising the first finger only (of the right hand, which is placed on the thigh, while sitting on the left foot), and not the hand itself.] ― -b6- And xaTara , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. xaTaraAnN , (S,) (assumed tropical:) It (a spear) quivered, vibrated, or shook: (S, K:) or moved up and down previously to a thrusting with it. (S.) ― -b7- xaTara bibaAliY , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and EalaY baAliY , (JK, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. (S, ISd, IKtt, Mgh, K) and , (ISd, IKtt, K,) inf. n. xuTuwrN , (JK, S, Mgh, K,) or xaTarN , (Msb,) and xaTaraAnN , (JK,) or this last is a mistranscription, (Mgh,) (tropical:) It bestirred itself in my mind: (A: [see xaATirN :]) or it moved my mind: (Msb:) or it occurred to my mind [absolutely, or] after I had forgotten it. (K.) ― -b8- xaTara Al$~ayoTaAnu bayonahu wabayona qalobihi (assumed tropical:) The devil put vain suggestions into his mind. (TA.) xaTara Ald~ahoru xaTaraAnahu , (S,) or mino xaTaraAnihi , (TA,) (tropical:) [ Fortune, or time, produced, or brought to pass, its events, or among its events such and such things]: a phrase like Darba Ald~ahoru DarabaAnahu , (S,) or mino DarabaAnihi . (T, A. [See art. Drb .]) -A2- xaTura , aor. , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. xuTuwrapN , (S, K,) or xaTarN , (Msb,) (tropical:) He (a man, S &c.) was, or became, eminent, noble, or of high rank, (Msb, K,) or characterized by rank or station. (S, A.) And xaTara , [or this is probably a mistranscription for xaTura ,] aor. , inf. n. xaTarN and xuTuwrN , [or, more probably, xuTuwrapN ,] (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, great in estimation, rank, or dignity, after having been little in respect thereof. (TA.)

definition: The being at the point of, or near to, destruction;
sourceDefinition: The being at the point of, or near to, destruction; (JK, S, A, Msb, K;) [ imminent danger; peril; jeopardy; risk; hazard; ] and fear of perishing: (Msb:) pl. A^axoTaArN . (A.) You say, huwa EalaY xaTarK EaZiymK He is [ in a state of great peril, or] on the brink of destruction. (A.) And rakobuwA AlA^axoTaAra [ They embarked in perilous undertakings; or braved perils ]. (A.) [And A^amoru lahu xaTarN and *uw xaTarK A perilous affair or event or case: and hence, a momentous, or an important, affair or event or case; an affair, or event,. or a case, of moment or importance or magnitude: see also xaTiyrN .] And xaTarN [alone] signifies A thing, or an affair, &c., of great magnitude: and a trial, or an affliction: pl. as above. (Har p. 264.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A bet, wager, stake, or thing wagered; a thing staked at a shooting-match or a race, and taken by the winner: (T, S, * A, * Mgh, * Msb, * K, * TA:) [accord. to the TA, this is the primary signification; but accord. to the A, it is tropical:] pl. as above; (Msb;) or xiTaArN ; and pl. pl. xuTurN : (K: [but in some copies of the K, the last is written A^axoTaArN ; and so in the TA, where it is added that some say it is pl. of xaTarN , like as A^asobaAbN is of sababN , and A^anodaAbN of nadabN :]) xaTarN and sabaqN and nadabN all signify the same. (TA.) You say, waDaEuwA xaTarFA (tropical:) [ They laid a bet ]. (A.) And A^aHoraza fulaAnN AlxaTara (tropical:) [ Such a one won the bet ]. (A.) ― -b3- Hence, [app. as being likened to a stake won,] (TA,) (tropical:) Eminence; nobility; as also ↓ xaTorN : (K, TA:) in which sense it has become so much used as to be, in this acceptation, conventionally regarded as proper: (TA:) also excellence: (TA:) and (as also ↓ xaTorN , TA) rank; degree of dignity; station; of a man: (S, A, K, TA:) and highness of rank or account or estimation: and wealth: (TA:) pl. A^axoTaArN : (A:) accord. to some, it is only used to signify high rank: but accord. to others, you say, A_in~ahu laEaZiymu AlxaTari (tropical:) [ Verily he is of great dignity ] with respect to his good actions and his nobility, and Sagiyru AlxaTari (tropical:) [ of little rank ] with respect to his evil actions and his ignobleness. (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) A lot, or portion, or share. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A compensation. (TA.) -A2- (assumed tropical:) A like, or fellow, (S, K,) in rank or station, (S,) or in eminence; (K;) as also ↓ xaTiyrN . (S, K.) You say, h`*aA xaTarN lih`*aA , and ↓ xaTiyrN , (assumed tropical:) This is like to that. (S.) And Aljan~apu laA xaTara lahaA (assumed tropical:) Paradise has not its like. (TA.) And ↓ fulaAnN layosa lahu xaTiyrN (assumed tropical:) Such a one has not his like or fellow. (TA.) -A3- Also [an inf. n. of xaTara in the phrase xaTara bibaAliY and EalaY baAliY , accord. to the Msb And hence,] (assumed tropical:) A vain suggestion of the devil. (JK.) [See xaATirN .]

definition: The falling of a camel's tail between the parts above his thighs, when he moves it about;
sourceDefinition: The falling of a camel's tail between the parts above his thighs, when he moves it about; [see 1, first sentence;] as also ↓ xTAr . (TA: in which the latter is written without any syll. signs.) -A2- A camel's nose-rein; (S, K;) a nose-rein by which a she-camel is led: (Kr:) a rope: (Sh, K:) these, says Meyd, are one and the same thing. (TA.) It is related in a trad. of 'Alee that he said to [ a mistake for “ respecting ”] 'Ammár, jur~uwA lahu AlxaTiyra maA A@nojar~a lakumo [ Pull ye his noserein as long as it will be pulled by you ]: or, as some relate the saying, maA jar~ahu lakumo [ as long as he pulls it to you ]: meaning follow him as long as there is ground for doing so: or, accord. to some, as Sh says, act patiently towards 'Ammar as long as he acts patiently towards you: Meyd mentions it as a proverb. (TA.) -A3- (tropical:) Eminent; noble; of high rank: (Msb, K, TA:) characterized by rank or station: (S, A:) pl. xuTorN (K) and xaTiyruwna . (A.) And (assumed tropical:) Anything excellent. (TA.) You say A^amorN xaTiyrN (assumed tropical:) A thing, or an affair, of high account or estimation. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Ignoble; of low rank; (AZ, TA;) contemptible. (AZ, Msb.) ― -b3- See also xaTarN , in three places.

sourceDefinition: Fresh, green, or juicy, herbage : (S, IB, Mgh, Msb, K:) that which is dry is termed Ha$iy$ [but see this word]: (Msb, from the Kf:) or dry Ha$iy$ : (so in one place in the S: [app. a mistake occasioned by an omission:]) or i. q. ruTobN , (IB, Msb,) with damm, (IB,) [i. e. fresh, or green, pasture; or such as consists of the herbs, or leguminous plants, of the rabiyE ; or of these and of trees or shrubs :] or herbage that is cut, of the herbs, or leguminous plants, of the rbyE : (Lth, JK:) or, accord. to [the Imám] Mohammad, anything that is eaten as pasture, not [ growing ] upon a stem : (Mgh:) or slender herbage as long as it remains fresh, green, or juicy : (IAth, TA:) it is also written ↓ xalaA='N , with medd, like qaDaA='N : (Msb:) n. un. xalaApN : (S, Msb, K:) or this signifies any herb ( baqolap ) that one pulls up : (K, * TA:) pl. definition: , aor. yaxuwru , (S, A, Mgh,) inf. n. xuwaArN (JK, S, A, Mgh, K *) and xaworN , (JK,) He (a bull) uttered his cry; [i. e. lowed, or bellowed; ] (Lth, JK, S, A, Mgh, K;) this being its primary...
sourceDefinition: , aor. yaxuwru , (S, A, Mgh,) inf. n. xuwaArN (JK, S, A, Mgh, K *) and xaworN , (JK,) He (a bull) uttered his cry; [i. e. lowed, or bellowed; ] (Lth, JK, S, A, Mgh, K;) this being its primary signification: (Er-Rághib:) the inf. n. xwAr , used agreeably with this explanation, occurs in the Kur xx. 90 [and vii. 146]: (S:) it signifies the loud crying [i. e. the lowing or bellowing ] of a cow and of a calf: (Lth:) and the crying [i. e. bleating ] of sheep, or that of goats, and of gazelles, (K,) and of any beast: (Er-Rághib:) and the sounding [i. e. whizzing ] of arrows: (K:) of any of these, you say, xaAra , aor. and inf. n. as above. (TA.) [Hence,] lahu SawotN kaxuwaAri Alv~awori He has a voice like the bellowing of the bull. (A.) ― -b2- [And hence, (see 10,)] xAr Ealayohi (tropical:) He bent, turned, or inclined, towards him. (A.) -A2- xAr , aor. as above, (S, Msb,) inf. n. xuw^uwrN , (S, K, [for which Golius, as on these authorities, substitutes xuw^uwrapN ,]) said of a man, (S,) and of anything, (TA,) He, or it, was, or became, weak, or feeble, (S, Msb, K,) and languid; (S, TA;) as also xawira , (TA,) aor. yaxowaru , (JK,) inf. n. xawarN ; (S, * K, * TA;) and ↓ xiw~ir , (JK, TA,) inf. n. taxowiyrN . (K.) xAr and xawira both signify It was soft, or fragile; said of anything, like a reed. (JK.) It is said in a trad. of 'Omar, lano yaxuwra qawiY~N maA daAma SaAHibuhaA banoziEu wayanozuw , meaning A possessor of strength ( SaAHibu quw~apK ) will not be weak as long as he can pull his bow and leap to his beast. (TA.) In a camel that is drinking, xawarN denotes, or implies, a quality that is praised; i. e. Patient enduring of thirst and fatigue: and a quality dispraised; i. e. the lacking patience to endure thirst and fatigue. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, said of heat, (S, TA,) and of cold, inf. n. xuw^uwrN and xuw^uwrapN , (JK,) (tropical:) It became faint; it remitted, or abated; (JK, S, TA;) and so xawira , inf. n. xawarN ; and ↓ xw~r . (TA.) And xAr Ean~aA , said of cold, It ceased from us; quitted us. (A.) -A3- xaArahu , (JK, S,) inf. n. xaworN , (S, K,) He hit, or hurt, his xaworaAn , (JK, S, K, *) in thrusting or piercing him with a spear or the like. (JK, S.)

definition: [ He endeavoured to make her (namely, a gazelle, or a wild cow,) to utter her cry;
sourceDefinition: [ He endeavoured to make her (namely, a gazelle, or a wild cow,) to utter her cry; or] he uttered a cry in order that she should do the same. (TA.) The sportsman, coming to a place in which he thinks the young one of a gazelle or [wild] cow to be, utters a cry like that of her young one; and the mother, hearing it, if she have a young one, thinks the cry to be that of her young one, and follows the cry. (S, * TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (S, TA,) AstxArhu (tropical:) He endeavoured to make him bend, turn, or incline: (JK, S, A, K, TA:) and he called him to him: and he interrogated him; or desired him to speak; syn. AisotanoTaqahu : namely, a man. (JK.) [ AstxAr Almanozila is explained in the L and K as meaning AisotanoZafahu : to which is added in the TA, kA^n~h Tlb xyrh , with the remark that it should therefore properly be mentioned in art. xyr : but an explanation in the sentence immediately preceding, and a verse cited below, evidently show that AstnZfh is a mistranscription for AisotanoTaqahu , and that xyrh should be xabarahu : so that the meaning is He interrogated the place of abode. ] The author of the L cites, as an ex., the saying of El-Kumeyt, walano yasotaxiyru rusuwma Ald~iyaAri liEawolatihi *uw AlS~ibaY AlmuEwilu [ And he who is affected with youthful amorousness, wailing, will not ask the remains, or traces, of the dwellings to reply to his wailing: but for liEawolatihi I would rather read biEawolatihi ; i. e., will not interrogate them with his wailing ]. (TA.) ― -b3- AstxAr AlD~ab~a , (K, TA, [in some copies of the K, erroneously, AlD~abuEa ,]) and AlyarobuwEa , (TA,) He placed a piece of wood in the hole of the burrow of the [ lizard called ] Db~ , (K, TA,) and of the jerboa, i. e. in the qaASiEaA=' , (TA,) in order that it should come forth from another place, (K, TA,) i. e. the naAfiqaA=' , so that he might catch it. (TA.) Lth falsely assigns the act of AlAisotixaArap to the Db~ and the jerboa. (Az, TA.)
