sourceDefinition: A thing that is the equal of another thing (Msb, K) of any kind (K) in its measure so that it covers the whole extent of the latter like the lid: this is its primary signification: (Msb:) [whence] one says, h`*aA Al$~aYo'u Tabaqu h`*aA , like Tiboquhu , q. v.: (IAar, O, K:) and [hence] it signifies The cover, or lid, (Mgh, K,) of a jar, (Mgh,) or of anything: (K:) pl. A^aTobaAqN (S, * O, * K) [and TibaAqN , mentioned in the Msb as a pl. of TabaqN in another, but similar, sense, which will be found in what follows, but better known as a pl. of TabaqapN ], and A^aTobiqapN is added as another pl. in the K, but [SM says] this is strange; I have not found it in the [other] lexicons; and it may be that the right reading is waA^aTobaqahu , as syn. with what immediately there follows it, i. e. waTab~aqahu . (TA.) waAfaqa $an~N Tabaqaho is [a prov.] expl. (O, K, TA) by As (O, TA) as said of a company of men who had a receptacle of skin [i. e. a water-skin] that had become old and worn out, wherefore they made a Tabaq [or cover] for it: (O, K, TA:) [so that the meaning is, A water-skin that had become old and worn out suited its cover: ] or $an~N and TabaqN [in the O Tbqh ] were two tribes; (S, * O, K * TA;) and, as ISd says, $an~N does not here mean a water-skin, for this has no Tabaq : (TA:) or [ TabaqahN is for Tabaqapa , and] Tabaqapu was an intelligent woman, whom an intelligent man took as his wife. (O, K, TA. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 800.]) ― -b2- Also A certain household utensil; (Msb;) [i. e. a dish, or plate; perhaps thus called because the cover of a cooking-vessel is often used as a dish or plate;] the thing upon which one eats, (K, TA,) and in which one eats; and the thing upon which fruit is placed [i. e. a dish, or plate, used for that purpose; and likewise a round tray, and the like ]: (TA:) pl. A^aTobaAqN and TibaAqN . (Msb.) ― -b3- ― -b4- (tropical:) The surface of the earth [considered as a cover]. (K, TA.) [And in like manner applied to A layer, or stratum, of earth. dafanotu Al$~aYo'a is expl. in the Msb as meaning A^axofayotuhu taHota A^aTobaAqi Alt~uraAbi I concealed it beneath the layers, or strata, of the earth, or dust. See also TabaqapN .] ― -b5- (tropical:) The exterior part of the pudendum muliebre [considered as a cover]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K, TA.) ― -b6- A fold, a ply, or an overlapping part, of a thing. (PS. [See HafivN .]) ― -b7- [And hence, app., (tropical:) A roller of the sea: see A=*iY~N .] ― -b8- A thin bone [or cartilage ] that forms a division between any two vertebræ: (S, O, K:) what is between any two vertebræ of a horse [&c.]: pl. A^aTobaAqN : (Kr:) and some say, the vertebræ altogether: and some say, a vertebra, in any part. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the day of resurrection, taboqaY A^aSolaAbu AlmunaAfiqiyna TabaqFA waAHidFA , meaning [ The backbones of the hypocrites shall be (lit. continue to be ) as though they were] one vertebra: or, as some say, ↓ TabaqapF ; and [they say that] TabaqN is the pl. [or coll. gen. n.]. (O. [See also 1 in art. Eqm .]) ― -b9- [And Any of the successively-superimposed cartilages of the windpipe: pl. A^aTobaAqN . (See HanojarapN , in art. Hjr ; and see also HuloquwmN .)] ― -b10- Any of the stages of Hell [whereof every one except the lowest is imagined to be like a cover over another]. (TA.) [And in like manner, Any of the Seven Heavens: ] one says, Als~am`waAtu TibaAqN , meaning The Heavens are [composed of stages ] one above another; (S, O, Msb; *) every heaven [except the lowest] being like a Tbq to another: (Msb:) or this is said because of their being conformable, one with another: (K:) and it is said in the Kur lxvii. 3, Aal~a*iY xalaqa saboEa sam`waAtK TibaAqFA , meaning [ Who hath created seven heavens ] placed one above another; TbAqA being the inf. n. of TaAbaqotu Aln~aEola [q. v.], used as an epithet; or for Tuwbiqato TibaAqFA ; or *aAta TibaAqK , pl. of TabaqN or of ↓ TabaqapN . (Bd.) ― -b11- [ Any of the bones of the head; because they compose a covering: or] A^aTobaAqu Alr~aA^osi means the bones of the head because they suit one another and have certain parts of them inserted and infixed into other parts. (TA. [See 8 in art. $jr .]) ― -b12- Any joint of a limb: pl. A^aTobaAqN . (As, TA.) ― -b13- A collective number of men, and of locusts; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ TiboqN , (K,) which is thus expl. by As in relation to men: (TA:) or a multitude of men, and of locusts: (K:) [app. considered as covering a space of ground:] or a company of men that are equal with a company like them. (ISd, TA.) ― -b14- A generation of mankind; or the people of one time; syn. qaronN and EaAlamN ; as in the saying of El- 'Abbás, A_i*aA maDaY EaAlamN badaA Tabaqu [metre munosariH ] i. e. A_i*aA maDaY qaronN badaA qaronN [ When a generation passes away, a generation appears in its place]: the qaron being called Tabaq because they are a Tabaq [i. e. cover] to the earth: then they pass away and another Tabq comes: (O, TA:) or, as IAar says, TabaqN signifies a people after a people. (TA.) And (TA) A qaron [i. e. generation ] of time: or twenty years: (K, TA:) or, as in the book of El-Hejeree, on the authority of I'Ab, ↓ TabaqapN has this latter meaning. (TA.) ― -b15- (tropical:) A rain such as fills and covers the earth, or land; (TA;) or such as is general, (S, O, K, TA,) and of wide extent; termed by a poet (namely, Imra-el-Keys, O, TA) Tabaqu AlA^aroDi : (S, O, TA:) or a lasting rain, consecutive in its falls. (Msb.) And A^aSobaHati AlA^aroDu TabaqFA waAHidFA means (assumed tropical:) [ The land became, or became in the morning, ] covered with water over its surface. (TA.) ― -b16- A main portion of the night and of the day: (S, O, K:) or, accord. to the Mufradát [of Er-Rághib], Tabaqu All~ayoli waAln~ahaAri signifies saAEaAtuhu AlmTAbqp [app. a mistranscription for AlmutaTaAbiqapu , and meaning the commensurate, or similar, or equal, portions of the night and of the day ]. (TA.) See also TiboqN . ― -b17- And A state, or condition; (S, O, K, TA;) as also ↓ TabaqapN , of which the pl. is TibaAqN : the pl. of the former in this sense is A^aTobaAqN . (TA.) Hence the phrase, latarokabun~a TabaqFA Eano TabaqK , (S, O, K, TA,) in the Kur [lxxxiv. 19], meaning [ Ye shall assuredly enter upon ] state after state, (S, * O, TA,) and predicament after predicament; as in the A; (TA;) on the day of resurrection; (S;) the state being termed Tabaq because it will fill the hearts [as though the dread thereof covered them], or will be near to doing so; (O, TA;) and Eano being put in this instance, as it is in many others, in the place of baEoda : (TA:) or the meaning is, one after another of similar states of hardship: or it may be, degrees of hardship after degrees thereof; TabaqN accord. to this rendering being regarded as pl. [or coll. gen. n.] of ↓ TabaqapN : (Ksh and Bd:) or [ ye shall assuredly mount upon ] the heaven in one state after another state; for it (the heaven) shall be like muhol [i. e. molten brass or iron &c., as is said in the Kur lxx. 8,] and then successively in other states: (O, TA:) so says Aboo-Bekr: accord. to Er-Rághib, it points to the various successive states of man in the present world from his creation, and in the world to come until his resting in one of the two abodes [Paradise or Hell]: or, accord. to Ibn-Abi-l- Hadeed, it means [ ye shall assuredly enter upon ] difficulty after difficulty; as is related by MF; and the same is said by Az on the authority of I'Ab: (TA:) some read latarokaban~a , meaning thou, O Mohammad, shalt assuredly mount upon stage after stage of the stages ( A^aTobaAq ) of heaven; and I'Ab and Ibn-Mes-ood read latarokabin~a , with kesr to the b , which is accord. to the dial. of Temeem, and Keys and Asad and Rabee'ah pronounce the first letter of the future with kesr except when it is Y : 'Omar read layarokaban~a , either as relating to the Prophet or as referring to him who is mentioned in verses 10-15 of the same chapter. (O, TA.) One says also, baAta yaroEaY Tabaqa Aln~ujuwmi , meaning (tropical:) [ He passed the night watching ] the state of the stars in their course: (TA:) or Tabaqu Aln~ujuwmi means the falling [or app. setting ] of stars after [ other ] stars: or, accord. to Es-Sadoosee, the rising of a star and the setting of another: and a collective number thereof after a collective number [ of others ]: and such, he says, are termed mina Aln~ujuwmi ↓ TabaqaAtN . (O.) ― -b18- jaA='ati AlA_ibilu TabaqFA waAHidFA means EalaY xuf~K waAHidK [i. e. The camels came following one another, in a single line: see art. xf ]. (TA.) And one says, waladati Alganamu TabaqFA and ↓ TaboqFA , meaning The sheep, or goats, brought forth one after another: (L:) El-Umawee says, when they do thus, one says, waladatohaA Alr~ujayolaA='i and waladatohaA TabaqFA and ↓ TabaqapF [ They brought them forth (i. e. their young ones) one after another ]. (S, O.) ― -b19- [The pl.] AlA^aTobaAqu also signifies Those who are remote, and those who are remotely connected: so in a trad. respecting the signs of the resurrection, or of the time thereof; in which it is said, yuwoSalu AlA^aTobaAqu wayuqoTaEu AlA^aroHaAmu [ Those who are remote, and those who are remotely related, shall be brought into close connection, and the ties of relationship shall be severed ]. (TA.) ― -b20- binotu TabaqK is an appellation of A female tortoise, [app. because of the cover of her back,] which, (S, O, K,) as the Arabs assert, (S, O,) lays ninety-nine eggs, all of them [ eventually ] tortoises, and lays one egg which discloses (S, O, K) a serpent (K) [or a serpent such as is termed ] an A^asowad ; (S, O;) or, accord. to Az, sixty-nine [ eggs ], and the seventieth is [ eventually ] a viper. (So in a marg. note in one of my copies of the S; in which, also, the appellation is written binotu Tabaqa , instead of binotu TabaqK .) Hence the phrase A_iHodaY banaAti TabaqK , meaning (tropical:) A calamity; (S, O, TA;) as also binotu TabaqK : (TA:) banaAtu TabaqK meaning calamities [like muTobiqaAtN ]: as well as tortoises: and serpents: (K:) and A^um~u TabaqK [in like manner] means calamity: (TA in art. Trq :) or, accord. to EthTha'álibee, Tabaqu [thus, imperfectly decl., as written in the L,) signifies a yellow serpent: (L, TA:) and A^um~u TabaqK and binotu TabaqK are said to signify the serpent, because of its coiling itself round: or banaAtu TabaqK is an appellation applied to serpents because of their winding themselves round ( lA_iTobaAqihaA ) upon him whom they bite; or, as some say, because the Haw~aA=' [q. v.] confines them beneath the lids ( A^aTobaAq ) of the baskets ( A^asofaAT ) covered with leather; or, as Z says, because they resemble the Tabaq [i. e. cover, or dish, or plate,] when they coil themselves round. (TA.)

[or coll. gen. n.] of ↓ TabaqapN : (Ksh and Bd:) or [ ye shall assuredly mount upon ] the heaven in one state after another state; for it (the heaven) shall be like muhol [i. e. molten brass or iron &c., as is said in the Kur lxx. 8,] and then successively in other states: (O, TA:) so says Aboo-Bekr: accord. to Er-Rághib, it points to the various successive states of man in the present world from his creation, and in the world to come until his resting in one of the two abodes [Paradise or Hell]: or, accord. to Ibn-Abi-l- Hadeed, it means [ ye shall assuredly enter upon ] difficulty after difficulty; as is related by MF; and the same is said by Az on the authority of I'Ab: (TA:) some read latarokaban~a , meaning thou, O Mohammad, shalt assuredly mount upon stage after stage of the stages ( A^aTobaAq ) of heaven; and I'Ab and Ibn-Mes-ood read latarokabin~a , with kesr to the b , which is accord. to the dial. of Temeem, and Keys and Asad and Rabee'ah pronounce the first letter of the future with kesr except when it is Y : 'Omar read layarokaban~a , either as relating to the Prophet or as referring to him who is mentioned in verses 10-15 of the same chapter. (O, TA.) One says also, baAta yaroEaY Tabaqa Aln~ujuwmi , meaning (tropical:) [ He passed the night watching ] the state of the stars in their course: (TA:) or Tabaqu Aln~ujuwmi means the falling [or app. setting ] of stars after [ other ] stars: or, accord. to Es-Sadoosee, the rising of a star and the setting of another: and a collective number thereof after a collective number [ of others ]: and such, he says, are termed mina Aln~ujuwmi ↓ TabaqaAtN . (O.) ― -b18- jaA='ati AlA_ibilu TabaqFA waAHidFA means EalaY xuf~K waAHidK [i. e. The camels came following one another, in a single line: see art. xf ]. (TA.) And one says, waladati Alganamu TabaqFA and ↓ TaboqFA , meaning The sheep, or goats, brought forth one after another: (L:) El-Umawee says, when they do thus, one says, waladatohaA Alr~ujayolaA='i and waladatohaA TabaqFA and ↓ TabaqapF [ They brought them forth (i. e. their young ones) one after another ]. (S, O.) ― -b19- [The pl.] AlA^aTobaAqu also signifies Those who are remote, and those who are remotely connected: so in a trad. respecting the signs of the resurrection, or of the time thereof; in which it is said, yuwoSalu AlA^aTobaAqu wayuqoTaEu AlA^aroHaAmu [ Those who are remote, and those who are remotely related, shall be brought into close connection, and the ties of relationship shall be severed ]. (TA.) ― -b20- binotu TabaqK is an appellation of A female tortoise, [app. because of the cover of her back,] which, (S, O, K,) as the Arabs assert, (S, O,) lays ninety-nine eggs, all of them [ eventually ] tortoises, and lays one egg which discloses (S, O, K) a serpent (K) [or a serpent such as is termed ] an A^asowad ; (S, O;) or, accord. to Az, sixty-nine [ eggs ], and the seventieth is [ eventually ] a viper. (So in a marg. note in one of my copies of the S; in which, also, the appellation is written binotu Tabaqa , instead of binotu TabaqK .) Hence the phrase A_iHodaY banaAti TabaqK , meaning (tropical:) A calamity; (S, O, TA;) as also binotu TabaqK : (TA:) banaAtu TabaqK meaning calamities [like muTobiqaAtN ]: as well as tortoises: and serpents: (K:) and A^um~u TabaqK [in like manner] means calamity: (TA in art. Trq :) or, accord. to EthTha'álibee, Tabaqu [thus, imperfectly decl., as written in the L,) signifies a yellow serpent: (L, TA:) and A^um~u TabaqK and binotu TabaqK are said to signify the serpent, because of its coiling itself round: or banaAtu TabaqK is an appellation applied to serpents because of their winding themselves round ( lA_iTobaAqihaA ) upon him whom they bite; or, as some say, because the Haw~aA=' [q. v.] confines them beneath the lids ( A^aTobaAq ) of the baskets ( A^asofaAT ) covered with leather; or, as Z says, because they resemble the Tabaq [i. e. cover, or dish, or plate,] when they coil themselves round. (TA.)

definition: A species of tree, (S, O, K,) growing upon the mountains of Mekkeh;
sourceDefinition: A species of tree, (S, O, K,) growing upon the mountains of Mekkeh; (K;) described to AHn by some one or more of Azd-es-Saráh as being about the stature of a man in height, growing near one another, scarcely ever or never seen singly, having long, slender, green leaves, which slip [ between the fingers ] when squeezed, applied as a dressing to a fracture, which, remaining upon it, they consolidate; it has a clustered yellow flower; is not eaten by the camels, but by the sheep or goats; and grows among the rocks, with the EaroEar ; the bees eat from its flowers, and the mountain-goats also feed upon it: (O:) it is beneficial as an antidote against poisons, taken internally and applied as a dressing, and as a remedy for the mange, or scab, and the itch, and fevers of long continuance, and colic, and jaundice, and obstructions of the liver; and is very healing. (K.) [ TubaAqN , thus written by Golius, without teshdeed, is said by him to be Ocimum agreste; as on the authority of Meyd; but he has not given the syn. by which Meyd has explained it.] bayona $av~K waTub~aAqK , in a trad. of Mohammad Ibn-El-Hanafeeyeh, means in the places where grow these two species of trees; (O;) i. e. in the tracts of the mountains of Mekkeh. (TA.)

Arab. p. cxxiv.) “ mimosa gummifera; ” but it is more commonly termed an “ acacia: ” its pods are termed Eul~afN , q. v.:] a species of large trees, (S, K,) of the kind called EiDaAhN ; (S, Msb;) growing in El-Hijáz [ and Egypt and Nubia and other countries ]; the fruit of which is like that of the samurap ; having curved thorns: the places in which it grows are the interiors of valleys; and it is that species of the EDAh which is the largest in its thorns, and the hardest in respect of its wood, and the best in respect of its gum: Lth describes it as above, and says that it is the same as the A^um~u gayolaAna [and the like is said in the A]: ISh says that it is a tall tree, affording a shade in which men and camels repose, with few leaves, long and large branches, with many thorns, [ more ] than the prickles of the palm-tree, and a great trunk, which a man's arm cannot embrace; the same as the Am~ gylAn ; and grows in the mountains: AHn says that it is, of the trees called EDAh , the largest, and that which has most leaves, and the greenest, and has thick and long thorns, but these are of the least hurtful of thorns, producing no heat in the foot; it has a fruit ( baramapN ) of pleasant odour; and there is not among the trees called EDAh any that produces more gum than it, nor any more bulky; and it grows only in rugged, hard, fertile ground. (TA.) By TaloH in the Kur lvi. 28 may be meant the trees called Am~ gylAn , because they have a blossom of a very pleasant odour. (Zj.) [But see below.] ― -b2- TaloHN signifies also Banana-trees; syn. $ajaru Almawozi ; and is said [by some] to have this meaning in the Kur lvi. 28: (Zj, T, TA:) or i. q. mawozN [which some expl. as meaning the trees above-mentioned; but others as meaning the fruit of those trees ]: (Msb, K:) this, however, is said to be unknown in the [classical] language. (TA.) ― -b3- And i. q. TaloEN [generally meaning The spadix of the palmtree; but sometimes the spathe thereof ]: (K:) a dial. var. of the latter word: (S:) mentioned by ISk among words formed by the substitution of one letter for another: and this meaning, also, it is said [by some] to have in the Kur lvi. 28. (TA.) -A2- And Remains of turbid water in a watering-trough or tank. (K.) -A3- And Having the belly void of food. (K.) ― -b2- See also TaliyHN .

definition: an epithet applied to a camel.
sourceDefinition: an epithet applied to a camel. (A.) You say A_ibilN TaliHapN and TalaAHaY [the latter being the pl.] Camels having a complaint (S, A, K) of their bellies (S, K) from eating of the trees called TaloH : (S, A, K:) but [the meaning seems to be, from eating thereof immoderately, for] Aboo-Sa'eed disapproves of the phrase Abl TlAHY as meaning camels that have eaten of the TlH [ and become disordered thereby, though it appears from what is said in art. EDh that camels are sometimes disordered by eating of any of the trees called EiDaAh ], asserting it to signify camels that are fatigued, or wearied; for [he says that] the TlH do not disorder camels, but are wholesome food for them. (TA.) See also TaliyHN , in two places. ― -b2- And A^aroDN TaliHapN Land abounding with the trees called TaloH . (K.)

definition: He desired the thing;
sourceDefinition: He desired the thing; or sought it; or sought it by artful, or skilful, management: or he constrained himself to do it: or he took it, or imposed it, upon himself submissively. (TA.) You say, taTaw~aEo lih`*aA AlA^amori Hat~aY tasotaTiyEahu , (S,) and ↓ taTaAwaEo , (S, K, *) Constrain thyself to acquire ability to perform this affair until thou shalt be able to perform it. (S.) And tTw~E biAl$~aYo'i He did the thing without its being incumbent, or obligatory, on him; syn. tabar~aEa bihi . (S, O, * Msb.) mano taTaw~aEa xayorFA , in the Kur ii. 153 [and 180], means Whoso does good that is not obligatory on him: (Jel:) or does good in obedience, whether obligatory or supererogatory: or does good beyond what is obligatory on him: (Bd:) xayorFA being for bixayorK : (Bd, * Jel:) or it is an epithet qualifying an inf. n. suppressed: or the verb is made trans. as implying the meaning of A^ataY or faEalaY : (Bd:) and the Koofees, except 'Ásim, read yaT~aw~aEo , for yataTaw~aEo . (Az, * O, TA. *) [Hence,] TalaApu Alt~aTaw~uEi The supererogatory prayer; syn. Aln~aAfilapu . (O, K.) And Az says that taTaw~uEN signifies A thing that one does spontaneously, not made obligatory on him by an ordinance of God; as though it were made a subst. (TA.)

definition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. AisotiTaAEapN , (S, O, Msb,) originally AisotiTowaAEN , (O, B, TA,) i. q. A^aTaAqa [meaning He was able; and he was able to do, or accomplish, a thing, and to acquire or obtain it, and to have it, &c.]; (K, TA; [in the CK, erroneously, A^aTaAEa , which, however, correctly explains one meaning of AstTAE , as will be seen by what follows;]) the inf. n. being syn. with A_iTaAqapN , (S, O, TA,) or TaAqapN , (Msb,) and qudorapN : (Msb, TA:) but it is said peculiarly of a human being [or a rational creature], whereas ATAq is used in a general manner: (IB, TA:) and the application of the former requires a peculiar constitution of the agent, and the conception of the act, and the fitness of the object to be acted upon or effected, and the possession of an instrument when the action is instrumental as in the case of writing: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and one says also, (K,) or sometimes they said, (S, O, Msb,) AisoTaAEa (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. yasoTiyEu , (S, O, Msb,) with fet-h [to the first letter]; (Msb;) rejecting the t , deeming it difficult of utterance with the T , and disliking to incorporate it into the T because the s would then become movent, which it never is: Hamzeh (i. e. Ez-Zeiyát, TA, not Khallád, O, K, TA) read, [in the Kur xviii. 96,] famaA A@soT~aAEuwA , with idghám, combining two quiescent letters: (S, O, K:) this reading is said by Zj, as on the authority of Kh and Yoo and Sb and others, to be incorrect; but Abu-l-'Abbás Ahmad Ibn Mohammad Ibn-'Abd-El-Ghanee Ed-Dimyátee, who died in the year [of the Flight] 1116, and Ibn-El-Jezeree, and El-Háfidh Aboo-'Amr, contradict him, affirming it to be allowable: (TA:) and Akh says, (S, O,) and some of the Arabs say AisotaAEa , aor. yasotiyEu , (S, O, K,) rejecting the T ; (S, O;) which Zj holds to be not allowable in reading [the Kur-án]: (TA:) and some of the Arabs say A^asoTaAEa , aor. yusoTiyEu , [in the CK, erroneously, yasoTiyEu ,] with the disjunctive A [in the former], meaning A^aTaAEa , aor. yuTiyEu , (Akh, S, O, K,) making the s to be a substitute for the suppressed vowel of the medial radical letter of the verb [ ATAE ], (Akh, S, O,) for, as is said by Kh and Sb, A^aTaAEa is originally A^aTowaEa ; (TA;) or, as AZ says, the verb in this case, with damm to the aor., is likened to A^afoEala , aor. yufoEilu , inf. n. A_ifoEaAlN : (Msb:) but Zj says that he who reads famaA A@saT~aAEuwA errs; for the s of AisotafoEala is never movent: and Sb mentions maA A^asotatiyEu ; holding it to be an instance of substitution. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 4. Some say that halo yasotaTiyEu rab~uka A^ano yunaz~ila EalayonaA maAy^idapF mina Als~amaA='i , in the Kur [v. 112], means halo yujiybu [i. e. Will thy Lord consent, or comply with the desire, that He should send down to us a table with food upon it from Heaven? ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) ― -b3- and Ks read halo tasotaTiyEu rab~aka , meaning Wilt thou demand of thy Lord that He consent, or comply with the desire? (O, TA:) for AstTAEhu signifies also He demanded his obedience, and his consent, or compliance with what he desired of him. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ TaAEN , (O, K,) and some say ↓ TaAEK , formed from TaAy^iEN by transposition, (O,) and ↓ Tay~iEN , signify the same, (S, O, Msb, K,) i. e. Being, or becoming, submissive; [or, simply, submissive; and obeying; or obedient; ] (Msb;) and ↓ TawoEN , originally an inf. n., is likewise used as syn. with TaAy^iEN : (Ham p. 408:) the pl. is Tuw~aEN , (S, O, K,) i. e. pl. of TaAy^iEN , (S, O,) and TaAEapN is [also a pl. of TaAy^iEN , like as baAEapN is of baAy^iEN ; or] syn. with muTiyEuwna : (TA in art. swE :) [whence one says, daxala fiY TaAEatihi , and xaraja mino TaAEatihi , He entered among, and he quitted, his obeyers, or those who obeyed him; i. e. he became obedient, and he became disobedient, to him: ] and ↓ miTowaAEN , (S, O, K,) pl. maTaAwiyEu , (TA,) is [app., agreeably with analogy, an intensive epithet, meaning very submissive or obedient, but is said to be, in like manner,] syn. with muTiyEN , (S, O, K,) applied to a man: (S, O:) and ↓ miTowaAEapN , applied to a man, [is app. a doubly intensive epithet; or] is syn. with miTowaAEN : (TA:) and is applied to a pl. number, as meaning compliant and submissive. (Har p. 237.) One says, jaA='a fulaAnN TaAy^iEFA Such a one came [ submissively, or obediently, or willingly, ] not being compelled against his will. (S, O.) And a poet says, Halafotu biAlbayoti wamaA Hawolahu ↓ mino EaAy^i*K biAlbayoti A^awoTaAEi [ I swore, or have sworn, by the House of God (i. e. the Kaabeh), and what are around it, of such as betakes himself for refuge to the House or of such as renders obedience by visiting it]. (O.) And one says also, ↓ jaA='a Tay~iEFA [ He came of his own accord, or willingly ]. (M and TA voce *uw .) And All~isaAni ↓ Tay~iEu (tropical:) A man chaste, or eloquent, in speech. (TA.) And AlqiyaAdi ↓ naAqapN Tay~iEapu and AlqiyaAdi ↓ TawoEu (assumed tropical:) A she-camel that is gentle; [or tractable; ] that does not contend with her leader. (TA.) And AlEinaAni ↓ farasN TawoEu (tropical:) A traciable horse. (S, O, K, TA.) And yadika ↓ fulaAnN TawoEu (tropical:) Such a one is submissive to thy hand. (S, O, K, TA.) And AlD~ajiyEi ↓ AimoraA^apN TawoEu A woman submissive to the bedfellow. (TA.) And fulaAnN AlmakaArihi ↓ TawoEu (assumed tropical:) Such a one is submissive to misfortunes, [ being ] subject thereto. (T, TA.) [See also an ex. of ↓ TawoE in a verse cited in art. $mt voce $aAmitapN .] Als~inaAni ↓ huwa A^aTowaEu means (assumed tropical:) He is one to whom the spear-head is subservient, howsoever he will. (K in art. sn .)

definition: A supererogator in any good act.
sourceDefinition: A supererogator in any good act. (O, K.) One says, faEalahu mutaTaw~iEFA [ He did it without its being incumbent, or obligatory, on him; supererogatorily: or gratuitously, unasked, or unbidden: or disinterestedly; not seeking, or desiring, a compensation: syn. mutabar~iEFA ]. (S and K in art. brE .) And ↓ AlmuT~aw~iEapu means Those who exceed what is obligatory on them in fighting, or warring, against unbelievers or the like; (S, O, Msb;) originally AlmutaTaw~iEapu : (Msb:) hence ↓ AlmuT~aw~iEiyna in the Kur ix. 80; originally AlmutaTaw~iEiyna . (S, O.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EaborN and EubuwrN , [the latter of which is the more common,] (S, O, Msb, K,) He crossed it, went across it, or passed over it, (Mgh, Msb, K,) from one side thereof to the other; (Msb, K;) namely, a river, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, *) and a valley, (K, TA,) &c. (S, Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Eabara bihi AlmaA='a : see 2. ― -b3- Eabara Als~abiyla , (Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. EubuwrN , (TA,) He travelled, or passed along, the way, or road; (Msb, K; *) as though he cut it, or furrowed it. (K, * TK.) ― -b4- And hence, (TA,) Eabara , (aor. as above, S,) (tropical:) He died: (S, O, Msb, K:) as though he travelled the road of life: or, as F says in the B, as though he crossed over the bridge of the present world or life. (TA.) A poet says, faA_ino naEoburo faA_in~a lanaA lumaAtK waA_ino nagoburo fanaHonu EalaY nu*uwri i. e. (tropical:) So if we die, there are others like to us; and if we remain alive, we are waiting for that which must necessarily come to pass, as though we were bound by vows to meet it. (S, O.) ― -b5- And Eabarati Als~aHaAy^ibu , aor. as above, inf. n. EubuwrN , The clouds travelled, or passed along, quickly. (TA.) -A2- Eabara Alr~uw^oyaA : see 2, in two places. ― -b2- And [hence, perhaps,] Eabarotu AlT~ayora , aor. and , (O, K,) inf. n. EaborN , (TA,) i. q. zajarotuhaA [ I augured from the flight, or alighting-places, or cries, &c., of the birds; or I made the birds to fly away in order that I might augur from their flight, &c.]. (O, K.) ― -b3- And Eabara AlkitaAta , aor. , inf. n. EaborN , (As, S, A, * O, K, *) He meditated upon, endeavouring to understand it, or he considered, examined, or studied, (As, S, O, K,) or he read mentally, (A,) the book, or writing, not raising his voice in doing so, (As, S, A, O, K,) i. e. in reading it. (K.) And you say, baEoDa ↓ AiEotabara AlkitaAbi bibaEoDK , meaning Eabarahu [i. e. He considered and compared one part of the book, or writing, with another part, in order to understand it ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And Eabara AlmataAEa , and Ald~araAhima , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaborN , (TA,) He examined what was the weight of the goods, and of the dirhems, and what they were. (K, TA.) And you say, Ald~araAhima fawajadotuhaA A^alofFA ↓ AiEotabarotu , meaning EabarotuhaA , i. e. I tried, or examined, the dirhems, and found them to be a thousand. (Msb.) ― -b5- See also 8, second sentence. -A3- Eabira , with kesr, aor. , inf. n. EabarN ; (S;) or Eabara , inf. n. EaborN ; (K;) [but the former seems to be the more correct, as will be seen from what follows;] and ↓ AstEbr ; (A, O, K;) He shed tears; his eyes, or eye, watered. (S, A, K, TA.) And Eabirato Eayonuhu His eye shed tears, or watered; (S, O;) as also ↓ AstEbrt . (S.) ― -b2- And Eabira , aor. , inf. n. EabarN ; (AZ, T, O, * L, TA;) or Eabara , inf. n. EaborN ; (K; [but see above;]) He grieved, or mourned; was sorrowful, sad, or unhappy. (AZ, T, O, L, K, TA.) maA lahu sahira waEabira [ What aileth him? May he be sleepless by night, and may he grieve, or mourn: ] is a form of imprecation against a man, used by the Arabs. (TA.) And Eabirato , inf. n. EabarN , means She became bereft of her child, or children, by death. (A.) [See EuborN .]

EibaArapN (S, A, O, Msb, K) and EaborN ; (A, Msb, K;) He interpreted, or explained, the dream, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) and told its final sequel or result: (A, O, K:) or the former verb has an intensive signification: (Msb:) and taEobiyrN has a more particular [or more restricted] meaning than taA^owiylN : it is said to be from Eabara AlkitaAba [q. v.]; or, as some say, it is from EiborN signifying the “ side ” of a river, because the interpreter of the dream considers the two sides thereof, and meditates upon every particular of it from its beginning to its end. (TA.) In the phrase of the Kur [xii. 43], A_ino kunotumo lilr~uw^oyaA ↓ taEoburuwna , the l is termed laAmu Alt~aEoqiybi [the l of succedaneousness], because it is succedaneous to the connection termed A_iDaAfap [i. e. the phrase is succedaneous to A_ino kunotumo EaAbiriY Alr~uw^oyaA If ye be interpreters of the dream ]: (O, TA:) or it is inserted as an explicative: (Zj, TA:) the phrase is similar to A_ino kunota lilomaAli jaAmiEFA . (S, O.) ― -b2- Eb~r Eam~aA fiY nafosihi , (A, K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He declared, spoke out clearly or plainly, or explained, what was in his mind. (A, * K, * TA.) (S, O, TA.) -A3- Eb~r bihi , (K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) signifies A^araAhu Eubora Eayonihi (K, TA, in the CK Eayonayohi ,) i. e. He showed him what would make his eye to weep: or what would make his eye hot. (TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, EalaY malaqiy~aAtK yuEab~irona bAlgufori [ Upon swiftly-running mares that show the mountain kids, in the swiftness of their pace, what makes their eyes to weep from envy]. (TA.) And you say also, Eb~r Eayonayohi , meaning He made his eyes to weep. (TA.) ― -b2- Also He destroyed him: (K, TA:) as though he showed him what would make his eye to weep, or make it hot. (TA.) ― -b3- And He caused him to fall into difficulty, or distress. (A.) And It (an affair, or event,) was, or became, difficult, or distressing, to him. (O, K.)

definition: He became admonished, or reminded;
sourceDefinition: He became admonished, or reminded; he took warning, or example: in this sense the verb is used in the Kur lix. 2: and you say, AiEotabara bimaA maDaY He became admonished or reminded, or he took warning or example, by what passed: (Msb:) and Als~aEiydu mina A@Eotabara bigayorihi waAl$~aqiY~u mani A@Eotabara bihi gayoruhu [ The fortunate is he who takes warning by others, and the unfortunate is he by whom others take warning ]. (Kull p. 60.) And EabarN [as inf. n. of ↓ Eabira , aor. ,] signifies the same as AiEotibaArN [as inf. n. of AiEotabara in the sense expl. above]: (Fr, O, L, K, TA:) whence the saying of the Arabs, Aall~`hum~a A@joEalonaA mim~ano yaEobaru Ald~unoyaA walaA yaEoburuhaA , (Fr, O, L, TA,) with fet-h to the b of yEbr in the first case, and with damm to it in the second case, (TA,) meaning O God, make us to be of those who take warning, or example, by the present world, and do not [ pass through it or] die quickly, or soon, until they content Thee by obedience: (Fr, O, L, TA:) in the copies of the K, mim~ano yaEoburu Ald~unoyaA walaA yaEomuruhaA , the former verb with b [and damm], and the latter with m [and damm]: and in the A is given, as a trad., AuEoburuwA Ald~unoyaA walaA taEomuruwhaA : but the reading given by Sgh and in the L is pronounced by MF to be the right. (TA.) See also EiborapN . [And see 10, last sentence.] ― -b2- Also He took, or regarded, what he witnessed, or saw, or beheld, as an indication, or evidence, of what was concealed from him: (O:) he compared what was unapparent with what was apparent [ and so judged of the former from analogy ]: or he considered the essential properties of things, and their modes of indication, in order that, by the consideration thereof, another thing, of their kind, might become known. (Kull p. 60.) See, again, EiborapN . Ibn-Seereen used to say, A^aEotabiru AlHadiyva [ I judge by comparison with what has been transmitted by tradition from the Prophet]; meaning I interpret a dream according to what has been transmitted by tradition, like as I do according to the Kur-án; as when a crow is interpreted as meaning an unrighteous man, and a rib as meaning a woman, in imitation of forms of speech used by the Prophet. (O, * TA.) ― -b3- See also 1, latter half, in two places. ― -b4- Also He accounted, or esteemed, or regarded, a thing, in respect of predicamental order. (Msb.) See, again, EiborapN . ― -b5- [And He esteemed a person, or thing; held him, or it, in high estimation or regard. ― -b6- And He took a thing into account, regarded it, or included it in a mental view or an examination. Hence the phrase biA@EotibaAri ka*aA With regard, or respect, or with regard had, to such a thing; in consideration of such a thing, or of the implication thereof; and having regard, or respect, to such a thing; as also AiEotibaArFA lika*aA and bika*aA . And biA@EotibaArK waAHidK Considered in one respect; in one and the same light. Hence also the phrase,] yuEotabaru ka*aA liSiH~api AlEaqodi Such a thing is made a condition [or is taken into account ] for the soundness, or validity, of the contract. (Msb.) ― -b7- AEtbr minohu means He wondered at him, or it. (K, TA. In the CK, mnh is omitted.)

sourceDefinition: : see EibaArapN . -A2- Also A tear: (TA:) or a tear before it overflows: or a [ sobbing, or] reiteration [ of the sound ] of weeping in the bosom: (A, K:) or an overflowing of tears without the sound of weeping: (TA:) or a flowing, or an oozing, of tears: (S, O:) or grief without weeping: (A, K:) pl. EabaraAtN (O, K) and ↓ EabarN , (so in the O, [but this, if correct, is a quasi-pl. n.,]) or EibarN . (Thus in copies of the K.) Of the first meaning, the following is an ex.: waA_in~a $ifaAy^iY EaborapN lawo safaHotuhaA [ And verily my cure would be a tear if I shed it ]: and of the last, the following is an ex.: laka maA A^abokiY walaA Eaborapa biY or, as some relate it, wlA Ebrp liY ; and the meaning is, For thy sake I weep, but there is grief in me for myself: so says As: (TA:) or in this saying, which is a prov., mA may be redundant, or it may be what is termed maSodariy~ap ; and the meaning is, For thee I weep, or for thee is my weeping, I [myself] having no need of weeping. (Meyd.)

sourceDefinition: a subst. from AlAiEotibaAru ; An admonition, or exhortation: (Bd in iii. 11): an admonition, or exhortation, by which one takes warning or example: (Jel in xxiii. 21:) a thing by the state, or condition, of which one is admonished, or reminded, and guided, or directed: (Bd in xxiii. 21:) i. q. ↓ AiEotibaArN [lit. a being admonished, or reminded, &c.; but meaning a cause of being admonished, &c.; i. e. a warning, or an example ]: (Jel in xvi. 68:) or AiEotibaArN bimaA maDaY i. e. Ait~EaAZN and ta*ak~urN [meaning, in like manner, a cause of being admonished, or reminded, by what has passed ]: (Msb:) an indication, or evidence, (Bd and Jel in xxiv. 44, and Bd in xvi. 68,) whereby one passes from ignorance to knowledge: (Bd in xvi. 68:) a state [ of things or circumstances ] whereby, from the knowledge of what is seen, one arrives at the knowledge of what is not seen; as also ↓ AiEotibaArN : (B, TA:) and a wonderful thing [app. such as serves as a warning or an example ]: (A, K:) pl. EibarN . (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- And The account, or estimation, or regard, in which a thing is held in respect of predicamental order; as also ↓ AiEotibaArN . (Msb.) [Hence the common phrase laA Eiborapa bihi , meaning No regard is due to it. ] -A2- See also EibaArapN .

sourceDefinition: , applied to the [species of lote-tree called] sidor , means That grows on the banks of rivers, and becomes large: (S, O:) an anomalous rel. n. from EiborN : (TA:) [or a regular rel. n. from EuborN as syn. with EiborN :] or, accord. to 'Omárah, such as is large in the leaves, having few thorns, and taller than the DaAl : or, as Aboo-Ziyád says, that has no thorns except such as hurt [ not (see sidorN )]; the thorns [that hurt] being of the sidor called DAl : he does not say, as others do, that it is that which grows upon the water: some assert that it is also called EumoriY~N , the b being changed into m : (O:) or, as some say, such as has no trunk; and such is only of those that are near to the Eibor [or bank of a river ]: Yaakoob says that the terms EuboriY~ and EumoriY~ are applied to the sidor that imbibes water; and that such as does not this is that of the desert, and is the DAl : AZ says that the sdr , and such as is large of the Eawosaj , are called EuboriY~N ; and EumoriY~N is applied to the sdr that is old. (TA.) [See also EumoriY~N .]

sourceDefinition: A certain mixture (As, S, O, Msb, K) of perfumes, (Msb, K,) compounded with saffron: (As, S, O:) or, (K,) with the Arabs (S, O, TA) of the Time of Ignorance, (TA,) accord. to AO, it means saffron (S, O, K, TA) alone: but in a trad., mention is made of smearing with Ebyr or with saffron; and this shows Ebyr to be different from saffron: (S, O, TA:) IAth says that it is a sort of perfume, having colour, compounded of certain mixtures. (TA.) [See a verse cited voce *abiyHN ; and another cited voce raqoraqa .]

sourceDefinition: A wayfarer; a passenger; a person passing along a way or road; (S, O, TA;) a traveller: (TA:) or one who passes through without abiding: (Mgh:) pl. EaAbiruw sabiylK and Eub~aAru sabiylK . (TA.) And EaAbiru Als~abiyli The wayfarer; the passer along the way or road. (Msb.) A_il~aA EaAbiriY sabiylK , in the Kur [iv. 46], means Except those who, wanting something in the mosque, and their houses or tents being distant, [merely pass through, or] enter the mosque and go forth quickly: (TA:) or except travellers; for the traveller sometimes wants water [which is found in the mosque]: or, as some say, except passers through the mosque, not meaning to pray. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- Hence EaAbirN signifies (tropical:) Dying, or dead. (TA. [See 1.]) ― -b3- [And Passing, or having currency. Hence,] lugapN EaAbirapN An allowable form of word or expression: (S, K, TA:) from Eabara signifying “ he passed over ” a river. (TA.) -A2- EaAbirN also signifies Examining a thing: examining a book, or writing, and considering and comparing one part of it with another, so as to understand it. (TA.) -A3- Also Shedding tears, (S, O, *) applied to a man, and likewise to a woman: and ↓ EuboraAnu weeping, applied to a man; and so [its fem.] ↓ EaboraY applied to a woman: (S, O:) or ↓ EaboraAnu signifies weeping and grieving, applied to a man; as also ↓ EabirN ; (K, * TA;) and EaAbirN and ↓ EaboraY and ↓ EabirapN are applied to a woman in the same sense, (K,) or as meaning grieving: (TA:) pl. [of ↓ EaboraAnu and EaboraY ] EabaAraY , (K, TA,) like sakaAraY : (TA:) and EayonN ↓ EaboraY means a weeping eye. (O, K, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EadolN (S, * O, * Msb, K, * TA) and maEodilapN (S, * O, * Msb, K *) and maEodalapN (S, * Msb, K *) and EadaAlapN and EuduwlapN , (K, * TK,) He acted equitably, justly, or rightly. (S, O, Msb, K.) So in the phrase Eadala fiY A^amorihi , [ He acted equitably, &c., in his affair, ] inf. n. EadolN . (Msb.) And so in the phrase Eadala Ealayohi fiY AlqaDiy~api [ He acted equitably, &c., towards him in the judgment ]: (S, O:) and Eadala EalaY Alqawomi , [ he acted equitably, &c., towards the people, or party, ] inf. n. EadolN and maEodilapN and maEodalapN . (Msb.) lano tasotaTiyEuwA A^ano taEodiluwA bayona Aln~isaA='i , [ Ye will not be able to act with perfect equity between women ], in the Kur [iv. 128], is said to mean, in respect of love, and of jimaAE . (TA.) [See also EadolN below.] ― -b2- waA_ino taEodilo kul~a EadolK , in the Kur [vi. 69], means And if it would ransom with every [degree of] ransoming: (T, S, O, Msb, TA:) AO used to say, and if it would act equitably with every [degree of] equitable acting; but Az says that this is a blunder. (TA.) [See, again, EadolN below.] ― -b3- [ Eadala signifies also He declined, deviated, or turned aside or away; and particularly from the right course: thus having a meaning nearly agreeing with that assigned to Eadila in the last sentence of this paragraph.] balo humo qawomN yaEodiluwna , in the Kur [xxvii. 61], means [ Nay but they are a people ] who decline, or deviate, from the truth, and from the right course; i. e., who disbelieve. (O.) And one says, Eadala Eanohu , aor. , inf. n. EadolN and [more com- monly] EuduwlN , He declined, deviated, or turned aside or away, from him, or it. (K.) And Eadala Eani AlT~ariyqi , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. EuduwlN , (Msb,) He declined, &c., from the road, or way; (S, O, Msb;) as also Eanohu ↓ AnEdl . (S, O, K. *) And Eadala AlT~ariyqu The road declined, or deflected. (K.) And Eadala AlfaHolu (S, O, K) Eani AlA_ibili (S, O) The stallion left, left off, or desisted from, covering the she-camels; (S, O, K; *) and so Eani AlD~iraAbi ↓ AnEdl . (TA.) [ Eadala AlfaHola see in what follows.] And Eadala A_ilayohi , inf. n. EuduwlN , He returned to him, or it. (K.) -A2- Eadalahu : see 2, in two places. ― -b2- Eadala fulaAnFA bifulaAnK He made such a one to be equal, or like, to such a one; (K;) [and] so bh ↓ EAdlhu : (S:) or, accord. to some, AlEadolu signifies the rating a thing as equal to a thing of another kind so as to make it like the latter. (TA.) One says, Eadalotu h`*aA bih`*aA I made this to be like and to stand in the stead of, this. (Msb.) And Eadala birab~ihi , (El-Ahmar, TA,) aor. , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. EadolN and EuduwlN , [ gayorahu being understood,] He made another to be equal with his Lord, and worshipped him. (El-Ahmar, TA.) birab~ihimo yaEodiluwna , in the Kur [vi. 151, and accord. to some in vi. 1], means Attributing a copartner, or copartners, to their Lord. (O. [And the like is said in the S and Msb and TA.]) ― -b3- Eadalotu A^amotiEapa Albayoti I made the goods, or furniture, of the house, or tent, into equal loads, [ so as to counterbalance one another, ] on the day of departure, or removal. (TA.) And bayona Al$~ayoy^ayoni ↓ EaAdala (S, O, TA) He made an equiponderance to subsist between the two things. (TA.) ― -b4- fulaAnN yaEodilu fulaAnFA Such a one is equal to such a one. (TA.) And yaEodiluhu He, or it, is like him, or it. (Fr, S, O.) [Hence] one says, maA yaEodiluka EinodanaA $aYo'N Nothing stands with us in thy stead. (TA.) And Eadalahu , aor. , (K,) inf. n. EadolN , (TA,) It was, or became, equiponderant to it; as also ↓ EAdlhu , (K,) inf. n. muEaAdalapN . (TA.) And [hence] Eadalahu fiY AlmaHomili , (K,) and ↓ EAdlhu , (TA,) He rode with him in the [ vehicle called ] mHml [ so as to counterbalance him ]. (K, TA.) ― -b5- And Eadala , aor. , inf. n. EadolN , signifies also He turned a thing from its course, direction, or manner of being. (TA.) You say, Eadalotu fulaAnFA Eano Tariyqihi I turned such a one from his road, or way. (TA.) And laA tuEodalu saAriHatukumo Your pasturing cattle shall not be turned away, nor prevented, from pasturing. (TA, from a trad.) And Eadala AlfaHola (K, TA) Eani AlD~iraAbi (TA) He removed the stallion, or made him to withdraw [or desist ], from covering. (K, TA.) And Eadalotu Ald~aAb~apa A_ilaY mawoDiEi ka*aA I turned the beast to such a place. (TA.) [See also two meanings assigned to this verb in the next paragraph, third sentence.] -A3- Eadula , [aor. ,] inf. n. EadaAlapN (S, O, Msb) and EuduwlapN , (Msb,) He (a man, S, O, i. e. a witness, Msb) was, or became, such as is termed Eadol [q. v.]. (S, O, Msb.) -A4- Eadila , aor. , inf. n. EadalN , He acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically. (Msb.)

definition: , inf. n. taEodiylN , i. q. A^aqaAmahu , (K,) meaning He made it to be conformable with that which is right; (TK;) namely, a judgment, or judicial decision. (K, TK.) ― -b2- He made it straight, or...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taEodiylN , i. q. A^aqaAmahu , (K,) meaning He made it to be conformable with that which is right; (TK;) namely, a judgment, or judicial decision. (K, TK.) ― -b2- He made it straight, or even; namely, a thing; as, for instance, an arrow; (TA;) right, or in a right condition; direct, or rightly directed; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) and so ↓ Eadalahu . (O, K.) Hence, faEad~alaka and ↓ faEadalaka , accord. to different readers, in the Kur [lxxxii. 7, which I would rather render And hath made thee symmetrical ]: (O:) or the latter means and hath turned thee from unbelief to belief; (IAar, O, TA;) or, accord. to Fr, and hath turned thee to whatever form He pleased, beautiful or ugly, tall or short: but Az says that the former reading was the more pleasing to Fr, and is the better. (TA.) ― -b3- He made it equal; (Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) namely, a pair of scales, or a weight, (K, TA,) and a measure, &c. (TA.) Hence, qisomapu Alt~aEodiyli i. e. The division of a thing [ in an equal manner ] with regard to the value and utility, not with regard to the quantity, so that the smaller portion may be equal to the larger portion in value and utility. sourceDefinition: see 1, in four places. One says, yuEaAdilu fiY Alwazoni [ It is equal in weight; is equiponderant ]. (IF, Msb.) And yuEaAdiluka fiY Alwazoni waAlqadori [ He is equal to thee in weight and in size: as one who rides with thee in a maHomil ]. (S.) yuEaAdiluhu fiY Alqiymapi waAlmanofaEapi [ It is equal to it in value and utility ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- And EaAdalahumaA EalaY naADiHK He bound them two upon the two sides of a camel [or of a camel used for carrying water for irrigation, so that they counterbalanced each other ] like the [ two loads called ] EidolaAni . (TA.) ― -b3- And fulaAnN yuEaAdilu A^amorahu , and yuqas~imuhu , (O, and so accord. to a copy of the S,) or EadaAlN , (so in another copy of the S,) inf. n. yuEaAdilu h`*aA AlA^amora , Such a one wavers, or vacillates, [ in his case ] between two affairs, hesitating which of them he shall do. (S, O.) And EAdl A^amorahu taEodiylN He is in a state of entanglement in this affair, and does not execute it: (K:) he is in doubt respecting it. (TA.) And EAdl A^amorahu He paused [ in his case ], hesitating between two affairs, which he should do; as also ↓ Ed~lhu inf. n. taEodiylN : and hence, in the trad. of the miEoraAj [or ladder by which Mohammad is related to have ascended from Jerusalem to Heaven], ↓ faEad~alotu bayonahumaA [ And I paused in hesitation between them two ]; meaning that they were equal in his estimation, and he could not make choice of either of them. AlmuEaAdalapu is The doubting respecting two affairs: and one says, A^anaA fiY EidaAlK mino h`*aA AlA^amori I am in doubt respecting this affair, whether I should do it or leave it undone: (TA:) or AlEidaAlu is the considering deliberately respecting the case of two affairs that have occurred to one, when one knows not to which of them he should betake himself. (IAar, K.) And The case of one person's saying “ There is in it something remaining ” and another's saying “ There is not in it anything remaining. ” (S, O.) And one says, when he wavers, or vacillates, between two affairs, hesitating which of them he shall do, and then a right opinion occurs to him, and he determines upon that which is the more fit in his estimation, qaTaEotu AlEidaAla fiY A^amoriY wamaDayotu EalaY EazomiY [ I cut short wavering in my affair, and executed my determination ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And EAdl signifies also It became crooked, or bent. (K.)

definition: It was, or became, right, or in a right condition;
sourceDefinition: It was, or became, right, or in a right condition; direct, or rightly directed; straight, or even; (S, O, Msb, TA;) equal; (as a pair of scales, or a weight, and a measure, &c.; TA;) equable, or uniform; (Msb, TA;) [ symmetrical, proportionate, ] suitable in itself [or in its parts ]. (K.) The saying, cited by Sh, waA@Eotadalato *aAtu Als~anaAmi AlA^amoyali means And she that had an inclining hump became straight [ and erect ] in her hump by reason of fatness. (TA.) And one says jaAriyapN Hasanapu AlAiEotidaAli A girl, or young woman, goodly in respect of stature [or proportion ]. (A, TA.) And AEtdl Al$~iEoru The poetry, or verse, was, or became, measured, and right in its feet. (TA.) ― -b2- Also It was, or became, of a middling sort, in quantity, or quality; (K, TA;) as a body between tallness and shortness, and water between the hot and the cold; and [ moderate, or temperate, ] as a day of which the air is pleasant. (TA.)

definition: Equity, justice, or rectitude;
sourceDefinition: Equity, justice, or rectitude; contr. of jaworN ; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) i. e. i. q. qaSodN , in affairs; (Msb;) and qisoTN ; (S, M, Mgh, &c., in art. qsT ;) and sawiy~apN ; (O, K;) and AisotiqaAmapN ; (IAar, K;) and a thing that is established in the minds as being right; (K, TA;) as also ↓ maEodilapN (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ maEodalapN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ EadaAlapN and ↓ EuduwlapN : (K:) or, as some say, it is the mean between excess and falling short: and Er-Rághib says, it is of two sorts: one is absolute, such that reason requires the inference of its goodness; and this will not at any time be abrogated, nor described as a mode of transgression; as the doing good to him who does good to thee, and the abstaining from harming him who abstains from harming thee: and the other is such as is known to be Eadol by the law; and this may be abrogated sometimes; as retaliation, and fines for wounds and maimings, and the taking the property of the apostate; and this is what is meant by the saying in the Kur [xvi. 92], A_in~a A@ll~`ha yaA^omuru biA@loEadoli waA@loA_iHosaAni i. e. [ Verily God commandeth ] equality in recompensing, if good, with good, and if evil, with evil, and the requiting of good with more good, and of evil with less evil: [see also 4 in art. Hsn :] and he says of ↓ EadaAlapN and ↓ maEodilapN , that each is a term requiring the inference of equality, and is used with a regard to correlation. (TA.) One says, basaTa AlwaAliY Eadolahu and ↓ maEodilatahu (S, O) and ↓ maEodalatahu (S) [ The governor, or ruler, largely extended his equity, or justice ]. And ↓ fulaAnN mino A^aholi AlmaEodalapi , (S,) or ↓ AlmaEodilapi , (O,) i. e. mn Ahl AlEadoli [ Such a one is of the people of equity, &c.]. (S, O.) waA^a$ohiduwA *awaYo EadolK minokumo , in the Kur [lxv. 2], is said by Sa'eed Ibn-El-Museiyib to mean *awaYo EaqolK [i. e. And make ye to be witnesses two persons of intelligence from among you: but this rendering I think questionable]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Repayment, requital, compensation, or recompense. (K.) ― -b3- And Ransom, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) when regard is had therein to the meaning of equality, or equivalence. (TA.) This is [said to be] the meaning in the phrase of the Kur [v. 96], A^awo Eadolu *`lika SiyaAmFA [ Or the ransom thereof by fasting: but this is generally expl. as meaning or the like thereof of fasting; (see EidolN ;) i. e., in lieu of feeding a number of poor men, one shall fast the like number of days]. (S, O.) And so [accord. to some] in the saying, occurring in a trad., laA yuqobalu minohu SarofN walaA EadolN [of which see various explanations (including three renderings here following) in art. Srf ]. (O, Msb.) ― -b4- And Measure; syn. kayolN . (K.) So in the phrase A^aEoTaAhu biAlEadoli [ He gave him by measure ]. (TK.) ― -b5- And An obligatory act or divine ordinance. (En-Nadr, O, K.) ― -b6- And A supererogatory act. (O, K.) -A2- Also One who acts equitably, justly, or rightly; and so ↓ EaAdilN : (K, TA:) or the latter signifies thus: (S, O:) and the former [particularly] signifies a man approved and satisfactory in testimony; originally an inf. n.; (S, O, TA;) whose testimony is approved and available; (Msb;) a man whose testimony is allowable, or legally admissible, as also ↓ EaAdilN ; a man whose saying, and whose judgment, or judicial decision, are approved; and, accord. to Ibráheem, one from whom a thing occasioning doubt, or suspicion, or evil opinion, has not appeared: being originally an inf. n., it means *uw EadolK : or, accord. to IJ, it is an intensive epithet, as though meaning possessing every kind of Eadol : (TA:) one says rajulN EadolN , (S, O, Msb, * K,) and AimoraA^apN EadolN and EadolapN , (Msb, K,) the latter mentioned by IJ, (TA,) and rajulaAni EadolN and EadolaAni , (Msb, * TA,) and qawomN EadolN (S, O, Msb, * K) and nisowapN EadolN (TA) and qawomN EuduwlN , (S, O, Msb, * K,) EuduwlN being pl. of EadolN , (S, O, Msb,) or of EaAdilN , (K,) and EadolN used in a pl. sense being a quasi-pl. n. of EaAdilN , (M, K,) like tajorN [of taAjirN ] and $arobN [of $aAribN ]; (M, TA;) or rijaAlN EadolN and nisowapN EadolN mean rijaAlN *awuw EadolK and nisowaAnN *awaAtu EadolK . (TA.) ― -b2- AlEadolu as one of the names of God means He whom desire does not cause to incline, or decline, so that he should deviate from the right course in judgment. (TA.) ― -b3- And one says, h`*aA EadolN bayonahumaA , meaning This is intermediate in quality between them two, not in the utmost degree of goodness nor in the extreme degree of badness. (Mgh.) And makaAnN EadolN bayona fariyqayoni [ A place equidistant, or midway, between two parties ]. (S in art. swY .) ― -b4- See also EidolN , throughout the greater part of the paragraph. -A3- EadolN is also the name of a certain chief of the [body of armed men called] $uraT , (S, O,) or $uroTap , (K,) of a tub~aE [or King of El-Yemen], who, when he desired the slaughter of a man, delivered him to this person; (S, O, K;) whereupon the people said, wuDiEa EalaY yadaYo EadolK [ He has been consigned to the hands of 'Adl ]; (S, O;) and this was afterwards said of anything of which one despaired. (S, O, K.) [Meyd mentions EalaY yadaYo EadolK , as a prov., without wuDiEa : see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 80.]

Hsn :] and he says of ↓ EadaAlapN and ↓ maEodilapN , that each is a term requiring the inference of equality, and is used with a regard to correlation. (TA.) One says, basaTa AlwaAliY Eadolahu and ↓ maEodilatahu (S, O) and ↓ maEodalatahu (S) [ The governor, or ruler, largely extended his equity, or justice ]. And ↓ fulaAnN mino A^aholi AlmaEodalapi , (S,) or ↓ AlmaEodilapi , (O,) i. e. mn Ahl AlEadoli [ Such a one is of the people of equity, &c.]. (S, O.) waA^a$ohiduwA *awaYo EadolK minokumo , in the Kur [lxv. 2], is said by Sa'eed Ibn-El-Museiyib to mean *awaYo EaqolK [i. e. And make ye to be witnesses two persons of intelligence from among you: but this rendering I think questionable]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Repayment, requital, compensation, or recompense. (K.) ― -b3- And Ransom, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) when regard is had therein to the meaning of equality, or equivalence. (TA.) This is [said to be] the meaning in the phrase of the Kur [v. 96], A^awo Eadolu *`lika SiyaAmFA [ Or the ransom thereof by fasting: but this is generally expl. as meaning or the like thereof of fasting; (see EidolN ;) i. e., in lieu of feeding a number of poor men, one shall fast the like number of days]. (S, O.) And so [accord. to some] in the saying, occurring in a trad., laA yuqobalu minohu SarofN walaA EadolN [of which see various explanations (including three renderings here following) in art. Srf ]. (O, Msb.) ― -b4- And Measure; syn. kayolN . (K.) So in the phrase A^aEoTaAhu biAlEadoli [ He gave him by measure ]. (TK.) ― -b5- And An obligatory act or divine ordinance. (En-Nadr, O, K.) ― -b6- And A supererogatory act. (O, K.) -A2- Also One who acts equitably, justly, or rightly; and so ↓ EaAdilN : (K, TA:) or the latter signifies thus: (S, O:) and the former [particularly] signifies a man approved and satisfactory in testimony; originally an inf. n.; (S, O, TA;) whose testimony is approved and available; (Msb;) a man whose testimony is allowable, or legally admissible, as also ↓ EaAdilN ; a man whose saying, and whose judgment, or judicial decision, are approved; and, accord. to Ibráheem, one from whom a thing occasioning doubt, or suspicion, or evil opinion, has not appeared: being originally an inf. n., it means *uw EadolK : or, accord. to IJ, it is an intensive epithet, as though meaning possessing every kind of Eadol : (TA:) one says rajulN EadolN , (S, O, Msb, * K,) and AimoraA^apN EadolN and EadolapN , (Msb, K,) the latter mentioned by IJ, (TA,) and rajulaAni EadolN and EadolaAni , (Msb, * TA,) and qawomN EadolN (S, O, Msb, * K) and nisowapN EadolN (TA) and qawomN EuduwlN , (S, O, Msb, * K,) EuduwlN being pl. of EadolN , (S, O, Msb,) or of EaAdilN , (K,) and EadolN used in a pl. sense being a quasi-pl. n. of EaAdilN , (M, K,) like tajorN [of taAjirN ] and $arobN [of $aAribN ]; (M, TA;) or rijaAlN EadolN and nisowapN EadolN mean rijaAlN *awuw EadolK and nisowaAnN *awaAtu EadolK . (TA.) ― -b2- AlEadolu as one of the names of God means He whom desire does not cause to incline, or decline, so that he should deviate from the right course in judgment. (TA.) ― -b3- And one says, h`*aA EadolN bayonahumaA , meaning This is intermediate in quality between them two, not in the utmost degree of goodness nor in the extreme degree of badness. (Mgh.) And makaAnN EadolN bayona fariyqayoni [ A place equidistant, or midway, between two parties ]. (S in art. swY .) ― -b4- See also EidolN , throughout the greater part of the paragraph. -A3- EadolN is also the name of a certain chief of the [body of armed men called] $uraT , (S, O,) or $uroTap , (K,) of a tub~aE [or King of El-Yemen], who, when he desired the slaughter of a man, delivered him to this person; (S, O, K;) whereupon the people said, wuDiEa EalaY yadaYo EadolK [ He has been consigned to the hands of 'Adl ]; (S, O;) and this was afterwards said of anything of which one despaired. (S, O, K.) [Meyd mentions EalaY yadaYo EadolK , as a prov., without wuDiEa : see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 80.]

definition: The like (IAar, Zj, O, K) of a thing;
sourceDefinition: The like (IAar, Zj, O, K) of a thing; (IAar, O;) as also ↓ EadolN ; syn. mivolN ; (IAar, Zj, O, K;) and naZiyrN [which signifies the same, or the equal ]; and so ↓ EadiylN : (K:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, ↓ EadolN and EidolN are nearly the same; but the former is used in relation to what is perceived mentally, as in the phrase of the Kur [v. 96], A^awo Eadolu *`lika SiyaAmFA [mentioned voce EadolN ]; and EidolN and ↓ EadiylN , in relation to what is perceived by the sense, as things weighed and things numbered and things measured: Ibn-'Ámir, however, read Aw Eidolu *lk ; and Ks and the people of El-Medeeneh, with fet-h [i. e. Eadolu ]: (TA:) or Eidolu Al$~aYo'i , with kesr, signifies the like of the thing in kind, (Mgh, Msb,) or in quantity, or measure, or the like, (Msb,) or also in quantity, or measure, or the like, (Mgh,) and IF says, in weight; (Msb;) and ↓ Eadoluhu , with fet-h, (Mgh, Msb,) its like, (Mgh,) or what will stand in its stead, (Msb,) of a thing different in kind, (Mgh, Msb;) whence the phrase of the Kur A^awo Eadolu *`lika SiyaAmFA [mentioned above]; Eadol being originally an inf. n.: (Msb:) Akh says, AlEidolu , with kesr, signifies Almivolu ; and ↓ AlEadolu , with fet-h, is originally an inf. n., but is made a subst. to denote Almivolu in order to distinguish it from the Eidol of goods or commodities [which will be expl. in what follows]: Fr says, AlEidolu , with kesr, is the like ( Almivolu ), as in the saying EinodiY Eidolu gulaAmika [ I have the like of thy boy or young man ] and Eidolu $aAtika [ the like of thy sheep or goat ]; but you say ↓ AlEadolu , with nasb [i. e. fet-h] to the E , when you mean the [ equal in ] value, of what is different in kind; though sometimes it is pronounced with kesr by some of the Arabs, app. by an error on their part: (S, O:) or some allow one's saying EinodiY Eidolu gulaAmika as meaning I have the like of thy boy or young man, [and app. ↓ Eadoluhu also,] and Eadoluhu with fet-h only as meaning his value: (TA:) but Zj says that AlEadolu and AlEidolu both signify the like, whether it be of the same kind or of a different kind; and if one make a mistake, he should not say that some of the Arabs have erred: (O:) the pl. (S, O, K) of EidolN , by common consent, (S, O,) is A^aEodaAlN , (S, O, K,) and [that of ↓ EadiylN is] EudalaA='u . (K.) ― -b2- Also The half of a load, (K, TA,) such as is on either of the two sides of the camel; (TA;) or a burden [ borne on one side of a beast, counterbalancing another on the other side, or] made equiponderant to another burden: (Az, TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEodaAlN and [of mult.] EuduwlN : (Sb, K:) and ↓ EadiylN signifies the equal of a person in weight and measure or size or the like (S, K, * TA) in the [vehicle called] maHomil : (TA:) Sb says that it signifies a human being that is the equal of another [ in weight ]; distinguishing it from EidolN , which, he says, is applied only to goods, or commodities: (IB, TA:) [but] ↓ EadiylataAni signifies two sacks ( giraArataAni ); because each counter balances, or is equiponderant to, the other. (TA.) Hence one says of the Euduwl of an evil judicial decision, maA humo EuduwlN wal`kino EuduwlN [meaning They are not witnesses whose testimony is approvable, but equalized loads of merchandise ]. (TA.) And [hence also] one says, waqaEa AlmuSoTariEaAni EidolaYo baEiyrK , meaning The two [ men wrestling ] fell together, neither of them having thrown down the other. (TA. [See also EikomN .])

definition: It is an inf. n. of Eadula (S, O, Msb) said of a witness; like ↓ EuduwlapN : and signifies The quality of a witness such as is termed EadolN [q. v.]: it is expl. as being a quality the regard of...
sourceDefinition: : see EadolN , in two places. It is an inf. n. of Eadula (S, O, Msb) said of a witness; like ↓ EuduwlapN : and signifies The quality of a witness such as is termed EadolN [q. v.]: it is expl. as being a quality the regard of which necessitates the guarding against what falls short of the requirements of manly virtue or moral goodness, habitually and evidently; which evident falling short thereof is not effected by small instances of lapses or falls into wrongdoing, and by perversion of speech, because mistake and forgetfulness are supposable [ as the causes thereof ], and interpretation not according to the obvious meaning; but it is when such is the known and repeated practice of the person: regard is to be had to the goodness, or honesty, of every individual, and his usual practice in respect of his apparel, and his dealing in selling and buying, and the conveyance of goods, and other things; and when he does that which is not suitable to him, without necessity, his testimony is impugned; otherwise it is not. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , (Msb,) [aor. ,] inf. n. EasofN , (TA,) He did the affair [or he acted in it ] without consideration; (Msb, TA; *) and ↓ tEs~f and ↓ AEtsf have the like meaning: (Msb, * TA:) whence what next follows. (Msb.) ― -b2- Easafa AlT~ariyqa He travelled the road not following a right direction: (Msb:) [or you say,] Easafa Eani AlT~ariyqi , (O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EasofN ; (TA;) and ↓ AEtsf , and ↓ tEs~f ; (O, K;) he declined from the road, (O, K, TA,) and journeyed without direction and without pursuing a right course: (TA:) or Easafa AlT~ariyqa (K, * TA) he travelled the road, (K, TA,) seeking an object of want, (TA,) without direction: (K, TA:) and ↓ AEtsfhu , and ↓ tEs~fh , he travelled it without aiming at and hitting upon a right course: (TA:) and Easafa AlfalaApa , (Mgh,) or AlmafaAzapa , inf. n. as above, (TA,) he traversed, or crossed, the desert, or waterless desert, without direction, (Mgh, TA,) and without any travelled road; as also ↓ AEtsfhA : (Mgh:) or EasofN signifies the taking a course not along the road, (S, IAth, O, TA,) and without knowledge: (IAth, TA:) this is said by IAth to be the primary meaning: (TA:) or, accord. to IDrd, the primary meaning is the travelling the road without direction: (O:) and ↓ AlAiEotisaAfu signifies the taking a course at random, without direction and without knowledge. (Ham p. 613.) And one says, baAta yaEosifu All~ayola , inf. n. as above, He passed the night journeying therein without direction, seeking a thing. (Msb.) And EasofN [alone] signifies The going round about by night seeking an object of quest, or desire. (O, K.) [See also 2, and 4.] ― -b3- Hence, i. e. from the frequent usage of the verb in its primary sense, Easafa fulaAnN fulaAnFA , meaning Such a one treated, or used, such a one wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically; (O;) as also ↓ tEs~fhu : (O, * K:) and Easafa Als~uloTaAnu (O, K) i. e. [ The Sultán, or ruling power, ] acted wrongfully, unjustly, &c.: (K:) inf. n. as above. (IAth, Mgh, TA.) ― -b4- And [hence,] Easafa fulaAnapa He violated such a woman. (TA.) ― -b5- And Ald~amoEu yaEosifu Aljufuwna (assumed tropical:) The tears are copious so that they flow in other than their [ proper ] channels. (A, TA.) ― -b6- And Easafahu , aor. and inf. n. as above, He took him, or it, with strength, or force. (Msb.) ― -b7- And Easafahu He took him as a servant, (O, K, TA,) or an Easiyf ; (TA;) as also ↓ AEtsfhu . (O, K, TA.) ― -b8- Easafa Ealayohi and lahu He worked, or wrought, for him [ as a hired servant ]. (K.) One says, kamo A^aEosifu Ealayoka (O) or laka (TA) i. e. [ How long shall I ] work for thee, (O, TA,) and earn, or gain, for thee, going repeatedly to and fro for thee like him who goes round about in the night seeking an object of quest, or desire? (TA.) ― -b9- And Easafa DayoEatahumo , (K,) aor. as above, (O,) He kept, minded, or managed, their estate, and ordered its affairs in their stead, (O, K, TA,) and went to and fro occupied in that which should put it [or keep it ] in a good, or right, state. (TA.) -A2- EasofN signifies also The breathing of death, (O, K.) And Easafa , (O, K,) aor. , inf. n. EasofN (O, TA) and EusuwfN , (TA,) said of a camel, (O, K,) He was at the point of death, and had [ the affection, or disease, termed ] EusaAf : or, as some say, he had the affection, or disease, termed gud~ap [q.v.]: (O:) or he was at the point of death by reason of the [ affection, or disease, termed ] gud~ap , and began to breathe [or pant ] so that his Hanojarap [or head of the windpipe ] became convulsed. (K.) [See also Eazafa .]

definition: His joints (S, K) of the arms and legs (S) became dry.
sourceDefinition: His joints (S, K) of the arms and legs (S) became dry. (S, K.) [See EuqomN , below.] Hence, (TA,) it is said in a trad. (S, TA) of Ibn-Mes'ood, relating to the resurrection, (TA,) tuEoqamu A^aSolaAbu AlmunaAfiqiyna waAlmu$orikiyna walaA yasojuduwna (S, * TA) i. e. The joints [ of the backbones of the hypocrites and of the believers in a plurality of gods ] shall become dry, and bound, so that their backbones shall be [ as ] one vertebra, impacted together in their constituent parts, [ and they shall not be able to prostrate themselves. ] (TA.) ― -b2- And Euqimato ; (S;) or Eaqimato ; (Msb;) or both; and Eaqamato , aor. ; and Eaqumato ; (K;) inf. n. (K. [See EuqomN , below.]) And Euqimato and Eaqumato and Eaqimato are said of a woman [as meaning She was, or became, barren ]. (IB, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] Eaquma xuluquhu , said of a man, (tropical:) His disposition was, or became, bad, or evil. (TA.) ― -b4- And Eaqima , (K, TA,) inf. n. (TA.)

And it is also applied to a man, meaning To whom no child is born; (S, Msb, K;) and so ↓ EaqaAmN : (K:) pl. EuqamaA='u and EiqAmN (Msb, K) and EaqomaY . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] applied to a wind, (tropical:) Such as does not fecundate, or fructify; (K, TA;) that does not cause clouds to produce rain, nor trees to produce fruit; (S;) i. e. that does not bring rain, but is destructive: or that does not fructify the trees, nor raise clouds, nor bear rain. (TA.) And Alr~iyHu AlEaqiymu [mentioned in the Kur li. 41] means (assumed tropical:) The west, or westerly, wind, by means of which [ the tribe of ] 'Ád were destroyed. (TA.) ― -b5- It is applied to a day as meaning (assumed tropical:) Without air [or wind ], and therefore [ sultry, or] intensely hot. (Msb.) ― -b6- See also EuqaAmN . ― -b7- And see EaqaAmN . ― -b8- The day of resurrection is termed yawomN EaqiymN because [it is (assumed tropical:) A day ] having no day after it. (S, TA.) Accord. to some, it is thus termed in the Kur xxii. 54. (Bd &c.) ― -b9- Ald~unoyaA EaqiymN means (assumed tropical:) [ The present world ] does not render good to him who is of the people thereof. (TA.) ― -b10- And one says, Almuloku EaqiymN meaning (tropical:) Dominion is a condition in which, (A, K, TA,) or in the seeking of which, (Msb,) relationship profits not, (A, Msb, K, TA,) nor friendship: (Msb:) for a man will slay his son, (S, Msb,) if he fear him, (S,) and his father, (Msb,) for dominion; (S, Msb;) or because, in seeking it, the father will be slain, and the son, and the brother, and the paternal uncle; (Th, K;) or because, in it, the ties of relationship are severed by slaughter and by undutiful conduct. (TA.)

(TA.)

definition: A joint of a horse;
sourceDefinition: A joint of a horse; (S, K;) such as [ that of ] the pastern, next the hoof, and the knee, and the hock: (S:) pl. maEaAqimu : (S, K:) the pl. signifies certain vertebræ between [ the one called ] the fariydap [q. v.] and the Eajob [i. e. the root, or base, of the tail ], in the hinder part of the backbone, (K, TA,) of the horse. (TA.) One says of a horse, huwa $adiydu AlmaEaAqimi , meaning He is strong in respect of the vertebræ above mentioned: and likewise, in the joints of the pasterns. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A joint, or knot, in straw. (S, TA.)

Euluw~N ; (Msb, K;) and EaliYa ; and ↓ tEl~Y [which last see also below]; (K;) It (a thing, Msb) was, or became, high, elevated, or lofty; (Msb, K; *) syn. AirotafaEa ; (Msb;) and so ↓ tEAlY : (S, K:) or you say, EalaA fiY AlmakaAni [ it was, or became, high, or elevated, in place ], aor. yaEoluw , inf. n. Euluw~N : (S:) and EaliYa fiY Al$~arafi [(assumed tropical:) he was, or became, high, or elevated, or exalted, in dignity, or nobility ], (S, Mgh,) with kesr, (S,) aor. yaEolaY , inf. n. EalaA='N ; (S, Mgh;) and also EalaA , with fet-h, aor. yaEolaY : a poet says, lam~aA EalaA kaEobuka liY Ealiytu [(assumed tropical:) When thy nobility became exalted to me, I became exalted ]; thus combining the two dial. vars.: (S:) or you say, EaliYa fiY AlmakaArimi [(assumed tropical:) he was, or became, eminent in generous, or honourable, actions or qualities ], inf. n. EalaA='N [in some copies of the K EalFA ]; (Msb, K;) and EalaA , inf. n. Euluw~N ; (K;) and thus the two verbs are used in the saying of the poet cited above: (TA:) and ↓ AstElY , said of a man, signifies the same as EalaA . (S.) [Hence,] Ealati Al$~amosu The sun became high; as also ↓ AiEotalat : (Nawádir el-Aaráb, TA in art. dlk :) and [hence,] EalaA Aln~ahaAru The day became advanced, the sun being somewhat high; syn. AirotafaEa [q. v.]; as also ↓ AEtlY and ↓ AstElY . (K.) ― -b2- EalaA fiY AlmakaAni , inf. n. Euluw~N , signifies [also] He ascended the place, or upon the place; syn. SaEida : and Ealawotu EalaY Aljabali and Ealawotu A^aEolaAhu are syn. [as meaning I ascended the mountain, or upon the mountain, or upon the top, or highest part, thereof ]: and Ealawotuhu and Ealawotu fiyhi signify I ascended it; syn. raqiytu fiyhi . (Msb.) EalaAhu (S, Msb, K, TA) and EalaA bihi , (K, TA, [in the CK El~Ah wbh is put for EalaAhu wabihi ,]) and ↓ AstElAhu , (S, K, TA,) and ↓ AEtlAhu , (S,) and ↓ AiEolawolaAhu , and ↓ AElAhu , and ↓ El~Ah , (K, TA,) this last [for which the CK has EAlAhu ] being with teshdeed, (TA,) and ↓ EAlAhu and bihi ↓ EAlY , (K, TA, [in the CK EAl~aAhu wbh ,]) are syn., (S, K,) signifying He ascended it, or upon it; (K; [in the CK SaE~adahu , and so in my MS. copy of the K, but in other copies SaEidahu , which is certainly the right reading;]) whether the object be a mountain or a beast: (TA:) [or] you say, EalaA Ald~aAb~apa He mounted the beast; (K, TA;) and in like manner, anything: (TA:) and EalaY Als~aToHa , aor. yaEoliyhi ; (K, TA;) but in the M EaliYa Als~aToHa , i. e., like raDiYa ; (TA;) inf. n. EaloYN (K, TA) and EiloYN (TA, and so accord. to some copies of the K,) and EuliY~N ; (TA, and so accord. to other copies of the K instead of EiloYN ;) He ascended upon the flat house-top; syn. SaEidahu . (K, TA.) ― -b3- [ EalaAhu signifies also He, or it, was, or became, upon it, or over it: and it came, or arose, upon it; overlay it; was, or became, superincumbent, or supernatant, upon it; or overspread it; as scum, and rust, &c. And It lay on him as a burden. Hence,] one says, maA saA^alotuka maA yaEoluwka ZahorFA i. e. [(assumed tropical:) I did not ask, or demand, of thee, what would lie as a burden on thy back; or] what would be onerous, burdensome, oppressive, or troublesome, to thee. (TA.) ― -b4- And [hence also] EalaAhu It over- topped it, rose above it, or exceeded it in height. (TA in art. dSr .) [And in like manner, ↓ AstElY Ealayohi It became elevated above it. ] ― -b5- And Ealawotuhumo biAl$~arafi and biAljamaAli [(assumed tropical:) I was, or became, superior to them in nobility and in goodliness ]. (S in art. frE .) ― -b6- And EalaAhu [(assumed tropical:) He had, or gained, ascendency over him, or it; as also EalaA Ealayohi and Elyh ↓ AstElY : and] (assumed tropical:) he overcame him; or had, or gained, the mastery over him; (S, Msb, TA;) and subdued him; (Msb;) namely, his opponent, or adversary; as also ↓ AstElAhu : and in like manner, EalaA HaAjatahu and ↓ AstElAhA (assumed tropical:) he gained the mastery over the object of his want: and ↓ AEtlY Al$~aYo'a (assumed tropical:) he prevailed against the thing, or had power over it, and overcame it; and EalaA lil$~aYo'i , aor. yaEoluw , (assumed tropical:) he was, or became, able to do, or accomplish, or to bear, the thing. (TA.) EalaA biAlA^amori means AiDoTalaEa bihi waA@sotaqal~a [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He had strength, or power, sufficient for the affair, and had absolute control over it ]: (S: [so in one of my copies: the other has AiT~alaEa , which I find also in the PS and in my copy of the TA; and which is allowed by some, but disallowed by others, in the sense of AiDoTalaEa , as is shown voce muDoTaliEN :]) a poet says, faA@Eomido limaA taEoluw famaA laka biAl~a*iY laA tasotaTiyEu mina AlA^umuwri yadaAni [ Then aim thou at that for which thou hast sufficient strength, or power, and over which thou hast absolute control: ( bihi being understood after tElw :) for what object hast thou in meddling with that which a pair of hands cannot accomplish, of affairs? ]. (S.) [And hence, perhaps,] one says to him who possesses much property, AEl bh i. e. Abq bEdh [app. AuEolu bihi and Aiboqa baEodahu , as though meaning (assumed tropical:) Have thou ability to consume it, and so survive thou it; like as one says to him who puts on a new garment, A^aboli (see 4 in art. blw )]: or [perhaps a mistake for “ and ”] it is [virtually] a prayer for his continuance in life. (TA.) ― -b7- Ealawotu EalaY fulaAnK Alr~iyHa means I was [or went ] on the windward side of such a one: and one says, laA taEolu Alr~iyHa EalaY AlS~ayodi fayaraAHa riyHaka wayanofira [i. e. Go not thou on the windward side of the game, lest it scent thy odour, and take fright and flee ]. (TA.) ― -b8- Ealawotuhu biAls~ayofi means I smote him [ with the sword; or, more properly, I set upon him therewith ]. (S, TA.) And [in like manner] one says, EalaAhu biAl$~atomi waAlD~arobi [(assumed tropical:) He set upon him, or assailed him, or overcame him, with reviling and beating ]. (S and M in art. vwl , &c.) ― -b9- EalaA fiY AlA^aroDi , (S, TA,) inf. n. Euluw~N , (S,) signifies (assumed tropical:) He exalted, or magnified, himself, [ in the earth, ] or behaved proudly, insolently, or exorbitantly. (S, * TA.) And [in like manner] laA taEoluwA EalaY A@ll~`hi , in the Kur xliv. 18, (assumed tropical:) Exalt not, or magnify not, yourselves against God; or behave not proudly, &c. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b10- EalaA Eanohu [lit. signifies It rose from it: and hence,] it recoiled from it, i. e., a thing from another thing; it did not cleave to it: and taEoluw Eanohu AlEayonu means (assumed tropical:) The eye recoils from him. (TA.) ― -b11- AuEolu Ean~iY : see 3. ― -b12- EalaA bihi as syn. with A^aEolaAhu : see expl. with the latter below.
