In many instances, fiY may be rendered Of, or concerning, or in respect of; as in qaAla fiyhi ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He said of, or concerning, him, or it, thus; for qaAla fiY *ikorihi ka*aA (assumed tropical:) He said in mentioning him, or it, thus, or fiY waSofihi in describing him, or it; or the like hence, for ex., one says kataba kitaAbFA fiY Eilomi All~ugapi (assumed tropical:) He wrote a book of, or concerning the science of lexicology: and hence, in the Kur ii. 133, A^at~uHaAj~uwnanaA fiY A@ll~`hi (assumed tropical:) Do ye argue with us concerning, or in respect of, God? ] ― -b3- It also denotes concomitance, (Mughnee, K,) and (K) in this ease (Mughnee) it is syn. with maEa . (Msb, Mughnee, K.) Thus in the phrase, qaAla A@doxuluwA fiY A^umamK [ He shall say, Enter ye with peoples ]. (Msb, Mughnee, TA,) in the Kur [vii. 36]: (Msb, TA:) or, as some say, the meaning is, fiY jamaAEapi A^umamK [ in the company of peoples ]. (Mughnee.) Thus. too, in the phrase, in the Kur [xlvi. 15], fiY A^aSoHaAbi Aljan~api [ With the inmates of Paradise ]. (Msb, TA.) [Or in these and similar instances, fiY may be rendered, more agreeably with the primary signification, as meaning Among. ] In the K, the meaning as denoting concomitance and that which is identical with maEa are made distinct: and it has been said that bi denotes the continuance of concomitance and maEa denotes its commencement; though this is not invariably the case. (MF, TA.) [Hence it is used to denote a combination of two qualities: as in the phrase TuwlN fiY A@sotiroxaA='K (assumed tropical:) Length together with laxness: (occurring in the K voce TanabN :) and sawaAdN fiY HumorapK (assumed tropical:) Blackness blending with redness: and the like. And in like manner it is used to denote the combination of the length and breadth of a thing: as in the phrase Tuwluhu Ei$oruwna *iraAEFA fiY valaAvi A^a*oruEK EaroDFA Its length is twenty cubits with (or as we say by ) three cubits in breadth: in which case the number of square cubits is expressed by the phrase Ei$oruwna fiY valaAvK as though meaning Twenty as a multiplicand with three as its multiplier; i. e. twenty multiplied by three: see Daraba as signifying “ he multiplied. ”]. ― -b4- It also denotes the assigning of a cause. (Msb, Mughnee, K.) Thus in the phrase fiY A^arobaEiyna $aApN i. e. On account, or because, of completing [the possession of] forty sheep or goats, [the giving of] a sheep or goat [for the poor-rate] is incumbent [on the possessor: or this may be rendered, in the case of the possession of forty, a sheep or goat is to be given]. (Msb.) And thus in the saying, [in the Kur xii. 32,] fa*`likun~a A@l~a*iY lumotun~aniY fiyhi [ And that is he because of whom ye blamed me ]. (Mughnee.) Thus also in the saying, in a trad., A_in~a A@moraA^apF daxalati Aln~aAra fiY hir~apK HabasatohaA [ Verily a woman entered the fire of Hell because of a she-cat which she confined without food]. (Mughnee.) [And thus in the phrase A^asolafa fiY ka*aA He paid in advance, or beforehand, for, or on account of, such a thing. ] ― -b5- It also denotes superiority; (Mughnee, K, TA;) i. e. (TA) it is used in the sense of EalaY . (T, S, M, Msb, TA.) Thus in the saying, in the Kur [xx. 74], walaA^uSal~iban~akumo fiY ju*uwEi A@ln~axoli [ And I will assuredly crucify you upon the trunks of palm-trees ]. (T, S, Msb, Mughnee, TA.) And so in the verse of 'Antarah cited voce saroHN . (T, M, Mughnee, TA.) And Yoo asserts that the Arabs say, nazalotu fiY A^abiyka , meaning Ealayohi [i. e. I alighted, or descended and stopped, &c., at the abode of thy father ]. (S.) ― -b6- It is also syn. with bi , (T, S, M, Mughnee, K,) sometimes. (S.) Thus in the saying of Zeyd-el-Kheyl, watarokabu yawoma Alr~awoEi fiyhaA fawaArisu baSiyruwna fiY TaEoni AlA^abaAhiri wAlkulaY (S, Mughnee, TA,) meaning, biTaEoni AlAbAhr wAlklY [i. e. And horsemen skilful in piercing the aortas and the kidneys ride in the day of fear therein ]. (S, TA.) And thus in a verse cited by Fr, A^arogabu is made trans. by fiY and Eano instead of bi and Eano . (T, TA.) [Thus, also, layosa fiY $aYo'K is sometimes used for layosa bi$aYo'K , meaning It is nought; or not of any account or weight; &c.: see more in art. $yA^ .] ― -b7- It is also syn. with A_ilaY . (Mughnee, K.) Thus in the Kur [xiv. 10], farad~uwA A^ayodiyahumo fiY A^afowaAhhm [ And they put their hands to their mouths ]. (Mughnee, TA.) ― -b8- It is also syn. with mino . (M, Mughnee, K, TA.) Thus in the Kur [xxvii. 12], fiY tisoEi A=yaAtK [ Of, or among, nine signs ]. (M, TA.) And in the saying, xu*o liY Ea$orFA mina AlA_ibili fiyhaA faHolaAni [ Take thou for me ten of the camels; of, or among, them let there be two stallions. (M, TA.) [Thus too in the saying huwa fiY A^aSoli qawomihi He is of, or among, the purest in race, &c., of his people: and the like thereof.] ― -b9- It also denotes comparison; and this is when it occurs between a preceding [mention of a] thing excelled and a following [mention of a] thing excelling: as in the saying, [in the Kur ix. 38,] famaA mataAEu A@loHay`wpi A@ld~unoyaA fiY A@loA=xirapi A_il~aA qaliylN [ But the enjoyment of the present life, in comparison with that which is to come, is no other than little ]. (Mughnee, K.) ― -b10- It is also used for compensation; and this is when it is redundant as a compensation for another [ fiY ] which is suppressed: as in the saying, Darabotu fiymano ragibota for Darabotu mano ragibota fiyhi [ I beat, or struck, him whom thou desiredst ]: (Mughnee, K:) but this is allowed by Ibn-Málik alone. (Mughnee.) ― -b11- And it is used for corroboration: (Mughnee, K:) this is when it is redundant without its being for compensation: and this El-Fárisee allows in a case of necessity in verse; citing as an ex., A^anaA A^abuwA saEodK A_i*aA All~ayolu dajaA taxaAlu fiY sawaAdihi yaranodajaA [ I am Aboo-Saad; when the night becomes dark, thou imagining its blackness to be black leather ]. (Mughnee.) And it is thus used in the saying, in the Kur [xi. 43], waqaAla A@rokabuwA fiyhaA [for A@rokabuwhaA , i. e. And he said, Embark ye therein, the like of which occurs also in xviii. 70 and xxix. 65], (Mughnee, K,) accord. to some. (Mughnee.) -A2- fiY as a prefixed noun in the gen. case, syn. with fam , and fiY~a as syn. with famiY , see voce fuwhN , in art. fwh .

sourceDefinition: is a word expressive of wonder: they say, yaA faY~a maA liY A^afoEalu ka*aA [ O my wonder! What has happened to me that I do thus? ]: or it is expressive of regret on account of a thing that is passing away [so that this exclamation may be rendered Oh! What has happened to me &c.]: Ks says that it is not to be written with ' [though it is so written in several of the lexicons in art. fyA^ , i. e. faYo'a ]; and that it means yaA EajabiY [as first expl. above]: and in like manner one says, yaA faY~a maA A^aSoHaAbuka [ O my wonder! What are thy companions? i. e. what manner of men are thy companions? mA here denoting interrogation respecting qualities, or attributes; as in the Kur xxvi. 22]: and he says that mA in this case occupies the place of a noun in the nom. case. (M, TA.) Ks is also related to have said that some of the Arabs express wonder by faY~a and haY~a and $aYo'a ; and some add maA , saying yaA fay~amaA and yaA hay~amaA and yaA $ayoy^amaA , meaning How good, or beautiful, is this! the K is faulty here; mentioning only yaA fay~amaA , and explaining it as denoting wonder. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Mgh, &c.,) aor. yafiyDu , inf. n. fayoDN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and fayoDuwDapN (S, O, K) and fuyuwDN (M, O, K) and fiyuwDN and fuyuwDapN (M, K) and fayaDaAnN , (M, O, K,) It (water) overflowed: poured out, or forth, from fulness: (Mgh:) it (water, S, O, K, or a torrent, Msb) became abundant, (S, O, Msb, K and flowed from [ over ] the brink of the valley, (Msb,) or so as to flow over the side of the valley, (S, O,) or so as to flow like a valley; (K;) and ↓ AfAD signifies the same: (Msb, TA:) it (water) became abundant: (TA:) [ contr. of gaADa , aor. yagiyDu :] it (water, and that of the eyes, and the like, M, or anything fluid, Msb) ran, or flowed: (M, Msb:) or it poured out, or forth; or poured out, or forth, vehemently; gushed out, or forth: (M:) and it (water, and blood,) fell in drops. (Msb.) ― -b2- It (a vessel) became full: (Msb:) [or it overflowed: for you say,] faADa Aln~ahoru bimaAy^ihi The river overflowed with its water: and faADa AlA_inaA='u bimaA fiyhi The vessel overflowed with what was in it: (Msb:) and a poet says, $akawotu wamaA Al$~akowaY limivoliYa EaAdapF wal`kino tafiyDu AlkaA^osu Einoda A@motilaAy^ihaA [ I complained; and complaint is not a custom of the like of me; but the cup overflows on the occasion of its being full ]. (A) You say also faADato Eayonuhu , aor. as above, inf. n. fayoDN , The eye flowed [with tears]. (TA.) And faASa EaraqFA , said of a man, [ He sweated; ] sweat appeared upon his body, on an occasion of grief. (IKtt) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) It (a thing) was, or became, much, abundant, many, or unmerous. (O, K.) You say, faADa All~iy^aAmu (assumed tropical:) The mean became many: (S, O:) opposed to gaADa , q. v. (S and A in art. gyD .) And faADa Alxayoru (tropical:) Good, or wealth, &c., became abundant, (A, Msb,) fiyhimo among them. (A.) ― -b4- Aor. as above, (S,) inf. n. fayoDN , (TA,) (tropical:) It (a piece of news, or a story,) spread abroad; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ AstfAD ; (S, M, A, Msb, K, TA;) it spread abroad among the people. (Msb and TA in explanation of the latter verb,) like water. (TA.) ↓ The latter is also said of a place, meaning (tropical:) It became wide, or ample. (A.) And you say, faADa Ealayohi Ald~iroEu (tropical:) [ The coat of mail spread over him; or covered him ]. (A.) ― -b5- Aor. as above, inf. n. fayoDN and fuyuwDN , (tropical:) He (a man, S, O, K) died: (S, M, O, K:) and, (S, M, O, K,) in like manner, (S, O,) faADatN nafosuhu , (S, M, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (M,) inf. n. fayoDN , (M, Msb,) (tropical:) his soul departed, or went forth; (S, M, A, * Mgh, * O, Msb, K;) of the dial. of Temeem; (S, M, O;) on the authority of AO and Fr; and AZ says the like; but As says that one should not say, fAD Alr~ajulu , nor fADt nfsh , for fAD is only said of tears and of water: (S, O:) to which is added in the O, but one says, faAZa , with Z , [as is also said in the Mgh,] as meaning “ he died, ” and not fAD , with D , decidedly: (TA:) [see, however, the remarks of IB below:] or the more chaste expression is fAZ , with Z , without the mention of the nfs ; and some do not allow any other: (Msb:) but in the L we find as follows: IAar says. fAD Alrjl and fAZ , meaning “ the man died: ” and Abu-l-Hasan says, fAZt nfsh , the verb relating to the nfs ; and fAD Alrjl and fAZ : but As says, I heard AA say that one should not say, fAZt nfsh , but fAZ , meaning “ he died; ” and not fAD , with D , decidedly: IB, however, says that what IDrd has cited from As is different from that which J has ascribed to him; for IDrd cites the words of As thus: the Arabs says, fAZ Alrjl , meaning “ the man died; ” but when they speak of the nfs , they say fADt nfsh , with D ; and he quotes the ex. fafuqiy^ato EayonN wafaADato nafosu [ And an eye was put out, and a soul departed ]: and he [IB] adds that this is what is commonly known to be the opinion of As: but J has committed and error; for As quotes from AA that one should not say, fAZt nfsh , but fAZ , meaning “ he died; ” not fAD , decidedly and he also says, nor does it necessarily follow from what he relates that he firmly believed it: AO says that fAZt nfsh is of the dial. of Keys; and fADt , of the dial of Temeem and AHát says, I heard AZ say that Benoo-Dabbeh alone say, fADt nfsh : in like manner also El-Mázinee says. on the authority of AZ. that all the Arabs say, fAZt nfsh . except Benoo-Dabbeh, who say, fADt nfsh with D . (TA.) [See also art. fyZ . It is further said, that] AlfayoDu signifies Death: (A, K;) as occurring in a trad respecting Ed-Dejjál, where it is said, vum~a yakuwnu EalaY A^avari *`lika AlfayoDu [ Then shall be, after that, death ] (A, TA:) Sh says, I asked El-Bekráwee respecting this, and he asserted AlfyD , in this case, to signify “ death; ” but I have not heard it from any other; unless it be from faADato nafosahu signifying His slaver collecting upon his lips at the departure of his soul [ flowed ]. (TA.) ― -b6- You say also faADa Sdoruhu mina AlgayoZi (tropical:) [ His bosom overflowed with wrath, or rage ], (A, TA.) And faADa Sadoruhu biAls~ir~i His bosom disclosed, or concealed, the secret; (S, O, K;) his bosom could not conceal the secret; (M;) his bosom was full with the secret, and disclosed it, not being able to conceal it. (TA.) ― -b7- And fayoDN is used as meaning (assumed tropical:) God's suggesting ( A_iloqaA=' ) [of a thing]: what the Devil suggests ( yuloqiyhi ) is termed Alwasowasapu . (Kull p. 277.) ― -b8- faADa AlbaEiyru bijir~atihi : see 4, latter half.

(A, TA.) ― -b5- A^afaADuwA mino EarafaAtK (tropical:) They pushed on, pressed on, or went quickly, syn. dafaEuwA , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) or AinodafaEuwA , (M, A,) with multitude, (M, Mgh, O,) from 'Arafát, (S, M, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) to Minè, (S, M, O,) exclaiming lab~ayoka : (M:) or they returned, and dispersed themselves from 'Arafát: (O, K:) or they hastened from 'Arafát to another place: (K:) the last rendering is taken from Ibn-'Arafeh; and agreeably with all of these renderings, the phrase in the Kur [ii. 194], faA_i*aA A^afaDotumo mino EarafaAtK , has been explained: (TA:) and [in like manner,] you say AfADwA mina minaY A_ilaY mak~ipa (tropical:) They returned from Mine to Mekkeh; on the day of the sacrifice: (Msb:) A_ifaADapN signifies (tropical:) the advancing, and pushing on, or pressing on, in journeying, or pace, (A, * TA,) and the like, (A,) with multitude, and is only after a state of separation and congregation: (TA:) it is from the same word as signifying the “ pouring out, or forth; ” (A, O, TA,) or from AfAD AlmaA='a signifying “ he poured the water out, or forth, copiously ” (Mgh:) and the original expression is AfAD nafosahu . or raAHilatahu ; but they omit the objective complement, and hence the verb resembles one that is intrans.: (O, TA:) or AfADp signifies the quickly impelling or urging [a beast] to run, with one's foot or leg, or feet or legs: and AfAD , he (a rider) made his camel to exert himself beyond measure, to go a quick run, between the utmost rate and what is less than that; AfADp denoting the half [ of the full rate ] of the run of camels having riders upon these; and being only applied when they have riders upon them: (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh:) and every dafoEap [or act of pushing on, or pressing on, ] is termed A_ifaADapN . (S, Msb, K.) Hence, TawaAfu AlA_ifaADapi , signifying The circuiting [around the Kaạbeh] on the return from Mine to Mekkeh; (Msb, TA) on the day of the sacrifice: (TA:) or the circuiting of visitation. AinodafaEuwA : (Lh, S, M, A, O,) they entered thereinto; launched forth, or cut, thereinto: (Lh, M, O;) they were large, or copious, or profuse, therein; (O, TA:) or they dilated therein (M:) or they began, commenced, or entered upon, discourse: (Msb;) as also ↓ AstfADwhu , (M, Msb,) accord. to some; (Msb;) but this latter is disallowed by most; (M;) or by the skilful, (Msb.) You say also, AfAD fiY EamalK (assumed tropical:) He entered into an action, or employment; and pushed on, or pressed on, therein: (Bd in x. 62:) or he began it, commenced it, or entered upon it. (M.) ― -b9- maA AfAD bikalimapK (assumed tropical:) He did not make clear, or distinct, or perspicuous, a word, or sentence. (Msb, TA.) Daraba biAlqidaAHi [which has two significations: He turned about, or shuffled, the gaming-arrows: and he played with the gaming-arrows ]: (S, M, A, O, K:) and A^ajaAlahaA [which has the former of the above significations]: or he dealt them forth. SdE :) by EalaY AlqidaAHi is meant biAlqidaAHi . (S voce EalaY .) One relation of this verse substitutes yaxuwDu for yufiyDu . (TA.) Az says that A_ifaAD [a mistranscription for A_ifaADapN ] is always a consequence of a state of separation, or dispersion, and abundance, or copiousness. (M.) -A3- AfAD AlmaroA^apa He made the masolakaAni [i. e. vagina and rectum ] of the woman to become one, on the occasion of devirgination; (M;) i. q. definition: A river, (M, TA,) in general: (TA:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A river, (M, TA,) in general: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^afoyaADN and [of mult.] fuyuwDN : the pluralization thereof shows that it is not an inf. n. used as a subst.: (M, TA:) [and a river, or water, that overflows. ] AlfayoDu is [hence] applied to The Nile of Egypt: (S, O, K:) or, accord. to the Tekmileh, to a place in the Nile of Egypt: (TA:) and to the river of El-Basrah: (As, S, K:) or this last is called fayoDu AlbaSorapi , because of its greatness. (M.) You say also A^aroDN *aAtu fuyuwDK Land in which is water: (Lh, M:) or in which are waters that overflow. (M.) ― -b4- Much, or abundant, water. (M.) ― -b5- (tropical:) Much, or abundance: as in the saying, A^aEoTaAhu gayoDFA mino fayoDK (tropical:) He gave him little from much. (S, M, O.) sourceDefinition: Mighty; (M, K;) that overpowers, or subdues, others: (M, TA:) also strong; applied to a man: and courageous: (TA:) pl. qasaAwiru . (M.) ― -b2- A lion; as also ↓ qasowarN : (S, M, K:) because he overcomes and overpowers. (TA.) So in the Kur, [lxxiv. 51,] kaA^at~ahumo HumurN musotanofirapN far~ato mino qasowarapK [ As though they were asses taking fright and running away at random that have fled from a lion ]. (S, M.) Or it has here the signification next following. (S.) ― -b3- Hunters that shoot, or cast: (S, K:) sing. ↓ qasowarN ; (K;) accord. to Lth.; [and in the M it is said that ↓ qasowarN signifies a shooter, or caster: or, accord. to some, a hunter: ] but this is a mistake; for qswrp is a coll. n., having no sing.; and Fr says, that in the verse of the Kur cited above, it means shooters, or casters of missile weapons: it is also related of 'Ikrimeh, that it was said to him that qswrp signifies, in the Abyssinian language, a lion; but he said that is signification is that given above on the authority of Fr, and that the lion in the Abyssinian language is called Eanobasap : and Ibn-'Arafeh says qswrp is of the measure faEowalapN from Alqasoru ; and that the meaning [in the Kur] is, as though they were asses made to take fright and run away by shooting or hunting &c. (TA.) Or, accord. to I'Ab, in the passage above cited, it has the signification here next following. (IKt, TA.) -A2- The sound of men, (IKt, K, TA,) and their voices, or cries. (IKt, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , and qaSadalahu , and A_layohi , (S, M, A, L, Msb, K,) and naHowahu , (A in art. smt , &c.,) aor. , (M, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. qaSodN , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) from which the pl. quSuwdN is formed by some of the professors of practical law; [and maqoSadN , q. v., is also an inf. n.;] (Msb;) He tended, repaired, or betook himself, or went, to, or towards, him, or it; (originally and properly, either in a direct course, in which sense it is in some places specially used, or indirectly; IJ, M, L;) he directed himself, or his course or aim, to, or towards, him, or it; he made for, or towards, him, or it; he made him, or it, his object; he aimed at him, or it: he sought, endeavoured after, pursued, or endeavoured to reach or attain, or obtain, him, or it: he desired it, or wished for it: he intended it; purposed it; or meant it: syn. tawaj~aha wanahada wanahaDa naHowahu , (IJ, M, L,) and naHaAhu , (S, L,) and A^ataAhu , (S, A, L,) and Talabahu biEayonihi , (Msb,) and A^am~ahu , and AiEotamadahu , (M, L, K,) and AiEotazamahu . (IJ, M, L.) ― -b2- qaSadotu qaSodahu : see qaSodahu , below. ― -b3- qaSadotuhu bika*aA and qaSadotuhu lahu bihi [ I brought to him such a thing: lit. I directed, or betook, myself to him with such a thing: see an ex. in the first para. of art. bY ] (Ham. p. 41.) A_ilayoka qaSodiY , and ↓ maqoSadiY , (the latter with fet-h to the S , Msb), To thee is my tending, or repairing, &c. (A.) ― -b4- qaSada fiY AlA^amori , [aor. ,] (A, Msb,) inf. n. qaSodN ; (S. definition: The affair caused me to tend, repair, betake myself, or direct my course, to, or towards, him, or it;
sourceDefinition: The affair caused me to tend, repair, betake myself, or direct my course, to, or towards, him, or it; to aim at him, or it; to seek, endeavour after, pursue, or endeavour to reach, attain, or obtain, him, or it; to desire it, or wish for it; to intend it, or purpose it. (M, L.) ― -b2- (tropical:) It (an arrow) hit its object, and killed on the spot. (S, K.) ― -b3- He pierced a man with a spear, (K,) or shot him with an arrow, (TA,) and did not miss him: (K:) he struck, or shot, a thing so that it died on the spot: (As:) he killed on the spot: (Lth:) it (a serpent) killed a person (Lth, S) on the spot: (Lth:) or bit him so as to kill him. (L, K.) See muqoSdN .

(L.) ― -b2- And (L, K), or *uw qaSiydK , (L,) A bone containing marrow. (L, K.) ― -b3- Dry, or tough, ( yaAsis ,) fleshmeat; (Lth, S, L, K;) as also ↓ qaSodN ; and, as some say, fat fleshmeat. (L.) ― -b4- A fat she-camel, (L, K,) plump and corpulent, (L,) and having marrow in her bones; as also qaSiydapN . (L, K.) ― -b5- A fat camel's hump. (K.) -A3- A staff; (L, K;) as also qaSiydap ; (K;) or the latter has not been heard: (TA:) pl. qaSaAy^idu . (L.) -A4- Poetry, or a poem, trimmed, pruned, or free from faults, well executed, (K,) and composed with premeditation; (TA;) as also qaSiydapN : (TA:) [but the latter is used as a subst.] ― -b2- qaSiydN , a gen. n., applied properly to poetry, and, by extension of the signification, to a single poem, for qaSiydapN ; (IJ, L;). or it is pl. of qaSiydapN , like as safiynN is of safiynapN ; (S, L;) and so is qaSaAy^idu ; (L;) [but properly, qaSiydN is a coll. gen. n., and qaSiydapN is its n. un., and qaSaAy^idu is pl. of the latter;] Poetry, or a poem, [or an ode, (for it was always designed to be chanted or sung,)] of which the bipartition ( $aTor ) of the verses is complete; (M, L, K;) [i. e., of which the hemistichs are complete, not curtailed; (see Alr~amalu ;)] consisting of three verses or more; (Akh, M, L, K;) or of sixteen or more; (M, L, K;) for it is usual to call that which consists of three verses, or ten, or fifteen, qiToEapN , and what consists of more than fifteen the Arabs call qSydp : (IJ, M, L:) or, as Akh has once said, what is of the metre called AlT~awiyl , and AlbasiyT that is complete, and AlkaAmil that is complete, and Almadiyd that is complete, by which he means the first species thereof, which is the most complete that is in use, and AlwaAfir that is complete, by which, in like manner, he means the first species thereof, and Alr~ajaz that is complete, and Alxafiyf that is complete, and [ any ode, or] any poem that is sung by persons riding; but, he adds, we have not heard them sing what is of the metre called Alxfyf : (M, L:) such poetry is thus termed because composed with purpose and consideration, and earnest endeavour to make it excellent; from qaSodN as syn. with A^am~N : or because composed with care, and trimmed with excellent expressions and choice meanings, from qaSiydN signifying “ thick and fat marrow; ” for the Arabs tropically apply to chaste, or eloquent, or excellent, language the epithet samiyn , or “ fat: ” (L:) or because of its completeness, and the soundness of its measure. (M, L.) For the meanings of bayotu AlqaSiydapi , see bayotN ; last sentence. -A5- See also qaSidN .

definition: What is behind the head;
sourceDefinition: What is behind the head; (S, in art. qHd ; and Msb;) that is to say, (Msb,) the [ occiput or] hinder part of the back of the head; (T, Msb, K;) i. e., the surface between the *uw^aAbap [here app. meaning the hair that surrounds the round part of the head ] and what is termed faA^osu AlqafaA [or the small protuberance above the back of the neck ]: (T:) also, the protuberance above the back of the neck, (L, K,) between the *uw^aAbap [see above] and the back of the neck, sloping down from the haAmap [or middle, or crown, or top, of the head ]; it is the part of the head which touches the ground when a man lies on his back: (L:) also, the upper part of the back of the head: (L, K:) or that part of the bone of the head which projects over the back of the neck; the hAmp being above it; and the qa*aAl , below it, next the part of the back of the neck that is between the ears: (AZ, L:) pl. qamaAHidu (S, L, K, &c.) and qamaAHiydu and qamaHoduwaAtN . (L.) Accord. to J and AHei, the m is an augmentative letter; but others hold it to be a radical; and F says, that J's mentioning this word in art. qHd requires consideration. (TA.)

definition: , (A, TA,) [aor, yaqiyDa ,] inf.
sourceDefinition: , (A, TA,) [aor, yaqiyDa ,] inf. n. qayoDN , (K,) He clave, or broke or rent asunder. (A, * K, TA.) You say, qaADa AlbayoDapa He (a young bird) clave, or broke asunder, the egg: and he (a bird) clave, or broke asunder, the egg from over the young one. (Lth, A, * TA.) And it is said in a trad, respecting the day of resurrection, faA_i*aA kaAna ka*`lika qiyDato h`*ihi Als~amaA='u Ald~unubaA Eano A^aholihaA , i. e., [ And when it shall be thus, this lowest heaven ] shall be cleft, or rent asunder, from over its inhabitants, meaning the inhabitants of the earth ( AlA^aroD ), which is previously mentioned in the trad.:] or, as Sh says, shall be dissolved. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, first pers. qiDotu , (AZ, S,) or qaDotu , (IAth,) He cracked a glass bottle, without separation of the parts. (AZ, S, IAth.) ― -b3- And qiDotu AlbinaA='a is a dial. form of quDotu [meaning I demolished, destroyed, or threw down, the building ]. (Sgh.) -A2- Also, inf. n. as above, It became cleft, or broken or rent asunder. (K, in which only the inf. n. is mentioned.) You say, qaADati AlbayoDapu The egg became cleft, or broken asunder. (TK.) [See also 7.] ― -b2- And qaADati Als~in~u , inf. n. as above, The tooth fell out from its root; as also with S . (S, * TA in art. qyS .) -A3- Also, (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He hollowed out a well (K, TA) in a rock. (TA.) And qiyDa signifies It was dug. (TA.) -A4- Also, (TK) inf. n. as above, (K,) He likened, or assimilated. (K, TK.) You say, qaADahu bihi He likened, or assimilated, him, or it, to him, or it. (TK.) [See also 5; and see qayoDo , below.] -A5- See also 3, in two places.

definition: He (God, Msb) ordained, or appointed, for him such a thing.
sourceDefinition: He (God, Msb) ordained, or appointed, for him such a thing. (Mgh, Msb.) And qy~D A@ll~`hu fulaAnFA lifulaAnK , (S, A, K,) in [some of] the copies of the K, bifulaAnK , which is a mistake, (TA,) God ordained, or appointed, or prepared, such a one for such a one: (A:) or brought such a one to such a one, and ordained, or appointed, or prepared, him for him. (S, K.) Hence the saying in the Kur, [xli. 24,] (S,) waqay~aDonaA lahumo quranaA='a (S, K) And we have appointed, or prepared, for them associates (A, * Bd, * K, TA) whence they do not expect, (A, K, TA,) which shall have possession of them like as the qayoD , or shell, has possession of the egg. (Bd.) And so in the same, [xliii. 35,] nuqay~iDo lahu $ayoTaAnFA We will appoint, or prepare, for him a devil [ as an associate ]. (Zj.) Accord. to some, the verb is used only as relating to evil; but this is not true, as is shown by the saying of Mohammad, maA A^akorama $aAb~N $ayoxFA lisin~ihi A_il~aA qay~aDa A@ll~`hu lahu Einoda sin~ihi mano yakorimuhu [ A young man hath not honoured an aged man for his age but God hath appointed for him in his age such as shall honour him ]. (TA.)

EaAraDahu , (S, O, L, and so in a copy of the K,) bimataAEK ; (S;) or EaAwaDahu ; (A, and so in some copies of the K; in the CK, EAyaDahu ;) and baAdalahu ; (A, K;) i. e. he gave him a commodity and took another commodity in its stead: (TA:) [as also qaAbaDahu , with b :] and ↓ qaADahu , aor. yaqiyDu , he gave him a thing in exchange. (TA.) You say, qAyDhu bika*aA [ He gave him in exchange for such a thing ]. (Mgh.) Hence, bayoEu AlmuqaAyaDapi The selling a commodity for another commodity. (Mgh.) And hence the saying of Mohammad, A_ino $iy^ota qaAyaDotuka bihi AlmuxotaArapa mino durwuEi xayobara , or bihi ↓ A^aqiyDuka , accord. to different relations; i. e. [ If thou wilt, ] I will give thee in exchange for it [ the choice of the coats of mail of Kheyber ]. (TA.) You say also, A^aEoTayotuhu farasFA bifarasayoni muqaAyaDapF [ I gave him a horse for two horses in exchange ]. (JK.) And maA A^uqaAyiDu bika A^aHadFA (tropical:) [ I do not give, or take, in exchange for thee any one ]. (A, TA.) And lawo A^uEoTiytu milo'a Ald~ahonaA='i rijaAlFA qiyaADFA bifulaAnK raDiytuhumo (tropical:) [ If I were given what would fill the desert of men, in exchange for such a one, I would not accept them ]: (A, TA:) and the like occurs in a trad. of Mo'áwiyeh, as said by him, with reference to Yezeed. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ kar~a , i. e.] kar~a binafosihi , as distinguished from the trans. kar~a , [aor. ,] (S, Mgh,) inf. n. kr~N , (S,) or kuruwrN , (Mgh,) [or both,] He returned. (S, Mgh.) You say kar~a Ealayohi , (A, K,) aor, , (TA,) inf. n. kar~N and kuruwrN and takoraArN (A, K) and kariyrN , (CK,) He turned to, or against, him, or it: (A, K:) he returned to or against, it: (TA:) the primary signification is the turning to, or against, a thing, either in person, or in act. (El-Basáïr.) And Ainohazama vum~a kar~a Ealayohi [ He was put to flight: then he returned, or turned back, against him ]. (A.) And kar~a AlfaArisu , aor. , inf. n. kar~N , The horseman [ wheeled round, or about, or] fled, to wheel round, or about, and then returned to the fight: (Msb:) [or returned to the fight after wheeling round, or about, or retiring, or being put to flight; as is implied in the phrase next preceding, from the A, and in many other examples: and simply, he charged, or assaulted: opposed to far~a : see kar~apN , below.] You say also AljawaAdu yaSoluHu lilokar~i waA@lofar~i [ The courser is suitable, or fit, for returning to the fight, or for charging, or assaulting, and fleeing ]. (Msb.) [And kar~a signifies He, or it, returned time after time. ] You say A^afonaAhu kar~u All~ayoli waAln~ahaAri The returning of night and day time after time caused him to come to an end. (Msb.) Also kar~a Eanohu He returned from him, or it. (A, K.) And Eano *`lika ↓ takarokara He returned from that. (TA.) -A2- kar~a is also trans., as well as intrans.; (S,) TA;) kar~ahu , (aor. , TA,) inf. n. kar~N , signifying He made, or caused, him, or it, to return: (S, Mgh, TA:) and [in like manner,] Eano ↓ karokarahu ka*aA , inf. n. karokarapN , he made him to return, or revert, from such a thing. (TA.) You say kar~a Ealayohi rumoHahu , and farasahu , inf. n. kar~N , [ He turned back his spear, and his horse, against him ]. (A.) -A3- kar~a , aor. , (S, K,) and [see. pers. karirota ,] aor. , (K,) inf. n. kariyrN , (S, A, * K, * TA,) He uttered a sound like that of one throttled, or strangled: (S, K:) or like that of one harassed, or fatigued, or overburdened: (TA:) or he rattled in his throat ( Ha$uraja ) in dying: (AZ, S:) or he made a sound in his breast like Ha$orajapN [or rattling in the throat in dying ], (A, TA) but not the same as this latter: and thus do horses, in their breasts. (TA.) [See $axara .] ― -b2- Also, He (a sick man) gave up his spirit, at death. (TA.) ― -b3- See also kariyrN , below.

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. takoriyrN (S, Msb, K) and takoraArN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) or, as AA said to Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer, in reply to a question respecting the difference between the measures tafoEaAlN and tifoEaAlN , the latter is a simple subst., and the former, with fet-h, is an inf. n., (S, TA,) [but there are two inf. ns. of the measure tifoEaAlN , both of unaugmented verbs, namely tiboyaAnN and tiloqaA='N ,] and takir~apN , (Ibn-Buzurj, K,) [ He repeated it, or reiterated it, either once or more than once: ] he repeated it several times; reiterated it: (Msb:) or he repeated it one time after another; (K;) which may mean he tripled it, unless the “ other ” time be not reckoned as a repetition; (TA;) as also ↓ karokarahu ; (K; [in the CK, karokarapF is put by mistake for karokarahu ;]) either by act or by speech: (MF:) it differs from A^aEaAdahu , which signifies only “ he repeated it once; ” for none but the vulgar say A^aEaAdahu mar~aAtK ; whereas kar~arahu may signify [not only the same as A^aEaAdahu , as it does in many instances, but also] he repeated it time after time: (Aboo-Hilál El-'Askeree:) some explain kar~arahu as signifying he mentioned it twice, and he mentioned it one time after another: (Sadr-ed-Deen Zádeh:) when it is used in the former of these two senses, the term takoraArN applies to the second, and to the first [with respect to the second]: ('Ináyeh, in the early part of chap. ii.; and TA:) but its explanation as signifying the mentioning a thing one time after another is a conventional rendering of the rhetoricians: (MF:) Es-Suyootee says, that takoraArN signifies the renewing the first word or phrase; and it denotes a sort of taA^okiyd [or corroboration]: but it is said to be a condition of tA^kyd that the words or phrases [which are repeated] be without interruption, and occur not more than three times; and that tkrAr differs from it in both these particulars; so that the phrase in the Kur, [chap. lv.,] fabiA^aY~i A=laA='i rab~ikumaA tuka*~ibaAni is an instance of tkrAr , not of tA^kyd , because it occurs [with interruptions and] more than three times; and so another phrase in the Kur, [chap. lxxvii.,] wayolN yawomay^i*K lilomuka*~ibiyna . (TA.) You say kar~ar EalaY samoEihi ka*aA [ He repeated, or reiterated, such a thing, or saying, to his ear, or ears, or hearing ]. (A.)

definition: A rope [ made in the form of a hoop ] by means of which one ascends a palm-tree;
sourceDefinition: A rope [ made in the form of a hoop ] by means of which one ascends a palm-tree; (S, K;) accord. to A'Obeyd, a name not applied to any other rope; and so, says Az, I have heard from the Arabs; it is made of the best of [ the fibres of the palm-tree called ] liyf : (TA:) or a thick rope; (K;) accord. to AO, made of liyf , and of the outer covering ( qi$or ) of the [ portions of the racemes of the palm-tree called ] Earajiyn and of the [ portion of the branch called ] Easiyb : (TA:) or a rope, in general: (Th, K:) and the rope [or sheet ] of a sail: (S:) or the rope of a ship: or the rope by which a ship is drawn: (TA:) and a qayod [or pair of shackles, or hobbles, ] made of liyf or of palm-leaves: (K:) pl. kuruwrN . definition: A certain measure of capacity, (Mgh, Msb, K,) of the people of El-'Irák, (Mgh, K,) for wheat;
sourceDefinition: A certain measure of capacity, (Mgh, Msb, K,) of the people of El-'Irák, (Mgh, K,) for wheat; (S;) well known; (Msb;) consisting of six ass-loads, (K,) that is, sixty times the quantity called qafiyz , (Az, Mgh, Msb, K,) accord. to the people of El-'Irák, (TA,) the qfyz being eight makaAkiyk , [in the TA, six, but this is a mistake,] and the mak~uwk being a SaAE and a half, which is three kiylajaAt ; so that the kur~ , accord. to this reckoning, is twelve times the quantity called wasoq , (Az, Mgh, Msb,) each wsq being sixty times the quantity called SAE : (Az, Mgh:) in the Kitáb Kudámeh, it is said that the kur~ called AlmuEad~alu is sixty times the quantity called qfyz , and the qfyz is ten A^aEo$iraA=' : and the kur~ called Alqanoqalu is twice the quantity of the kur~ muEad~al , that is, by the qfyz of the mEd~l , a hundred and twenty times the quantity of the qfyz ; with this kr~ are measured unripe dates and dried dates and also olives, in the districts of El-Basrah; and the qfyz used for measuring dates is twenty-five times the riTol of Baghdád; so that the kur~u Alqanoqali is three thousand times as much as the rTl : and the kur~ called AlhaA$imiY~u is the third part of the mEd~l , that is, twenty times as much as the qfyz , by the measure of the mEd~l ; with this kur~ , rice is measured: and the kur~ called AlhaAruwniY~u is equal to them two [but what these two are is not shown]: and the A^ahowaAziY~ is equal to them two: and the maxotuwm is sixth part of the qfyz : and the qfyz is the tenth part of the jariyb : (Mgh:) or the kur~ is forty times as much as the quantity called A_irodab~ ; (K;) by the reckoning of the people of Egypt, as ISd says: (TA:) the pl. is A_ikraAr . (S, Msb.) [It is app. connected with the Hebrew כֹּר , whence the Greek ko/ros (a measure containing, accord. to Josephus, six Attic medimni,) occurring in Luke xvi. 7.]

sourceDefinition: A return. (Msb.) So in the Kur, [ii. 162,] lawo A^an~a lanaA kar~apF [ Would that there were for us ] a return to the world, or former state. And so in xxvi. 102, and xxxix. 59. (Jel.) And so in the saying of Mohammad, All~`ha All~`ha waA@lokar~apa EalaY nabiy~ikumo Fear ye God, [ fear ye God, ] and return to your prophet. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence, The return to life; ] the resurrection; the renewal of mankind, or of the creation, after perishing. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also, A return to the fight, after wheeling away, or retiring: and simply,] a charge, or an assault, (Mgh, K,) in war; (TA;) as also ↓ kur~aY : (Sgh, K:) pl. kar~aAtN . (K.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] A time; one time; [ in the sense of the French “ fois ”; generally repeated, or used in the pl. form, so as to denote a returning to an action, once, or more; i. e., repetition, or reiteration, thereof, agreeably with the primary signification;] syn. mar~apN : (S, K:) pl. as above. (S.) You say faEalahu kar~apF baEoda kar~apK [ He did it time after time ]. And faEalahu kar~aAtK [ He did it several times ]. (A.) ― -b5- [Hence also,] A turn to prevail against an opposing party; victory. So in the Kur, [xvii. 6,] vum~a radadonaA lakumu Alkar~apa Ealayohimo [ Then we gave to you the turn to prevail against them; the victory over them ]. (Bd, Jel.)

definition: The callosity, or callous protuberance, upon the breast of the camel, ( raHaY zawori AlbaEiyri , S, K,) which, when the animal lies down, touches [ and rests ] upon the ground, projecting from his body, like a cake of bread;
sourceDefinition: The callosity, or callous protuberance, upon the breast of the camel, ( raHaY zawori AlbaEiyri , S, K,) which, when the animal lies down, touches [ and rests ] upon the ground, projecting from his body, like a cake of bread; (TA;) it is one of the five vafinaAt [ of which there is one at each knee and one at each stifle-joint ]: (S, TA:) or the breast of any animal of which the foot is of the kind called xuf~ : (K:) pl. karaAkiru . (TA.) Haz~u AlkaraAkiri [lit. The incision of the krAkr ] is when a camel has a disease, so that he is not even when he lies down upon his breast; in consequence of which, a vein is gently drawn forth from the krkrp , and then he [or it] is cauterized. Hence the following, in a trad. of Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr: EaTaAw^ukumu lilD~aAribiyna riqaAbakumo wanudoEaY A_i*aA maA kaAna Haz~u A@lokaraAkiri [ Your bounty is for those who smite your necks, and we are invited when there is a difficult undertaking to be accomplished, like the incision of the krAkr :] meaning, ye invite us only when ye are distressed, because of our skill in war; and on occasions of bounty, and ampleness of the means or circumstances of life, others. (IAth.)

(TA.) -A2- kafatN , [aor. , (S, K) inf. n. kafotN and kifaAtN and kafiytN and kafataAnN , (K,) He, or it, hastened, or was quick, or swift: (S:) it (a bird &c.) hastened, or was quick, or swift, in flying, and running, and contracted itself therein: (K:) it (a solid-hoofed animal) contracted its fore-legs quickly in running: (Az:) the kind of running and flying termed kafataAnN is like a turning aside, or starting aside, ( HayadaAnN ) with violence, or vehemence. (TA.) -A3- kafatahu , [aor. ,] inf. n. kafotN , He drove him, or urged him on, vehemently. definition: A place in which a thing is drawn together, or comprehended, (S, K,) and collected, or congregated.
sourceDefinition: A place in which a thing is drawn together, or comprehended, (S, K,) and collected, or congregated. (K.) So in the words of the Kur [lxxvii. 25 and 26,] A^alamo najoEali A@loA^aroDa kifaAtFA A^aHoyaA'F waA^amowaAtFA [ Have we not made the earth a place which comprehends the living and the dead? meaning kifaAta A^aHoyaA'K waA^amowaAtK :] (S:) EshShaabee, pointing to the houses of El-Koofeh, said, h`*ihi kifaAtu AlA^aHoyaA'$ ; and then, turning to its tombs, he said, h`dhi kifaAtu AlA^amowaAti ; meaning to explain the above text of the Kur: but ISd thinks, that kfAtA in this text is an inf. n., and that AHyA' and AmwAtA are governed by it in the acc. case. (TA.)

definition: A whiteness in the lower lip of a horse, (S, M, K,) not being a part of the [whiteness termed] gur~ap ;
sourceDefinition: A whiteness in the lower lip of a horse, (S, M, K,) not being a part of the [whiteness termed] gur~ap ; (M;) as also ↓ lamaZN : (M, K:) also the former, a gur~ap which descends so that it enters into the mouth of a horse, and so that he removes with it what has remained in his mouth after eating: and ↓ the latter, somewhat white in the lip of a beast of carriage, not passing beyond the place where the lip closes: (M:) or the former, a whiteness upon both the lips, only. (M, K.) Also, Somewhat of whiteness in the fore leg of a horse, or in his hind leg, upon the A^a$oEar [or hair which surrounds the hoof. ] (Ibn- 'Abbád, K.) And A small spot (As, T, S, M, K) of white: (As, T, S, K:) and contr. of black, in the heart. (K.) It is said in a trad., that faith begins like a lumoZap in the heart; (T, S;) and as faith increases, so the latter increases. (T.) And that hypocrisy in the heart is a black lmZp , and faith is a white lmZp ; and as either increases, so the lmZp increases. (M. TA.) ― -b2- Also, (tropical:) A small quantity of clarified butter, which one takes with the finger, (K, TA,) like a walnut: mentioned by Z and Ibn-'Abbád. (TA.)

definition: (from majuda , L) and ↓ maAjidN (from majada , L) A man (S) possessing, or characterized by, majod [or glory, honour, dignity, nobility, &c.
sourceDefinition: (from majuda , L) and ↓ maAjidN (from majada , L) A man (S) possessing, or characterized by, majod [or glory, honour, dignity, nobility, &c.; glorious, in a state of honour or dignity, noble, &c. ]: (S, L, K:) glorious, in a state of honour or dignity, noble, abounding in good, and beneficent; but the former has a more intensive sense: or the latter, characterized by gloriousness or nobleness of actions: (K:) or, by personal glory or nobility with goodness of actions; and the former has a more intensive sense: or both, generous and munificent: (L:) and the latter, good in disposition, and liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous: (ISh, L, K:) pl., either of the former or of the latter, A^amojaAdN . (T, L.) ― -b3- majiydN is also applied in the Kur as an epithet to the throne ( Earo$ ) of God; and to the Kur-án; (L.) and signifies exalted; sublime; (IAar. (L.) Almajiydu alone also occurs in a trad. as meaning the Kur-án. (L.)

sourceDefinition: A sheath or coat, of a plant, enveloping, or surrounding, another sheath or coat, and the latter another, and so on: (T, L:) a xawSap of the kind of plant called vumaAm , (S, K,) and of that called naSiY~ ; (S;) what is plucked from the nSY~ , like a rod; (AHn;) [i. e., a sheath of the vmAm or the nSY~ ;] there is a species of the vmAm having no leaves properly so called, its leaves being sheaths ( A^anaAbiyb ) set one into another, each sheath ( A^unobuwbap ) of which is called AmSwxp , and when it is pulled away it comes forth from the inside of another, as though it were a stopper taken out from a vessel in which collyrium ( kuHol ) is kept: (Lth:) pl. A^umoSuwxN and A^amaASiyxu : (S, K:) the former is a lexicological pl., [or rather a coll. gen. n., of which AmSwxp is the n. un.,] and the latter is the proper pl. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, The white pith of the barodiY~ . (AHn.)

definition: An assembly, (IAar, S, K,) absolutely, (TA,) [whether of nobles or others]: pl.
sourceDefinition: An assembly, (IAar, S, K,) absolutely, (TA,) [whether of nobles or others]: pl. A^amolaA='N . (IAar.) ― -b2- Nobles; chiefs; princes; syn. A^a$oraAfN and EiloyapN ; (K;) principal persons; persons whose opinion is respected. (TA.) ( AlmalaA^u AlA^aEloYa [ The most exalted princes; i. e.] the angels that are admitted near [ to the presence of God ]; or the archangels. TA.) See samEahu , for other explanations. ― -b3- A people of comely appearance, figure, attire, or adornment, united for some purpose or design; expl. by qawomN *w Al$~aArapi wAlt~ajam~uEi liloA_iraAdapi : (Abu-l-Hasan, K:) [but this is wrong, see Beyd, ii. 247.] Thus it is of a different class from rahaTN , though, like this word, a quasi-pl. n. It is an epithet in which the quality of a substantive predominates. (Abu-l-Hasan.) ― -b4- (tropical:) Consultation. (K.) [You say,] maA kaAna h`*aA AlA^amoru Eano malaA_K min~aA (tropical:) This thing was not the result of a consultation and consent on our part: [and] A^akaAna h`*aA Eano malaA_K minokumo (tropical:) Was this the result of a consultation of your nobles, and of your assembly? said by 'Omar when he was stabbed: asserted to be tropical in this sense by Z and others. (TA.) taHad~avuwA malaA^F They conversed, consulting together. (S.) ― -b5- Opinion. (K.) [See a supposed example below.] ― -b6- Disposition; nature; manners; (S, K;) a nature rich in needful qualities: (T:) pl. A^amolaA='N . (S.) [You say,] maA A^aHosana malaA^a baniY fulaAnK How good are the dispositions, or manners, and conversation, of the sons of such a one! (S.) ElJuhanee says, tanaAdawoA yaAla buhovapa A_i*o raA^awonaA faqulonaA A^aHosiniY malaA^F juhayonaA (S) [ They called out, one to another, O Buhtheh! come to our aid! when they saw us: and we said, ] Be of good disposition, or manners, O Juheyneh! or, accord. to some, Be of good opinion, O Juheyneh! (see above:) or, as some say, Aid well, O Juheyneh! taking mlA^ in the sense of mumaAlaA^apF : [see 3]. (TA.) ― -b7- A^aHosinuwA A^amolaA='a kumo Amend your manners; or have good manners. From a trad. (S, K.) ― -b8- Also malaA^N A coveting. (K.)

definition: What first appears of the water of a well (IDrd, K) when it is dug;
sourceDefinition: What first appears of the water of a well (IDrd, K) when it is dug; (IDrd;) as also ↓ nuboTapN : (K:) or the water that comes forth from a well when it is first dug: (Zj:) or the water that issues forth from the bottom of a well when it is dug; (S, accord. to one copy;) or this is termed ↓ nabiyTN : (S, accord. to another copy; and TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^anobaATN and [of mult.] nubuwTN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence the saying,] fulaAnN qariybu Alv~araY baEiydu Aln~abaTi (assumed tropical:) Such a one's promising is near, [but] his fulfilling is remote: i. e. he promises, but does not fulfil. (IAar.) And flAn laA yudoraku nabaTuhu , (TA,) and laA yudoraku lahu nabaTN , (ISd, TA,) (tropical:) Such a one's depth is not known, (K, * TA,) and the extent of his knowledge: (TA:) or such a one's depth is not known; meaning that he is cunning, or possessing intelligence mixed with craft and forecast. (ISd, TA.) And fulaAnN laA yunaAlu nabaTuhu (assumed tropical:) Such a one is invincible, and inaccessible to his enemy. (TA.) ― -b3- nabaTN also signifies A well of which the water has been produced, or fetched out, by labour [ of the digger ]. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And What oozes, or exudes, from a mountain, as though it were sweat, coming forth from the sides of the rock. (TA.) -A2- Aln~abaTu , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ Aln~abiyTu , (S, Msb, K,) and AlA^anobaATu , (K,) the last is a pl. (AAF, S, Msb) of the first, (AAF,) and the second is [a quasi-pl. n.] like kaliybN , (AAF, L,) [ The Nabathæans; ] a people who alight and abide in the baTaAy^iH [see A^aboTaHu ] between the two 'Iráks: (S, K:) or a people (T, M, Mgh, Msb) who alight and abide, (T, TA,) or who used to alight and abide, (Msb,) in the sawaAd (T, M, Mgh, Msb) of El- 'Irák: ) (M, Mgh, Msb:) afterwards applied to mixed people; or people of the lowest or basest or meanest sort; or the refuse of men; and the vulgar sort thereof: (Msb:) the people to whom these appellations properly apply were called nabaT because of their fetching out by labour ( liA@sotinobaATihimo ) what comes forth from the lands: (TA:) [for they were distinguished for agriculture; and hence their proper appellations are used as equivalent to “ clowns, ” or “ boors: ” but a derivation commonly obtaining with us is that from Nebaioth the son of Ishmael:] the n. un. is ↓ nubaATiY~N , (Yaakoob, IAar, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ nabaATiY~N , (IAar, S, Msb, K,) like yamaAniY~N , (S,) and ↓ nibaATiY~N , (K,) and ↓ nabaATK , (S, K,) like yamaAnK , (S,) and ↓ nabaTiY~N , (S, K,) like yamaniY~N , (S,) but this is disallowed by IAar, (Mgh, TA,) and, accord. to Lth, ↓ nabaTaAniY~N , but this [also] is disallowed by IAar. (Msb.)

(TA.) ― -b3- nadabN is also employed to signify (tropical:) Scars upon men's reputation. A poet says, qawomN saA^atoruku fiY A^aEoraADihimo nadabaA A people upon whose reputation I will leave scars, the effects of my satires. (TA.) -A2- nadabN The direction in which one shoots an arrow or arrows: syn. ri$oqN . definition: A place to which one is called, summoned, or invited.
sourceDefinition: A place to which one is called, summoned, or invited. Hence baAbu Almanodabi [The Strait Báb el-Mendeb, or The Strait of the Place of Summons: ] so called because a certain king summoned a number of men to break through the mountain there, which originally opposed a barrier to the sea, in order to drown his enemy; and this they did, thus overwhelming with the waters many cities and towns with their inhabitants, and forming the sea which intervenes between El-Yemen and Abyssinia, and which extends to 'Eydháb and Kuseyr [&c.]. (Yaakoot.) This king was Alexander the Greek! (TA.) [It is probable that the appearance of the Strait gave rise to this story, and thus to its name: but it is also probable that the name may signify The Strait of the Place of Wailing for the Dead; as many perish who go forth from it.]

definition: One sent to do a thing;
sourceDefinition: One sent to do a thing; a messenger; an envoy; an ambassador. (TA.) ― -b2- fulaAnN manoduwbN liA^amorK EaZiymK , and lahu ↓ munad~abN , Such a one is sent to do a great thing; or to perform an important affair. (A.) ― -b3- ↓ munad~abapN an appellation, given by the people of Mekkeh to their Envoys, or ambassadors, to the palace of the Khaleefeh. (TA.) ― -b4- manoduwbN Desired; sought; sought after; as the name of a certain horse it is thus explained: from nadabN , as signifying “ a pledge that is given on the occasion of a race. ” (L.) ― -b5- manoduwbN : see nadaba Almy~t : A thing bewailed, [or complained of as painful, ] with the exclamation of yaA or waA . (KT.) [Freytag, in quoting the original words, omits fiEoluhu before rAjHFA .]

You say also. naD~a Alv~amanu (assumed tropical:) The price was, or became, produced, or apparent, or prepared, or ready: was, or became, given in ready money, or promptly, or quickly, or in advance: syn. HaSala : and taEaj~ala . (Msb.) (A, Mgh. *)

sourceDefinition: , aor. and , inf. n. nafovN (S, K) and nafavaAnN , (TA,) [ He puffed; or blew, without spitting: or he sputtered, or blew forth a little spittle in minute scattered particles: or] he spat: or he [ did as though he ] spat without ejecting spittle: and nafava fY AlEuqodapi signifies he spat, ejecting a little spittle, upon the knot, in enchantment: (Msb:) or Aln~afovu is like Aln~afoxu , or blowing, and less than Alt~afolu , or spitting, or ejecting spittle from the mouth: (S, K:) or like blowing, with [ the emission of ] spittle: (Keshsháf;) or like blowing, as done in enchantment, without spittle: the action, if accompanied by spittle, being termed Altfl : this is the most correct explanation: ('Ináyeh:) or gentle blowing without spittle: ( AlA*kAr :) or more than blowing; or like blowing; but less than spitting: sometimes without spittle, thus differing from Altfl ; and sometimes with a little spittle, thus differing from Alnfx : or the emitting wind from the mouth, together with a little spittle. (MF.) ― -b2- laA bud~a lilomaSoduwri A^ano yanofiva [ He who has a disease in his chest must spit ]. A proverb. (S.) ― -b3- nafavahu mino fiyhi , aor. , inf. n. nafovN , He ejected it from his mouth. (Msb.) ― -b4- [Hence,] nafava All~`hu Al$~aYo'i fiY Alqalobi (tropical:) God cast, or put, the thing into the heart. (Msb) ― -b5- nafiva fiY ruwEiY ka*aA (tropical:) Such a thing was inspired, or put, into my mind. (A.) ― -b6- nafava fiY ruwEiY (tropical:) He (the Holy Spirit [Gabriel]) inspired, or cast, or put, into my mind, or heart. (Nh, from a trad.) ― -b7- [You say,] lawo nafava Ealayoka fulaAnN qaT~araka [ If such a one blew, or spat, upon thee, he would throw thee down upon thy side. ]. Said to one who tries his strength with one superior to him. (A.) ― -b8- nafava EalaY~a gaDabFA as though meaning He blew at me by reason of the violence of his anger. (L.) [See also nafata .] ― -b9- AlHay~apu tanofivu Als~am~a A_i*aA nakazato [ The serpent ejects venom from its mouth when it inflicts a wound with its nose ]. (S.) ― -b10- nafava It (a wound) emitted blood. (TA.) ― -b11- [From the blowing or spitting upon the knots:] nafavahu , inf. n. nafovN , He enchanted him. (Msb.) ― -b12- nafavati Alqidoru , aor. , inf. n. nafiyvN and nafovN , The cooking-pot boiled: or, boiled, and threw forth what resembled arrows, by reason of the vehemence of its boiling. (Msb.) [See also nafatat .] It is when it begins to boil. (TA.)

definition: A thing that one has saved, rescued, or liberated;
sourceDefinition: A thing that one has saved, rescued, or liberated; (S, L, Msb, K;) of the measure faEalN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like nafaDN and qabaDN ; (S, L;) as also ↓ naqiy*N and naqiy*apN : (L:) a man saved, or rescued, or liberated: (L:) also, a horse taken from another people: (L:) or a camel &c. taken by, and then recovered from, the enemy; as also naqiy*apN and naqiy*N ; pl. naqaAy^i*u : (A:) or ↓ naqiy*apN signifies a horse saved, or rescued, or liberated, (S, L, K,) and taken, (S, L,) from the enemy; (S, L, K;) pl. naqaAy^i*u : (S, L;) or the sing. of nqAy^* , signifying horses saved, or rescued, or liberated, from the hands of men, or of the enemy, is ↓ naqiy*N , without p : (IAar, L:) and, accord. to El-Muffaddal, (L,) ↓ naqiy*apN signifies a coat of mail, diroEN ; (L, K;) because it saves the person wearing it from the sword: (L:) and Az says, I have read in the handwriting of Shemir, that it signifies a coat of mail saved, or rescued, from the enemy. (L.) You say also, huwa naqiy*apu buw^osK , and humo naqaAy^*u buw^osK , He is saved, or rescued, from distress, or adversity; and they are &c. (A.) ― -b2- maA lahu $aqa*N walaA naqa*N He possesses not anything. (K.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. nakosN , (S, Msb,) He turned it over, or upside down; inverted it; reversed it; changed its manner of being, or state: (Sh, Msb: *) he turned it over upon its head: (S, A, K:) and he turned it fore part behind; made the first part of it to be last; or put the first part of it last: (Sh:) and ↓ nk~shu , (S, A, K) inf. n. tanokiysN , (S,) signifies the same; (S, * A, K;) or has an intensive sense. (TA.) You say, nukisa Als~ahomu fiY AlkinaAnapi The arrow was turned, or put, upside down in the quiver. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur, [xxxvi. 68,] wamano nuEam~irohu nanokusohu fiY Alxaloqi , or, accord. to the reading of 'Ásim and Hamzeh, ↓ nunak~isohu ; meaning, And him whom We cause to live long, We cause him to become in a state the reverse of that in which he was, in constitution; so that after strength, he becomes reduced to weakness; and after youthfulness, to extreme old age. (TA.) ― -b2- nakasotu fulaAnFA fiY *`lika AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) I made such a one to enter again into that affair, or state, after he had got out of it. (ISh.) [Hence the saying in the Kur, xxi. 66,] vum~a nukisuwA EalaY ruw^uwsihimo (assumed tropical:) Then they were made to return to their disbelief: (Jel:) or (tropical:) then they reverted to disputation, after they had taken the right course by means of consulting together; their return to falsity being likened to a thing's becoming upside down: and there are two other readings; ↓ nuk~isuwA , and nakasuwA ; the latter meaning nakasuwA A^anofusahumo : (Bd;) or (assumed tropical:) then they reverted from what they knew, of the evidence in favour of Abraham. (Fr.) ― -b3- [And hence,] nakasahu , and nakasahu A_ilaY maraDihi , (tropical:) It made him to fall back into his disease. ] (TA, in art. hyD .) And nukisa , (S, Msb, K,) or nukisa fiY maraDihi , (A, TA,) inf. n. nukosN (S, Msb, K) and nakosN (TA, [but see what is said of this below]) and nukaAsN , (Sh, K,) (tropical:) He relapsed into his disease, after convalescence, or after recovery, but not complete, of health and strength: (S, A, K:) or the disease returned to him; [ he relapsed into the disease; ] as though he were made to turn back to it. (Msb.) You say, A^akala ka*aA fanukisa (tropical:) [ He ate such a thing, and relapsed into his disease ]. (A, TA.) And taEosFA lahu wanukosFA , and sometimes one says, nakosFA , (S, K,) in this case, (S,) for the sake of mutual resemblance, (S, K,) or because nakosFA is a dial form [of nukosFA ], (S,) [meaning, (assumed tropical:) May he fall upon his face, or the like, (see art. tEs ,) and relapse into disease: or] may he fall upon his face, and not rise after his fall until he fall a second time: and in like manner you say, ↓ taEasa waA@notakasa . (Msb, art. tEs .) [See also 8.] You say also, nukisa AljuroHu (assumed tropical:) [ The wound broke open again; or became recrudescent ]. (S, in arts. Erb and HbT , &c.) ― -b4- And nakasa AlT~aEaAmu wagayoruhu daA='a AlmariyDi (tropical:) The food, &c., made the disease of the sick man to return. (K.) And nakasa AlxiDaAba EalaY raA^osihi (tropical:) He put the dye upon his head repeatedly, or several times. (A, TA. *) ― -b5- Also nakasa [or more probably nukisa ] (assumed tropical:) He (a man) became weak and impotent. (Sh, in TA.) And nukisa Eano nuZaraAy^ihi , like EuniYa , (assumed tropical:) He fell short of his fellows; was unable to attain to them. (TA.) ― -b6- nakasa raA^osahu , and ↓ nk~shu , (TA,) [and nakasa alone, (see naAkisN ,)] and ↓ nk~s , (L, TA, art. bqr ,) and ↓ Antks , (TA,) [and in like manner ↓ tnk~s , said of a flower-stalk in the M and K, voce qi$obN ,] He bent, or inclined, his head; (TA;) he lowered, or stooped, his head; bent, or hung, it down towards the ground; absolutely; or by reason of abasement. (So accord. to explanations of the act. part. n., below.)

definition: quasi-pass. of nakasahu ; (S, A, TA;) [and therefore signifying It became turned over, or upside down; became turned over upon its head; became inverted; became reversed; became changed in its manner...
sourceDefinition: quasi-pass. of nakasahu ; (S, A, TA;) [and therefore signifying It became turned over, or upside down; became turned over upon its head; became inverted; became reversed; became changed in its manner of being, or state; it became turned fore part behind; its first part was made to be last, or was put last: ] he fell upon his head. (K.) This last signification [understood figuratively] it is said to have in the phrase taEasa waA@notakasa , a form of imprecation, meaning, (assumed tropical:) May he be disappointed, or fail, of attaining his desire: for he who is overthrown in his affair ( man A@notakasa fiY A^amorihi ) is disappointed of attaining his desire, and suffers loss. (TA.) [See also 1, where this form of imprecation is differently explained.] ― -b2- Also, i. q. nak~asa raA^asahu . (TA.) [See 1, last signification.]

definition: An arrow having its notch broken, and its top therefore made its bottom: (S, A, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: An arrow having its notch broken, and its top therefore made its bottom: (S, A, K:) pl. [of pauc.] A^anokaAsN (A, TA) and [of mult.] nukusN . (A.) ― -b2- A head, or blade, of an arrow &c., having its tongue ( sinox ) broken, and its point therefore made its tongue: (K:) pl. A^anokaAsN . (TA.) ― -b3- A bow of which the foot is made [ of ] the head of the branch; as also ↓ manokuwsapN . This peculiarity is a fault. (K.) ― -b4- A child such as is termed yatonN [ born preposterously, feet foremost; but yatonN is an inf. n., and I have not found it used as an epithet anywhere but in this instance]; (K;) i. q. manokuwsN ; and mentioned by IDrd; but he says that it is not of established authority. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) Low, or ignoble; base; vile; mean, or sordid: See a verse cited voce A^a$~aEala : (A:) (tropical:) one who falls short of the utmost point of generosity; (K;) or of courage and generosity: (TA:) (assumed tropical:) weak; (S, K;) applied to a man: (S:) (assumed tropical:) short: (AHn:) pl. A^anokaAsN . (A, K.) ― -b6- See also munak~isN : ― -b7- and nukusN .

definition: Lowering his head;
sourceDefinition: Lowering his head; bending, or hanging, down his head towards the ground; [absolutely;] (S, K;) [or] by reason of abasement: (TA:) pl. [properly naAkisuwna ; (see Kur, xxxii. 12;) and sometimes] nawaAkisu , (S, K,) used [only] in poetry, (S, TA,) by reason of necessity, (TA,) and anomalous, (S, K,) like fawaArisu . (S.) ElFarezdak says, waA_i*aA Alr~ijaAlu raA^awoA yaziyda raA^ayotahum xuDuEa Alr~iqaAbi nawaAkisa AlA^aboSaAri [ And when the men see Yezeed, thou seest them depressed in the necks, lowering the eyes ]: (S:) thus the verse is related by Fr and Ks: Akh says, that it is allowable to say nawaAkisi AlA^aboSaAri , after the manner of the phrase Hujoru Dab~K xaribK ; [see art. xrb ;] and Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà adds Y in relating it; saying nawaAkisiY AlA^aboSaAri . (TA.) [See the remarks on fawaArisu , pl. of faArisN .]

definition: A child [ preposterously brought forth;
sourceDefinition: A child [ preposterously brought forth; whose feet come forth before his head. (A, Msb, and so in a copy of the S.) See also nikosN . ― -b2- wilaAdN manokuwsN [ Preposterous childbirth ] is when the feet come forth before the head; (K, and so in a copy of the S, [and that this is what was meant by the author of the S seems to be indicated by what immediately follows]) i. q. yatonu . (S.) ― -b3- TawaAfN manokuwsN A circuiting of the Kaabeh performed in a way contrary to the prescribed custom, by saluting the black stone and then going towards the left. (Mgh.) ― -b4- qaraA^a AlquraA=na manokuwsFA He read or recited, the Kur-án, beginning from the last part thereof, (K,) i. e. from [ the commencement of the latter of ] the muEaw~i*ataAni [or last two chapters ], (TA,) and ending with the faAtiHap [or first chapter ]; contrary to the prescribed mode: (TA:) or beginning from the end of the chapter, and reading it, or reciting it, to its beginning, invertedly; (K;) a mode which A 'Obeyd thinks impossible; and therefore he holds the former explanation to be the right: (TA:) each of these practices is disapproved, excepting the former in teaching children, [in which case it is generally adopted in the present day,] (K,) and [in teaching] the foreigner the [portion of the Kur-án called the] mufaS~al ; an indulgence being granted to these two only because the long chapters are difficult to them: but if any one knows the Kur-án by heart, and intentionally recite it from the last part thereof to the first, this is forbidden: and if we disapprove this, still more is the reciting from the end of the chapter to the beginning disapproved, if the doing this be possible. (TA.) ― -b5- manokuwsN also signifies (tropical:) Suffering a relapse into disease, after convalescence; or after recovery, but not complete, of health and strength. (K.) ― -b6- manokuwsapN applied to a bow: see nikosN .

definition: , (A, Mgh, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (A, Mgh, K,) aor. yaziru , inf. n. wizorN , with kesr, (K,) He bore, or carried, a heavy load, or burden. (A, Mgh, K.) It is said in the Kur, [vi. 164, &c.,] walaA taziru waAzirapN wizora A^uxoraY Nor shall any [soul] bearing [a heavy burden] bear the [ heavy ] burden of another soul; (S;) i. e., its burden of sin: (Mgh, Msb:) meaning, that no one shall be punished for the sin of another; nor shall any sinning soul bear the heavy burden of another soul; every one shall be requited for his [own] deeds: (TA:) or nor shall any sinning [soul] sin by the sin of another. (Akh, S, TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (Akh, S,) wazara , (Akh, S, A, Msb, K,) aor. yaziru ; and wazira , aor. yawozaru ; (Akh, S, A, Msb, K;) and wuzira (the same and A,) aor. yuwzaru ; (Akh, S, K;) inf. n. wizorN and wazorN and zirapN , (K,) or wizorapN , accord. to Zj, as I have seen it [says IM] pointed and well written; (L;) (tropical:) He sinned: (Akh, S, A, K:) or he bore [ a burden of ] sin- (Msb.) See also 8. ― -b3- wuzira also signifies (tropical:) He was charged with, or accused of, a sin. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- wazara liloA^amiyri , (A,) and lilos~uloTaAni , (Msb, [this I believe to be the right reading; but in the only copy of the Msb, that I have, I find it written AlslTAn ;]) aor. yaziru ; (A, Msb;) inf. n. wazaArapN ; (A;) and liloA^amiyri ↓ twz~r , (S.) or lalomaliki ; (K;) and ↓ waAzrhu ; (S, K;) (tropical:) He was, or became, waziyr [or vicegerent ] (S, A, Msb, K) to the governor, (S, A,) or sultán, (Msb,) or king. (K.)

definition: A heavy load or burden, (A, Mgh, K,) a bundle, (S,) or great bundle, (K,) that is carried on the back: (S, K:) a weight;
sourceDefinition: A heavy load or burden, (A, Mgh, K,) a bundle, (S,) or great bundle, (K,) that is carried on the back: (S, K:) a weight; syn. vql : (S, [in which the syn. is written viqol : so in two copies; and so app. accord. to A 'Obeyd, who makes its pl. A^avoqaAl :] and Msb [in which, in my copy, the syn. is written without syll. signs:] and K [in which it is written viqal :]) pl. A^awozaArN . (Msb, K.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A weapon; an instrument of war: or weapons; arms: syn. silaAHN : (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) because heavy upon the wearer: (Mgh, Msb:) or A^awozaArN signifies the burdens and instruments of war, &c.; and the sing. is wizorN ; (A 'Obeyd, TA;) or it has no sing., accord. to some. (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely El-Aashà, (Mgh, TA.) waA^aEodadotu liloHarobi A^awozaArahaA rimaAHFA TiwaAlFA waxayolFA *ukuwraA [ And I prepared for the war its weapons and other apparatus; long lances and male horses ]. (S, Mgh, TA.) And it is said in the Kur, [xlvii. 5,] Hay~aY taDaEa A@loHarobu A^awozaArahaA , meaning, (tropical:) Until the war terminates: (Mgh, Msb:) because then the people thereof lay down their arms: (Mgh:) properly, until the people of the war lay down their burdens: (Msb:) their weapons and burdens: or, as some say, their sins. (Bd.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A sin: (S, Bd, ubi supra, and Msb, K:) and [especially] polytheism: (Fr, Bd, TA:) pl. as above. (Bd, Msb, &c.) This is the sense in which it is most frequently used in the traditions. (IAth.)

(TA.)

definition: A place that is even and soft, (S, K,) such as is termed dahosN , (K,) or kaviyru Ald~ahasi , (S,) in which the feet sink, (S, K,) and upon which it is troublesome to walk: (S:) or sand in which the feet of camels, &c.
sourceDefinition: A place that is even and soft, (S, K,) such as is termed dahosN , (K,) or kaviyru Ald~ahasi , (S,) in which the feet sink, (S, K,) and upon which it is troublesome to walk: (S:) or sand in which the feet of camels, &c., sink: (ISd:) and [in like manner] ↓ waEovaA'u signifies that in which the hoofs of horses and the like, and the feet of camels, sink, consisting of fine sand, and what is termed dahaAs , of small pebbles: (Az, from Khálid Ibn-Kulthoom:) or waEovN signifies whatever is soft and even: (As:) or sand that is not much in quantity: or a soft place: pl. wuEovN and wuEuwvN : and [in like manner] ↓ naqFA muwaE~avN an extended and gibbous tract of sand, which is soft, and in which the feet sink. (TA.) ― -b2- Also waEovN and ↓ waEivN and ↓ muwaE~avN A difficult road. (K.) ― -b3- huwa yamo$iY fiY AlwaEovi , and fiY AlwuEuwvi , He walks along a tract such as is called dahaAs , ( and along tracts of that kind, ) in which walking is laborious. (TA.) ― -b4- waEovN (tropical:) A bone broken, (S, K,) and chipped, or notched. (S.) ― -b5- waEovN Leanness: (K:) soft leanness. (TA.) ― -b6- waEovN A corrupt and confused state of an affair: pl. wuEuwvN . (L.) ― -b7- waEovN (tropical:) Anything inconvenient, troublesome, difficult, or toilsome. (Msb.) ― -b8- A_imoraA^apN waEovapN A woman who is fat, (K,) or fleshy; (S;) as though the fingers would sink into her, by reason of her softness and fleshiness. (TA.) AmrAp waEovahu AlA^arodaAfi (tropical:) A woman having soft buttocks. (ISd.) Ru-beh says, tumiyluhaA A^aEojaAzuhaA AlA^awaAEivu [ Her soft buttocks make her to bend ]. Here AwAEv may be pl. of waEovN , contr. to analogy; or it may be pl. of A^awoEuvN , which may be pl. of waEovN . (ISd.) ↓ waEovaA'u also signifies the same as waEovN . (ISd.) ― -b9- [For the prov.] EalaY maA xuy~ilato waEovu AlqaSiymi (TA,) [see 2, in art. xyl .]

definition: a word denoting compassion, or pity: (AZ, As, S, K:) wayolN denotes [an imprecation of] punishment;
sourceDefinition: a word denoting compassion, or pity: (AZ, As, S, K:) wayolN denotes [an imprecation of] punishment; (S;) or [of] removal from good, or from prosperity: (AZ, As:) or [of] destruction: (AZ:) and wayosN denotes the same as wyH ; (AZ;) or less than wyH : (As:) or wyH and wys denote compassion, or pity, and admiration of one's beauty; as when you say of a child, wayoHahu maA A^amolaHahu , and wayosahu mA AmlHh , [ Mercy on him! or the like: how beautiful is he! ] (Kh) or, accord. to most of the lexicologists, wyl is a word said to, or of, any one who falls into destruction or trial, or misfortune, and on whom one does not wish God's mercy: and wyH is said to, or of, any one who falls into trial or misfortune, and for whom one wishes God's mercy, and his escape therefrom: the former word being so used in the Kur-án, and the latter by the Prophet: (T:) or wyl is said to, or of, him who falls into destruction: and wyH is a word by which one chides him who is at the point of falling into destruction: (Sb:) or wyH and wyl are syn., (Yz, En-Nadr, S, Ibn-Et-Faraj,) and wys signifies the same: (Ibn-El-Faraj:) or wyH is a little softer, or more gentle, than wyl : (En-Nadr:) [if so, wayoHahu signifies woe to him: in the same, or in a milder, manner than wayolahu :] or the original of wyH is wayo ; sometimes H being added to this latter word, and sometimes l and sometimes b , and sometimes s ; (K;) so that it becomes wyH and wyl and wyb and wys . (TA.) [See wyl and wyb and wys and wy .] You say wayoHN lizayodK [ Mercy on Zeyd! or woe to Zeyd! ]; putting wyH in the nom. case as an inchoative; (S, K;) and in like manner, wayolN lizayodK : (S:) and also wayoHFA lizayodK ; putting wyH in the acc. case because of a verb understood; (S, K;) as though you said A^alozamahu A@ll~`hu wayoHFA [ May God make mercy, or woe, to attend him constantly! ]; and in like manner, wayolFA lizayodK : (S:) or [it is put in the acc. case as an absolute complement of a verb understood, i. e., as an inf. n., and] the meaning is A^ataraH~amuhu taraH~umFA . [ I say, May God have mercy on him! emphatically ]: (Z, in the Fáïk:) you also say wayoHaka , and wayoHa zayodK ; (S, K;) making wyH a prefixed n.; (S;) and putting it in the acc. case again because of a verb understood; (S, K;) and in like manner, wayolaka , and wayola zayodK : (S:) and also wayoHamaA zayodK in the same sense. (K.)

sourceDefinition: A certain bird (S, K) of prey, (S,) resembling the [ kind of hawk called ] baA$aq : (S, K:) it is of the birds called Suquwr , [pl. of SaqorN ,] as are also the baAziY and the $aAhiyn and the zur~aq and the baA$aq : (AHát in TA, in art. b$q :) accord. to Dmr, it is a small bird, short-tailed, the temperament of which is, in comparison with that of the bA$q , cold and moist; for it is more patient, or enduring, and heavier in motion: the people of Egypt and Syria, he adds, call it jalamN , on account of the lightness and swiftness of its wings: (TA:) pl. yaA^=y^iYu , and, in a verse, yaA^=y^iYo . definition: ― -b2- A^asolamotu wajohiY ll~`h I resigned, or resign, myself to God: i.
sourceDefinition: ― -b2- A^asolamotu wajohiY ll~`h I resigned, or resign, myself to God: i. e., I became, or become, * Muslim: wjh is here used for the whole because it is the most noble part: (Jel, ii. 106:) or *AtY my course. (TA.) ― -b3- mino kul~i wajohK In every respect; considered from every point of view. ― -b4- Alwajohu A^ano yakuwna ka*aA The [ proper or reasonable ] way is that it should be thus: or the valid and obvious [ way ]. (Msb.) See turoEapN . ― -b5- wajohN A course, a purpose, or an object, which one is pursuing; a direction in which one is going or looking, & c. as also ↓ jihapN . ― -b6- The way of a thing. (TA.) ― -b7- layosa likalAamika wajohN There is no truth, or correctness, in thy saying. (TA.) ― -b8- wajohN Brightness [of intellect]. (L, voce kad~N .) ― -b9- liwajohi A@ll~`hi (Kur, lxxvi. 9) For the sake of God; or to obtain the countenance or favour of God. (Kull, p. 378.) See fiY *aAti A@ll~`hi in art. *uw . ― -b10- lawokaAna ka*aA lakaAna wajohFA Were it so, it were reasonable. ― -b11- laA wajoha lahu , said of a phrase, &c., There is no reasonable way of accounting for it. ― -b12- laysa biAlwajohi same as layosa biwajiypK ? Not of respectable, or esteemed, or high, authority: (said of a word or phrase, &c.:) or it is not the proper way. ― -b13- AibotigaA'a wajohi All~`hi From a desire of God's recompense: (Kur, ii. 274; and Expos. of the Jeláleyn:) or countenance, meaning favour. There are several similar phrases in the Kur, where wjh is explained in the same sense of vawaAbN in the Expos. of the Jeláleyn. ― -b14- jabasahu Eano wajohihi [ He withheld him, or restrained him, from his course, purpose, or object ]. (S, art. Alt .) ― -b15- Sarafa Al$~aYo'a Eano wajohuhu He turned the thing away, or back, from its course, Eano sananihi . (TA.) ― -b16- xaraja wajohuhu (S, A, L, art. mrd ; and L voce AstElj ;) [for xaraja nabaAtu wajohihi , The hair of his face grew forth ]. ― -b17- wajohu Ald~ahori The beginning of time, (K,) and nahaArK of day. (TA.) ― -b18- rawaAhu EalaY wajohihi , (S, K, art. qS ,) and Had~ava bihi EalaY wajohihi : (Msb, art. qS :) see qaS~a , in two places. ― -b19- A^atayotu AlA^amora mino wajahihi , &c., and ↓ jihatihi : see maA^otFY . ― -b20- wajohN The drift of speech. (K, Kull, p. 378.) ― -b21- maDaYa EalaY wajohihi [ He went at random, heedlessly, headlong, or in a heedless, or headlong, course, or manner; and so *ahaba EalaY wajohihi ]: see rakiba raA^osahu in art. rkb . ― -b22- dahaba EalaY wajohihi Hayovu $aA='a [ He went away at random whither he would ]. (TA in art. swm .) ― -b23- bal~ato maTiy~atuhu EalaY wajohihaA and A^abal~ato : see 1 in art. bl . ― -b24- A^uTolubuwA AlHawaAy^ija A_inaY HisaAni Alwujuwhi Make ye petition, for the things that ye want, to persons of good rank or station. (El-Hasan El-Muäddib, in TA, art. nDr .) ― -b25- wajohN (assumed tropical:) Consideration and regard. See 3 in art. Asw . ― -b26- wajohN and ↓ jihapN The place towards which one goes: (Munjid of Kr:) or the place, region, quarter, part, or point, towards which a person, or thing, goes, tends, or is directed: so I have rendered ↓ jihapN : see SuqoEN , and masojuwHN : ↓ jihapN signifies any place towards which one looks or goes; as also ↓ wijohupN : (Har, p. 373:) the place, or point, of the tendency or direction or bearing of anything: whence ka*aA ↓ jihapa in the direction of such a thing: and ↓ lijihapK towards one quarter. ― -b27- Hence, wajohu AlT~ariyqi The point, or place, to which the way, or road, leads: see *anaAbapN . And in like manner, wajohu A^amorK and ↓ jihatuhu The end, or result, of an affair, to which it leads, or tends. ― -b28- ramawoA wajohFA waAHidFA [ They shot in one direction ]. (M voce ri$oqN .) ― -b29- wajohu AlD~uHaY The first, or beginning, of the DuHaY . (TA voce rawonaqN , q. v.) ― -b30- wajohN A chief of a people or party. (K.) ― -b31- A^atawoA mano wajohihimo : see faworN . ― -b32- wajohN i. q. TariyqapN [meaning The mode, or manner, of a thing]. (KL.) ― -b34- maA A^adoriY maA wajohuhu I know not what is its meaning. ― -b35- A^axa*a wajohahaA [app. He degraded her; took away her grade: and hence he took her maidenhead: see waj~ahoti sijaAfatahu ].

definition: The thing, or affair, [ fell, befell, ] happened;
sourceDefinition: The thing, or affair, [ fell, befell, ] happened; took place; came to pass; became [ executed, performed, or] realized; syn. HaSala . (TA.) ― -b2- waqaEa fiY He lighted, or came, upon a thing or place; and he became in a place. ― -b3- waqaEuwA fiY Als~unay~aAti AlbiyDi [ They lapsed into the years of scantiness of herbage ]. (K in art. snh , q. v.) ― -b4- waqaEa A_ilayohi It chanced, or happened, to come to him, or it: and, said of a thing borne by water, it drifted to it, namely, a place. ― -b5- waqaEa Ealayohi It fell, lay, or closed, upon it, or against it. ― -b6- waqaEa biAlA^amori He originated the thing, or event, and made it to befall. (TA.) ― -b7- waqaEa He fell into a snare, or the like: he became insnared. ― -b8- waqaEa fiY A^aroDK falaApK i. q. SaAra fiyhaA [ He was, or became, meaning he found himself, came to be, or chanced to be, in a desert, or waterless, land ]; (Msb:) and fiY rawoDapK [ in a meadow, or garden ]: (T, S, in art. Anq :) [or he lighted upon, &c.; from the lighting of a bird]. ― -b9- yaqaEu followed by EalaY , often signifies It (a garment, &c., or a portion thereof,) lies against or upon a certain part of the body, &c. ― -b10- waqaEa bihimo and bihimo ↓ A^awoqaEa He made much slaughter among them: (Msb:) or he fought them vehemently: (K:) or he fell upon them in fight: (PS:) both mean the same: (S:) he made an onslaught upon them: AwqE biAlEaduw~i he made an assault, or a sudden assault, upon the enemy. (MA.) ― -b11- waqaEa fiyhi , inf. n. waqiyEapN , He spoke evil of him, behind his back, or in his absence, or otherwise, saying of him what would grieve him if he heard it; (S;) slandered him. ― -b12- He reviled, vilified, or vituperated, him; charged him with a vice, fault, or the like; defamed him; or detracted from his reputation. (Msb.) ― -b13- waqaEa mawoqiEFA mino kifaAyatihi , [and mino HaAjatihi , (see K, art. fqr ,)] It supplied, or sufficed for, his need; syn. A^agonaY ganaA='F . (Msb.) waqaEa mawoqiEFA signifies It stood in stead, or in some stead: see faqiyrN , in the K; and see Bd, and Jel, ix. 60: and mawoqiEFA EaZiymFA , in great stead. ― -b14- lamo yaqaEo minohu mawoqiEFA [ It did not stand with him in any stead ]. (S, K, voce tasax~aTa , end of art. sxT .) [You say] waqaEa minohu AlA^amoru mawoqiEFA HasanFA A^awosay~iy^FA The thing stood with him [ in good stead, or (if the expression be allowable) in evil stead ]; syn. tabata ladayohi . (TA.) ― -b15- waqaEa mawoqiEFA mina AlHaAjapi [ It supplied, or sufficed for, what was needed ]. (Bd, ix. 60.) ― -b16- waqaEotu biqur~ika , and biquHaAHi qur~ika : see quHaAHN . ― -b17- yaqaEu EalaY ka*aA It (a word) applies to such a thing.

definition: , (MA, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (MA, TA,) inf. n. tawoqiyEN , (KL, TA,) [as commonly used in the present day,] He signed the writing [ for the purpose of giving effect to it, either beneath, or by endorsing it ]: (MA, KL:) [but as generally used in earlier, though post-classical, times,] he annexed to the writing, after it had been finished, for the Sultán or the administrator of affairs, to whom it had been submitted, something [ for the purpose of giving effect thereto ]; as, for instance, when a complaint is submitted to the Sultán or to the administrator, and one writes beneath the writing or on the back thereof, “ Let the affair, or case, of this person be looked into, and let his right, or due, be fully exacted for this person: ” or, accord. to Az, he wrote, upon the writing, a concise abstract, omitting redundances, of the objects of want [ petitioned for therein ]: from tawoqiyEu Ald~abari Zahora AlbaEiyri [“ the gall's, or sore's, marking the back of the camel ”]; as though the muwaq~iE upon the writing marked, upon the case respecting which the writing was written, that which confirmed it, and rendered its execution obligatory: (TA:) tawoqiyEN also signifies such a writing itself ( maA yuwaq~aEu fiY kitaAbKi ; S, K, TA;) and its pl. is tawoqiyEaAtN : (TA:) it is said to be an Islámic term; not old Arabic. (TA.) [Also He made an entry of a note or postil or the like, or entries of notes, &c., in the writing, or book: see an ex. voce DiEof . ― -b2- wq~E bihi He blamed him; reproved him angrily, or severely. (TA.) ― -b3- See 4.
